items.title: feat: CyberBrick remote to MicroDuck via UART (no USB hub) or USB
items.body:
## Summary
- Add a MicroPython receiver program for stock CyberBrick X11 (paired with X12 transmitter), forwarding all 10 channels and receiver timestamps over USB CDC.
- Add a TaishanPi Python serial-to-UDP bridge targeting the Pollen MicroDuck `DKPD` v1 / `netpadd` protocol; retain four independent analog joystick axes and K1 Start, with optional K2–K4 mappings.
- Add timestamp-based queue freshness checks, serial backlog discard, 200 ms RF silence neutralization, one-shot neutral shutdown, and 32-bit sequence/timestamp encoding.
- Include setup, calibration, physical safety notes, and CPU-only tests.

## Validation
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_cyberbrick_bridge.py' -v` — **8 passed** locally (no hardware).
- `python3 -m compileall -q scripts/cyberbrick` — passed locally.
- **Not yet tested on physical CyberBrick / TaishanPi / motors.**

## Compatibility / next step
- Only routes input into **Pollen** `robotd/netpadd` on UDP port 4210. It does **not** connect directly to URT-2 or drive Feetech HD-1910 servos.
- For user's TaishanPi + 15× HD-1910 XGO-Duck build, the actual motion runtime (which may not include netpadd) must expose an equivalent velocity/action input + watchdog before robot movement can be tested.
- Upstream MicroDuck policy/joint config is not interchangeable with the 15-servo XGO build. Do not run it on the floor before calibrating joint order, IMU, gait and safety.

## References
- https://github.com/CyberBrick-Official/CyberBrick_Controller_Core/blob/master/docs/cyberbrick_core/lib/rc_module.rst
- https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/docs/robot/udp-pad.md
## Update: USB-free UART bridge
- X11 receiver also streams `CB` frames over UART1 (A11 GPIO21 TX / GPIO20 RX) at 115200 baud, leaving the TaishanPi USB host free.
- For TaishanPi RK3566: X11 D1 signal TX -> **2.2 kΩ series** -> physical pin 10 UART3_RX, plus **10 kΩ from pin 10 to GND** (3.3 V -> ~2.70 V). X11 and HAT share GND; power X11 via its rated supply input, not a GPIO.
- Run `python3 scripts/cyberbrick/bridge.py --port /dev/ttyS3 --dry-run` after enabling/checking the UART3 pinmux. Check any conflict with the user's custom HAT.
- The new MicroPython UART transport and the physical UART wiring have **not yet been verified on hardware**.

items.title: MAKHEX request: permission scope to mirror Microduck CAD/PCB files for signed-in makers
items.body:
Hello kissqy — we are featuring and crediting Microduck on the independent maker site **MAKHEX** (https://makhex.com/projects/microduck-robot/) with links to your repository and guides. We already have permission from the MAKHEX owner to use the demo media, but **we are not assuming that permission covers CAD, PCB or firmware redistribution**. We reviewed the mixed-license notice and want to respect your rights and upstream contributors.

Could you confirm, **in writing**, whether you personally have rights to authorize any of the following for MAKHEX, and if so on what terms?

1. Host unmodified copies of the **FrankenDuck 36 STL files / 3MF print project** behind free MAKHEX maker-account login, with creator credits, original notices and links.
2. Host the **four EasyEDA Pro .epro2 HAT/IMU project files** (October 7 EH2.5 and October 15 AMP2.0 revisions) in the same member-only reference library, retaining your notices.
3. Separately: whether physical printed parts / assembled HAT/IMU boards derived from your own original contributions can be offered as optional paid components, without implying your endorsement. We will **not** sell or bundle derivatives until permitted by all relevant rights holders.

We recognize that some geometry, hardware and firmware originated with third parties and you cannot grant rights you do not hold; if permission is limited, a list of files/scopes permitted or other maintainers to contact would be very helpful. An explicit repo license/permission file or a written response on this issue will work for our documentation.

Until confirmed, MAKHEX links visitors to your original source downloads rather than republishing CAD binaries or selling their derivatives. Thank you for documenting the project.

items.title: Overhaul 5/9: Robot-agnostic observation contract
items.body:
**Goal:** an observation contract that fits Microduck today and other robots later: optional sensors, no legged/floor assumptions in the core.

Source: [big-picture review](https://github.com/arteeh/ito/blob/316a556/docs/big-picture.md), §2 "Architecture: the policy is underspecified", §5 critique table (calibration / named frames rows). Can run alongside #41; needed before #43.

### Work
- Replace the "first camera" motion and "Y = height over floor" + `standing/walking/turning/held/fallen` assumptions (`protocol/__init__.py:205`) with named-frame observations: per-frame camera timing/calibration/exposure, optional IMU, optional range (ToF zones with angular footprint and quality), optional motion prior with uncertainty.
- Robot-specific semantics (gait states etc.) move into the Microduck driver. The driver already tracks the v8 gait (adapter yaw rate, pan trim), so this is easier now.
- Keep it small: a clear contract and the Microduck + sim drivers using it, not a generic factor framework for hypothetical sensors.

### Done when
- Microduck (sim) runs end-to-end on the new contract with no regression against current main, re-measured when work starts (the #38 metrics from 07ca8a3 are stale).
- The core runs with camera-only input (motion prior and ToF disabled) and degrades gracefully instead of failing.
- Wire version bumped; contract documented.

items.title: MicroDuck Feetech Replica – Hardware, Firmware and Software Clarification Before Assembly
items.body:
Hello,

My name is Gianluca, and I am building your MicroDuck Replica using the Feetech 3D-printing project (52 printed parts). I have already started printing the components.

Thank you for sharing your work and documenting your progress. I would like to reproduce your Feetech version as faithfully as possible.

Before purchasing the electronics and assembling the robot, I would appreciate your help confirming the current hardware and software configuration. I have read your repository and recent updates, but I want to make sure I follow the latest tested setup rather than an earlier design or a component that is still under development.

I hope to clarify the remaining questions in one message and avoid disturbing you repeatedly during the build.

1. Recommended hardware and electronics

Could you please confirm the exact hardware configuration you currently recommend for a new Feetech build?

Are 15 Feetech HD-1910-C001 servos still the correct model and quantity?

Is the Radxa Zero 3W still the recommended main computer? Is the 8 GB RAM / 64 GB eMMC variant compatible with your design and software?

Which controller boards, adapters and custom PCBs are required for the completed robot?

Which components have already been tested on your assembled Feetech robot, and which are still experimental or planned?

Is there an updated bill of materials (BOM) that reflects your current build?

2. Servo interface, connections and calibration

I understand that you successfully controlled all 15 Feetech servos using a Feetech URT-2 USB adapter.

Is the URT-2 also the recommended interface between the Radxa and the servo bus in the completed robot, or is it mainly used for testing and calibration?

How should the 15 servos be physically connected and powered?

Is a specific bus distribution board, adapter or wiring arrangement required?

Which wiring diagram and power-connection instructions should I follow?

Where can I find the latest servo ID mapping, joint directions, zero positions, standing positions and safe movement limits?

3. IMU and orientation feedback

I have read about the imu_to_dxl board and the recent firmware contribution by @Abo1ish. I understand that an initial firmware implementation has been tested and that IMU orientation can be displayed in the servo-web diagnostic interface through J-Link.

I also understand that the Feetech 15-byte bus protocol has not yet been implemented in that firmware.

Could you please clarify:

Which IMU hardware is installed in your current Feetech robot?

Which IMU solution do you recommend for a new Feetech build?

Is the imu_to_dxl board ready to build and use, or should I wait for a newer hardware or firmware revision?

Is the alternative BNO085 IMU connected directly to the Radxa still a recommended option?

Has either solution already been integrated and tested with the Feetech movement-control software, rather than only with the diagnostic interface?

Where can I find the current wiring instructions, firmware, software configuration and calibration procedure for the recommended IMU?

My aim is to install an IMU that the movement-control software can actually use.

4. Current movement software and capabilities

I have seen your video showing the Feetech robot standing up and sitting down. I have also read about your FeetechIo implementation and the current status of walking-policy training.

Could you please confirm which of the following capabilities have already been physically tested on your Feetech version?

Standing up and sitting down

Maintaining balance using IMU feedback

Walking forward

Turning while walking

Recovering after a disturbance or fall

Is the feetech branch of your MicroDuck fork currently ready to run on an assembled Radxa-based robot, or should a new builder initially use only the servo-web diagnostic console?

Does the Feetech version require a separately trained walking policy? If so, are the required model files already available, or is this work still in progress?

5. Operating system and first startup

I noticed your recent Radxa Zero 3W Armbian release and the documentation about boot issues on certain board revisions.

Which operating-system image and installation procedure do you currently recommend?

Are there any Radxa board revisions that require special attention?

Which instructions should I follow for initial servo configuration and calibration?

Is there a recommended first-start and testing procedure before enabling full-body movements?

6. Power supply and battery

For the initial build, I would like to follow the power configuration used in your working Feetech robot.

Could you please confirm:

The battery model, voltage, capacity and connector you currently use

The recommended power connection for the 15 Feetech servos

How the Radxa receives its regulated 5 V supply

Any required voltage regulators, distribution boards, switches or protection components

The correct power-on and power-off sequence

If available, could you please point me to your latest corrected wiring diagram?

7. Camera, distance sensor and audio

Could you please confirm the exact camera, distance sensor, microphone, speaker and audio interface or amplifier recommended for the current Feetech build?

I noticed that your recent documentation recommends the VL53L5CX instead of the VL53L8CX because of the mounting-hole dimensions of face_part. Is the VL53L5CX the correct choice for the Feetech printed parts?

Is the beak servo already independently controllable through the available software? If so, where can I find the corresponding command or documentation?

8. Current documentation and remaining work

Your project is progressing quickly, and I want to make sure I am using the latest instructions.

Could you please point me to the current recommended BOM, wiring diagram, firmware, software branch and assembly instructions for the Feetech version?

It would also be helpful to know which components or software features are still under development and should not yet be considered ready for a new build.

If these questions are already answered in your latest documentation, links to the relevant files would be more than sufficient.

Thank you very much for your time and for sharing your project. I appreciate any guidance you can provide to help me assemble and configure the Feetech MicroDuck correctly.

Best regards, Gianluca

items.title: Research: robust head-camera tracking
items.body:
Research task, handed to a Claude Code cloud session on Oct 11. Its result is PR #36. The original prompt follows, as sent.

```text
Branch fix/tracking-research-cloud. Report: docs/research/tracking.md. Repo arteeh/ito, start from main (cabaa4d). Read AGENTS.md and VISION.md first and follow them. This is a RESEARCH task: the deliverable is one markdown report committed on your branch and a PR against main (never merge; the owner and coordinator review). You have no GPU and the owner's PC is not reachable: base conclusions on reading the Ito code, papers, repos and licences (cite URLs), and if your sandbox allows, small CPU-only checks; say clearly what you could not verify. Be concrete and opinionated; rank options; no fluff. Context: Ito is a VR-first teleoperation app (pilot in a headset, robot = Pollen Microduck: small biped, head camera IMX219, VL53L5CX 8x8 ToF, IMU). The pilot sees a 3D reconstruction of the robot surroundings rendered at 90 Hz stereo, updated asynchronously as new camera frames arrive (the pilot's newest view matters most; a raw flat live camera feed is bad in VR). Today: MASt3R-SLAM (CUDA, RTX 4070 Ti 12 GB shared with the Ito app) gives poses + dense pointmaps, which become isotropic fixed-size Gaussians that are never optimised, rendered by Ito's own OpenGL 3DGS renderer (ito/render/scene.py, renderer.py, shaders/, sorted on GPU, loads standard 3DGS PLY). Results in the MuJoCo Microduck sim are poor: blurry, skipped frames (MASt3R tracker match fraction), tracking loss/map restarts, doubled walls. A truth benchmark (fix/truth-bench, in progress elsewhere) will score pilot-view PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, geometry ghosts and an oracle ladder (true vs estimated poses/depth). Agreed plan: benchmark, offline real Gaussian splatting from recordings, choose tracking, then online. Relevant code: ito/reconstruction/{slam.py,rgbd.py,ring.py,mast3r_runtime.py}, ito/render/*, drivers/microduck/*, e2e/slam_replay.py, e2e/splat_quality.py; issues #32 #33 #34 on github.com/arteeh/ito.
Step 3 of the plan is choosing the tracking. Research and recommend how Ito should track the robot head camera robustly in real time, with the codebase as context:
1. Review what exists: ito/reconstruction/slam.py (MASt3R-SLAM wrapper, restarts, heading checks, recall keyframes), the IMU-gating attempt on branch origin/fix/imu-slam (e957e4a, issue #33) and why it failed on the owner's PC (heading p95 improved 5.2->1.5 deg but map restarts 20->27, PSNR 22.75->19.02, path error 0.27->0.60 m), PR #15 (DROID-SLAM docs), and the Microduck driver: which signals are available (IMU model/rate, head joint encoders, walking policy body odometry, ToF), their timestamps and clock sync.
2. Options: MASt3R-Fusion (arXiv 2509.20757, github.com/GREAT-WHU/MASt3R-Fusion), VIO (OpenVINS, Basalt, ORB-SLAM3 VI, Kimera), DROID-SLAM/DPVO/DPV-SLAM, VGGT-SLAM, feed-forward GS-SLAM, and a kinematic prior (robot head pose from joint encoders + IMU + leg odometry) fused with visual relocalisation. Compare accuracy, robustness to fast head turns, motion blur and textureless walls, latency, GPU/CPU cost alongside reconstruction on a 4070 Ti, Windows support, licence.
3. Recommendation with a concrete integration design (interfaces in ito/reconstruction, what runs on the robot vs the pilot PC, time sync) and a test plan using the truth benchmark's oracle ladder (true vs estimated poses).
Open a PR titled "Research: robust head-camera tracking".
```

items.title: duck-sim: a default that walks, keyboard teleop, and a race to run
items.body:
From a first session driving a simulated duck on a Mac, where neither of the ways a robot is normally driven by hand is available: padd wants a real gamepad, and the console needs a camera.

**A default that walks.** `drive` defaulted to vx 0.15, which sits in the walking policy's dead band (measured: 0.15 moves it 6 mm in 4 s; 0.25 moves 0.32 m; 0.3 moves 0.47 m) — the command looked like a duck that would not walk and a simulator that was broken. Default is now 0.3. The Mac camera guard is gone too: mediad's GStreamer pipeline streams there now, so the guard would steal a working camera.

**Keyboard teleop, and a guard for a missing body.** New `keys` subcommand: raw-mode /dev/tty, the 10 Hz resend `drive` already does, same `robot.move` the console sends. Arrows drive (0.3 / 1.5 yaw — the measured floors), space stops, u stands a fallen duck up, r/k/l run the skills, q quits and restores the terminal. `u`/`r`/`k`/`l` send `robot.enable`/`robot.do` as requests so a refusal is printed. New `require_body` guard on `drive` and `keys`: closing the MuJoCo window stops the simulator while the daemons carry on against a dead port, so every drive command would be accepted and do nothing.

**A race to run.** New `scripts/duck-race` scoreboard: clock starts past 0.20 m, nine checkpoints, +3 s a fall, −5 s for the roll wall, best in `~/.cache/duck-sim/race-best.json`. Reads only the body's trunk/imu report, never talks to `robotd`. Course is `scene_challenge` in microduck_rl (`DUCK_SIM_SCENE=challenge`); the clock is wall-clock, so below-real-time sim counts against the run.

Docs in `docs/robot/simulation.md` cover all three. Depends on the challenge/playground scenes, currently only on my microduck_rl fork — opening that PR separately. Verified: bash -n, shellcheck clean, embedded Python parses. Session-tested live against a MuJoCo body.

items.title: Microduck Build 12: qualify supplier variants and Doroppu/Squarespace checkout
items.body:
Linked implementation: #59 (Microduck Build 12). The customer gallery and BOM research records are ready, but **the drop-ship kit is not orderable or source-qualified**.

### Acceptance criteria — exact source parts first
- [ ] Find supplier listing + exact selectable variation for 15 × **Feetech HD-1910-C001** serial bus servos; do **not** substitute STS3215, PWM servos or adjacent HD1910 models.
- [ ] Match **Radxa ZERO 3W 2GB / no eMMC / header-equipped** and boot storage, not an arbitrary ZERO or ESP32.
- [ ] Match **IMX219 160° camera**, specific CSI cable/connector, **VL53L5CX V2 8×8** ToF breakout, proper connectorized speaker and safe NP-F550 power/charger pair.
- [ ] Decide October 15 AMP2.0 vs October 7 EH2.5 HAT/IMU. Source or fabricate **only a compatible connector-and-PCB-revision pair**, with proper component rights and separately approved manufacturing review.
- [ ] Match 6700 (10×15×3 mm) and ET2216 (16×22×4 mm) installed quantities; include M2/M2.6 fastener lengths and 22 AWG/AMP2.0 harnesses. Separate the optional roller 623ZZ configuration.
- [ ] Check 3MF/STL print scale, TPU plate5, raw mesh repairs, 2 alternative battery holders and physical clearances before promising a printed kit.

### Sourcing and checkout gate
- [ ] Import actual supplier-owned product listings using Doroppu's intended Squarespace integration, not customer-facing supplier links.
- [ ] Reconcile source image variants and supplier option IDs to MAKHEX product slugs used by Build 12. Never show invented prices, availability, U.S. shipping or model photos.
- [ ] Qualify exact supplier stock and buyer-checkout shipping to ZIP **11021**, safe battery shipment, lead times, returns, refund route, duties and total landed cost.
- [ ] Apply MAKHEX owner-defined **2.5× supplier-price** policy with **free shipping** only once landed cost is confirmed.
- [ ] Establish independent storefront cart, payment, supplier placement, tracking and refund test; maintain checkout HOLD until an authorized real end-to-end test passes.
- [ ] Record dated evidence per SKU, including vendor selection and source-matched variant; only then publish orderable MAKHEX listing, update project cart and remove research-only flag.

### Current evidence
- 14 research parts have first-party MAKHEX product pages and 14-line baseline BOM; optional 623ZZ separately in shop.
- Native 3D archive and four board projects reviewed in `docs/microduck-cad-review-20261025.md`.
- Site's `sourcing.json` deliberately exposes no supplier cost, options, direct supplier links or inventory clearance.

items.title: Overhaul 7/9: Spend on the remaining bottleneck: initializer or ToF
items.body:
**Goal:** spend the next effort on whatever #40/#43 showed is the remaining bottleneck, using what the Microduck beta already has (mono GC2093 camera, ToF, LSM6DSV16X head IMU). No stereo camera or new hardware.

Source: [big-picture review](https://github.com/arteeh/ito/blob/316a556/docs/big-picture.md), §4 proposals 2 and 3, §6 step 6. Depends on #43.

Related: #47 (depth-mesh prototype), #48 (view-cache prototype), feed-forward reconstruction (CUT3R, StreamVGGT).

### Work (pick by evidence, not both by default)
- **If initialization/convergence dominates:** feed-forward Gaussian initializer trial (DepthSplat-small first, MVSplat as challenger) on fixed stretches of a session script (slow motion, turns, revisits), past/current views only, then bounded optimization. One model, sharing outputs; no stacking MASt3R + VGGT + DPVO + DepthSplat.
- **If metric geometry dominates:** integrate Microduck's ToF as optional metric evidence in the map and estimator, using its real angular footprint and quality (no upsampling the zones into invented edges).
- The initializer follows the Precision setting (Full/Half); when it runs out of GPU memory it drops the frame and shows the "reconstruction is degraded" warning, never a silent switch to Full.
- The beta sim already simulates the ToF (tofd) and head IMU (robotd), as on main; `--no-tof`/`--no-head-imu` turn them off. #42 (`feat/obs-42`) wired them as observations without a visible gain yet.
- Also check whether MASt3R (CC BY-NC-SA) is still needed in the product path once these exist.

### Done when
- Initializer: session recordings plainly sharper than the point-seeded optimizer and sharp sooner, no worse coverage or stereo, no new stalls; holds under pure turns and its own poses.
- ToF: visible improvement in the recordings (pot/ball occlusion, floor seams, shelf edges) with no render/freshness regression; Ito still runs with ToF absent.
- Improvement holds at near-eye offsets, on turns and away from the floor, with no plausible-but-wrong surfaces. If neither passes, keep the baseline.

### How to test (see AGENTS.md)
No automated tests and no numeric gates (no dB/PSNR/LPIPS/coverage thresholds). On ceres: build the branch with `release.ps1 -Branch <branch>` and a fresh main build, record each with `uv run tools/session.py <build> <name>` against the virtual Microduck (beta board; `tools/scripts/room-tour.json`, or a longer script added to `tools/scripts/`), same Settings (Precision, Input %, Max splats) for both, and note those Settings with the result. Then look at matching frames of both runs' `screen.mp4`/`camera.mp4` with `uv run tools/frame.py VIDEO FRAME -n N` (frame numbers per step in `steps.txt`). Judge by eye; a trade-off is not an improvement. Delete recordings once judged (50 GB per job at most).

items.title: robotd: play emotions as skills (robot.do sad)
items.body:
An emotion (a head, body and beak animation with its sound, like the ones in [microduck_emotions](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_emotions)) becomes a skill. Put `sad.json` and `sad.wav` in `/var/lib/robot/emotions/`, restart robotd, and:

```
robotctl robot do sad
sudo robotctl pad bind y sad
```

No new call and no padd change: `robot.do` already reaches every client (pad, robotctl, console), and `pad bind` already puts any skill on a button.

## What

- **robotd**, new `emotion.rs`: reads every `<name>.json` in `[emotions] dir` at startup, with the `<name>.wav` beside it. The JSON is the microduck_emotions keyframe format (`t`, `neck`, `head_pitch`, `head_yaw`, `head_roll`, `body_pitch`, `body_z`, `mouth`, `skill`; other fields ignored, missing ones 0). While one plays, the loop puts its frame in place of the clients' head, body pose and mouth, with a zero twist, for that tick only. It reaches the motors through the same policy and safety as the sticks (the pad's body + head mode, scripted), and the robot is back on the clients' values when it ends. It starts only on a robot the policy is driving with no move in flight; a fall, limp-fall, Start or a rest ends it, and cuts its sound. A keyframe with `"skill": "sit"` sits the robot down (devastated).
- `robot.do` looks emotions up after the policy skills. Their names are listed where skills are: the refusal, `pad bindings`, and the subscribe answer `robotctl pad bind` checks a name against.
- `sound.rs`: `play_file`, the bank player for one wav, and `stop` for a one-shot cut short.
- **robotd-params**: `[emotions] dir`, default `/var/lib/robot/emotions` (registry entry; `robotctl configure` offers a robotd restart).
- **scripts/duck-sim**: `[emotions] dir = ~/.cache/duck-sim/emotions`.
- **docs**: an "Emotions" section in the cheat sheet; one row in robotd-design §4.5.

No protocol change, so no `API_VERSION` bump.

## Not in this PR

- Play dead: its dead pose needs per-servo torque off and scripted joint targets, which the runtime does not have. The robot set in microduck_emotions leaves it out.
- Several sounds per emotion with a random pick, and more than six emotions on the pad at once.

## Tested

- **On a physical Microduck** (Rémi's new duck, Pro Controller, this branch's CI build `0.16.1-dev.1301.9bcdc89`): the 13 emotions played from the command line, and `yes` / `no` from the pad on Y and X. A press while an emotion played was ignored.
- **In the simulator** (`scripts/duck-sim`, macOS, headless): the 13 emotions one after the other with `robotctl robot do <name>`. The duck stayed upright throughout (worst tilt 8°), devastated sat down and `robot do sit_toggle` stood it up, `robotctl pad bind y sad` was accepted and a typo refused with the list. Repeated from fresh clones of the public repos.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude nfc` (1593 pass; `nfc` does not build on macOS, on main either), `cargo clippy` adds no warning, `cargo fmt`.
- New tests: interpolation and end, unknown fields ignored and missing ones zero, bad files refused, the sit asked once, the directory loader, `robot.do` queues an emotion and the subscribe answer lists it.

## How to test

**1. The emotion files.** From a clone of [microduck_emotions](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_emotions), this script writes one `<name>.json` and `<name>.wav` per emotion into the folder you name, cut to what the real duck plays. A `robot/emotions/` folder with the same files is coming to that repo.

<details><summary>The script</summary>

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_emotions
python3 - emotions <<'EOF'
import json, pathlib, shutil, sys
src = pathlib.Path("microduck_emotions")
out = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser()
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for e in json.loads((src / "emotions.json").read_text())["emotions"]:
    if e["name"] == "play_dead":
        continue  # its dead pose needs a joint-level call the runtime does not have yet
    start, end = e["sound_at_s"], e["sound_at_s"] + e["duration_s"]
    keys = [dict(k, t=round(k["t"] - start, 3))
            for k in json.loads((src / e["keyframes"]).read_text())["keyframes"]
            if start - 1e-6 <= k["t"] <= end + 1e-6]
    if e["name"] == "curious":  # the real duck keeps only the two tilts
        for k in keys:
            k["neck"] = k["head_pitch"] = 0.0
    (out / f"{e['name']}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"keyframes": keys}))
    shutil.copy(src / e["sounds"][0], out / f"{e['name']}.wav")
EOF
```

</details>

That gives 13 emotions: `angry`, `curious`, `defiant`, `devastated`, `excited`, `impatient`, `laugh`, `mmh`, `mock`, `no`, `sad`, `yes`, `yes_fast`.

**2a. On a robot** (a dev board; this installs the branch's CI build):

```bash
scp -r emotions <you>@<duck>:/tmp/
# on the duck
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/robot/emotions && sudo cp /tmp/emotions/* /var/lib/robot/emotions/
sudo robotctl update apply --ref play-emotions daemon     # restarts robotd, which loads them
journalctl -u robotd -b | grep "emotions loaded"          # the names it found
```

Press Start twice (stand up, then the policy drives), then play one:

```bash
robotctl robot do yes
```

On the pad, Y plays yes and X plays no:

```bash
sudo robotctl pad bind y yes
sudo robotctl pad bind x no
```

They are live within a second (`[pad]` in `/etc/robot/robotd.toml`), and `sudo robotctl pad reset` undoes them. On the current mapping X and Y are the only free buttons. padd binds buttons by position, so on a Switch Pro Controller `y` is the top button, which is labelled X there.

Two things unrelated to this PR came up on an older duck: an expired GitHub token on the robot (`--ref` answers HTTP 401; sideloading the release with `--from` works), and main's `fast_sync_read = true` default timing out on its servo firmware (`fast_sync_read = false` under `[bus]` fixed it).

**2b. In the simulator**, from this branch, with the same script writing to the simulator's folder (`python3 - ~/.cache/duck-sim/emotions <<'EOF'` …):

```bash
scripts/duck-sim
scripts/duck-sim ctl robot do yes
```

items.title: Overhaul 4/9: Independent state estimator with a pixel-level error budget
items.body:
**Goal:** a fast, independent state estimator whose error budget is good enough for a sharp stereo map: pixel-level consistency, not centimeter "usable".

Source: [big-picture review](https://github.com/arteeh/ito/blob/316a556/docs/big-picture.md), §2 "Estimation", §3 "Estimation and surface geometry worth borrowing", §4 proposal 1 "Estimator", §6 step 4. Depends on #38, #39, #40.

Related: #50 (robot-first tracking research, PR #36), robot-first fusion on main (97deed6), #49 (DROID-SLAM, PR #15; close to the DPVO challenger).

### Work
- The sim has no head IMU: `--head-imu` fails without tofd. IMU work needs either a simulated head IMU in the sim body plus a sim mode for robotd/tofd, or the real robot.
- Calibrate timing and extrinsics: camera capture delay/jitter (Microduck stamps *receipt*, `camera.py:85`), head-camera vs IMU vs joints, rolling-shutter where known. If true exposure time can't be obtained, measure and model delay/jitter explicitly.
- Split the immediately propagated pose (robot motion prior) from delayed visual corrections and from surface updates; publish poses without waiting on mapping.
- Compare as bounded challengers against current fusion (`fix/pixel-poses`, now on main): a sensor-aided feature/VIO baseline (OpenVINS/Basalt) where raw IMU exists, and DPVO. Start without map alignment. Use sensors (IMU, odometry, ToF) wherever they help, but the estimator must still work with camera + generic motion prior alone.
- Replace `floor_scale` (histogram of downward points assumed to be floor) with metric scale from robot motion/IMU/ToF evidence; vision-only fallback stays possible.
- Record on the current sim (velstand v8 walking policies, real 62° lens); recordings from before #56 move differently. Compare against current main at the same Settings (Precision, Input %, Max splats), and record those values with every motion sheet and A/B.

### Done when
- Static shelf/door edges stop sliding or doubling during turns; no scale breathing when the floor leaves view.
- On both sequences: causal p95 rotation error halved vs current main, re-measured when work starts (the 07ca8a3 baseline predates the GPU/VRAM budget, the padding fix, #54 and #56), no worse p95 translation, no added pose-publication delay, no lower pose rate.
- Supported cross-view reprojection ≤2 px p95 (or uncertain measurements explicitly excluded while keeping common-region coverage).
- Holds on an independent motion sequence.

items.title: Prototype: depth-mesh world (robot pose + Depth Anything RGB-D patches, newest wins)
items.body:
Separate prototype, outside the overhaul sequence (#38-#46). Question: how far does a plain **robot pose + monocular depth model → textured mesh** world get us, with no SLAM map and no Gaussian training?

## Idea
For each keyframe from the Microduck head camera:
1. Run a Depth Anything style model on the RGB frame to get a depth map.
2. Turn the depth into a coarse grid mesh (~160x90), cull triangles across depth jumps (no rubber sheets between foreground and background).
3. Texture it with the full-resolution camera image.
4. Place it in the world using the robot's pose (skeleton/kinematics + IMU), not visual tracking.
5. **Newest wins**: a newer patch replaces older ones where they overlap (free-space culling: older surfaces that the new view sees *through* are removed). Keep a cap on how many patches live at once.

## Variants to compare
- Depth model: Depth Anything V2 (Small and larger), Video Depth Anything (less flicker between frames), a metric-depth model (Metric DA / Depth Pro / UniDepth), Prompt Depth Anything fed with the 8x8 ToF (when a ToF is present; must stay optional).
- Pose: sim ground-truth pose (oracle) vs robot pose + IMU as Ito would see it.
- Licences: non-commercial models are allowed for this prototype (Ito is planned as free software); note each model's licence in the results.

## Known risks to measure
- Scale/shift flicker of relative depth between frames → walls breathing or doubling.
- Pose error at patch seams (~1.5° p95 ≈ 8 cm at 3 m).
- Stretched or missing surfaces when viewed from far off the capture angle.
- Lighting baked into textures.

## Rules
- Own branch (`proto/depth-mesh`) and module; do not change the main pipeline. Sim first, then recorded Microduck footage.
- Ito core must not require any extra sensor.
- Use the #38 measurement/eye-check kit where it exists (sim ground truth vs prototype, same frames).

## Done when
- Side-by-side eye-check sheets (sim truth | main | depth-mesh) for sweep180 and tour, plus PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS against held-out views, oracle and real pose.
- Short write-up: does it look better than main to the owner? where it breaks? is it worth using as the best-effort "always a room, never black" layer under #43/#45?

items.title: Research: robust head-camera tracking
items.body:
Closes #50

Research only: adds `docs/research/tracking.md`. No product code changes. This is step 3 of the plan (choose tracking). Please don't merge without review by the owner and the coordinator.

## Summary
- **Recommendation: robot-first tracking.** The driver streams the camera pose from head FK, the trunk/head IMU and leg odometry, at 50 Hz and timestamped at the source. A small sliding-window pose graph on the pilot PC (CPU, scipy, already pinned) fuses it with visual relative poses. The world frame is the robot's odometry frame, so map restarts stop existing. The first front end is the current MASt3R tracker, with the robot prior added inside its Gauss-Newton solve. A licence-clean DPVO/DROID front end (PR #15) comes later, behind the same `Frontend` interface.
- **Why:** the robot's pose was already measured at p95 1.32° rotation and 1.77 cm/m drift (`e957e4a`). MASt3R-SLAM's heading p95 is 5.21° (issue #33). Pure rotation, blur and blank walls are exactly where monocular vision fails and encoders and gyros do well.
- **Why the IMU gate (#33) failed:** it overwrote MASt3R's rotation after a joint Sim3 solve, and rolled back or patched local solves. It also vetoed frames at a 6° gate, using a prior stamped on arrival at 20 Hz with a constant 90 ms offset. A CPU check in the appendix shows that prior is off by p95 1 to 4.5° (max 5 to 21°) during turns, from timing alone. The same motion from samples timestamped at the source gives p95 0.07 to 0.18°.
- **Cheapest win:** robotd already sends `t_ns` on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, which is the driver's `perf_counter` on the robot, and Ito ignores it. The Microduck also has a head IMU that Ito doesn't use (BMI088 on zero3, off by default). Only the camera has no source timestamp; Pollen's own `remote-webrtc.md` §11 wants that fixed.
- **Not recommended:**
  - MASt3R-Fusion as a dependency: no LICENSE file, CC BY-NC-SA weights, a Linux-only GTSAM fork, and it needs raw stamped IMU data. Borrow its design instead.
  - Classical VIO (OpenVINS, Basalt, ORB-SLAM3, Kimera).
  - VGGT-SLAM online. It suits the offline step instead.
  - Feed-forward GS-SLAM: no public code.
- The report also includes an integration design (protocol `Motion` message, `motion.py` / `fusion.py` / `tracking.py`, what runs where, eased corrections for comfort) and a test plan. The test plan is an oracle ladder (truth → robot prior → stamped prior → fused → today → the gate) with adoption gates on the truth benchmark.

Each claim is tagged as verified (Ito code, Pollen source at the pinned revision, cloned upstream repos, PyPI, the CPU check), as a paper/owner number, or as an estimate. Nothing ran on a GPU or on the robot; the report's last section lists what couldn't be verified.

Note: AGENTS.md says "no `docs/` tree". The file lives in `docs/research/` because the task asked for it there, same as PR #15.

items.title: docs: khảo sát thị trường robot servo + vì sao microduck "sống" hơn Open Duck Mini v2
items.body:
## Summary

Hai tài liệu tiếng Việt trong `docs/ideas/`, cùng chỉ mục trong `docs/README.md`.

**`market-analysis-servo-robots.md`** — khảo sát thị trường robot servo. Tách rõ `[REPO]`
(Open Duck Mini v2, microduck, MiniPlan-V6, có dẫn dòng cụ thể) khỏi `[NGOÀI REPO]`
(Robi, PLEN2, ROBOTIS MINI, AiNex, Zeroth Bot, Berkeley Humanoid Lite — tra nguồn ngoài,
không kiểm chứng được từ code). Kết luận: khoảng trống là lớp RL/hành vi trên nền servo rẻ.

**`microduck-vs-open-duck-mini-v2.md`** — vì sao chuyển động của microduck đọc ra như một
con vật trong khi ODM v2 đọc ra như một robot đi rất tốt, dù cả hai đều là MuJoCo → PPO →
ONNX. Bốn nguyên nhân, mỗi cái có bằng chứng mã nguồn:

- Hợp đồng quan sát chứa lệnh tư thế đầu: `obs[51..55] = neck_pitch, head_pitch, head_yaw,
  head_roll`, nên `robot.look(x,y,z)` → `HEAD_FK.look_at` chảy *vào* policy thay vì cộng
  lên trên nó. ODM v2 chỉ điều kiện hoá theo lệnh vận tốc và có cả cờ `--zero_head`.
- Thư viện 9 policy cùng hợp đồng `obs[1,61] → actions[1,14]` sau một scheduler ưu tiên
  (`roulade > kick > ground pick > sit/rise > stand > walk`), với `last_action` *raw* dùng
  chung nên đổi mạng không giật.
- IMU nằm trên bus Dynamixel, đọc trong **cùng** `sync_read` với 15 servo → trọng lực và vị
  trí khớp cùng một thời điểm.
- Hằng số thời gian ở mọi đường ranh: `head_lowpass 0.5` / `legs_lowpass 0.7` khớp training,
  `CHORALE_MOUTH_TAU_S 0.09`, `HOME_RAMP 2 s`, fall predictor mềm gain *trước* khi đáp,
  theremin lấy một biến `closeness` ra cả pitch/level/mouth.

Ghi rõ giới hạn: runtime thật của ODM v2 nằm ở repo `Open_Duck_Mini_Runtime` không có trong
phạm vi kiểm chứng, nên so sánh tầng runtime dựa trên `experiments/`; và phần sim/nhận dạng
động cơ (BAM) của ODM v2 mạnh hơn những gì repo này để lộ. Mọi suy luận của tôi được đánh
dấu `[SUY LUẬN]`, tách khỏi `[MD]` / `[ODM]`.

Docs-only; CI có `paths-ignore` cho Markdown.


Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/04e27dea873f4d378214e4ef324cd7b2

items.title: Research: DROID-SLAM as an alternative to MASt3R-SLAM
items.body:
Research task, handed to a Claude Code cloud session on Oct 9. Its result is PR #15. The original prompt follows, as sent.

```text
Branch research/droid-slam-cloud. Repo arteeh/ito, start from main (b77daee). Read AGENTS.md and VISION.md first and follow their commit identity/trailers rules. This is a RESEARCH task: do not change product code on main paths; you have no NVIDIA GPU. Push your branch and open a PR against main titled "Research: DROID-SLAM as alternative to MASt3R-SLAM"; never merge.

Context: Ito reconstructs a Gaussian-splat scene from one monocular RGB robot camera (Microduck, real 62 deg lens, 640x360 default, 720p/1080p option) on the pilot's Windows PC (RTX 4070 Ti, 12 GB, shared with the VR/desktop renderer at 90-120 fps). Current backend: MASt3R-SLAM in ito/reconstruction/slam.py, plus rgbd.py fusion. Problems seen on the Microduck sim: MASt3R fails to match featureless walls during turns (most map restarts come from unmatched frames), 50-160 map restarts per 100 s, doubled/tilted wall planes after realigns, tracking ~3.5-5 Hz. The driver sends body heading, head pan and per-frame camera pose (head FK + IMU) which can serve as priors.

Research princeton-vl/DROID-SLAM (and its successors/relatives worth comparing, e.g. DPVO/DPV-SLAM, GO-SLAM, MASt3R-SLAM itself, any 2025-2026 monocular dense SLAM with released code and a permissive license) and answer concretely:
1. Fit: monocular RGB with known intrinsics; can it take pose/IMU priors (robot heading) or be fused with them; behaviour on low-texture walls and pure rotation.
2. Cost: GPU memory and fps at 360p/720p on a ~12 GB card shared with a renderer; frontend-only vs global BA; latency per frame.
3. Output: does it give dense per-keyframe depth + confidence we can turn into splats (feeding rgbd.py-style fusion), metric scale handling (we know robot motion).
4. Windows: can lietorch/CUDA extensions build on Windows (MSVC, CUDA 12.4, torch versions); known forks/wheels; WSL as fallback.
5. License and maintenance status of each candidate.
6. Integration sketch: how a backend would plug into ito/reconstruction (read __init__.py, slam.py, rgbd.py, ring.py), what interface it needs, effort estimate.
7. A recommendation (adopt / prototype on Ceres / don't), and a concrete Ceres experiment plan comparing it with MASt3R-SLAM on recorded frames via e2e/slam_replay.py (metrics: heading error median/p95 vs driver heading, restarts per 100 s, coverage, fps, VRAM).
If anything CPU-runnable helps (e.g. checking that a package resolves for torch/CUDA on Windows from metadata), do it; state clearly what is verified vs from papers/READMEs. Cite sources with URLs.
Deliverable: one file docs/research/droid-slam.md (concise, tables welcome) in the PR, nothing else.
```

items.title: 飞特版跟进请教：打印材料/质量、训练策略、HAT 板 PCBA、舵机参数 4 个问题
items.body:
你好！我在按你的飞特 HD-1910 版做复刻，目标是做一只能走路 + 有视觉/语音对话 + 接云端 LLM 的鸭子。
读了 microduck-replica 和 CAD 仓的文档，受益匪浅，有 4 个问题想请教（按我的下单优先级排序）。

## ① 打印材料与整机质量（最急，我要找打印服务下单）

你在 `imu-fix-1015` 里写「整鸭带电池 **806 g**，训练用 820 g，差 1.7%」。
我算了一下：官方 737.2 g + 15 只舵机各重 4.5 g ≈ 804.7 g，对得上。
我想让整机质量尽量贴近你那台，以便直接复用你的实机数据，所以想确认这个 806 g 的构成：

1. **是全 PLA，还是部分件用了铝合金增强？**
   CAD 仓 BOM 里「颈部 / 躯干底座 / 上腿加固板」标注了「可换铝合金增强」——
   你实际打的是塑料还是铝？
2. **填充率（infill）是多少？** 这在 Bambu Studio 的 3MF 里有预设，
   我要找打印服务商打（他们只收 STL，拿不到 3MF 参数），需要知道具体数值。
3. 层高 0.2 / 0.4 喷嘴 / PLA Basic 这几个参数，确认一下我没理解错。

另外：你的 3MF 是 09-15 版，v2.1 改了 TPU 合体轮胎。
**我们这种不做轮滑的版本，是不是直接按 09-15 那 52 个对象打就行？**

## ② 走路策略：重训还是调参

看到你 10-15 的记录里**收回了「舵机不行，要重训」**这个结论，
说「大家好多用他的跑通了」，元凶是 IMU 姿态模式（chip → gyro）。想确认现在的判断：

1. **现成 kissqy V167 策略 + 飞特舵机，是不是直接能走？** 还是要改动作缩放/滤波？
   （你的记录里用了「动作缩放 0.9、头滤波 0.5、腿滤波 0.7」）
2. **你 `software/training/` 里的 `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck-HD1910`，
   打算自己跑完整训练吗？** README 写「尚无本机实测通过的走路策略」
   「本次没有提交付费云端任务」。如果暂时不打算跑，我用 `--hf-jobs` 跑一版
   （官方说约 1–2 h / 十几元），训出来会发布回来给你。
3. 你提到「现有 Microduck 质量惯量仍是原版仿真值，后续需要按飞特实机数据校正」——
   **这个校正做了吗？** 还是仍用原版值？

## ③ HAT 板 / imu_to_dxl 板

看到 issue #25 有人问过套件，当时回答「舵机还没到」。现在应该到了，想再问一下：

1. **HAT 板 / imu_to_dxl 板有打样好的余量可转让吗？** 或者有没有拼单渠道？
   我们自己打样 4 层板 + SMT（113 个贴装位置、含 0603）起订量不划算。
2. 如果买不到，**嘉立创 PCBA 的 SMT 你走过吗？** 有没有踩过坑
   （哪些料要自己备、钢网要不要开）？

## ④ 舵机参数核对

你们和 LuwuDynamics 都用 `1910_m6.json`（`STS3215Actuator`）给 HD-1910 建模。想确认：

1. **HD-1910-C001 是否等同 HLS1910 / STS3215？** 飞特型号命名有点乱，
   XGO-Duck README 写 "HLS1910"，参数文件里写 `sts3215`。
   如果确认同族，我就直接沿用 `1910_m6.json`；否则要做系统辨识。
2. **规格书上的 10 kg·cm 是在几伏下测的？** `1910_m6.json` 里的 `kt` 隐含电压假设，
   我们总线是 6.6–8.2 V（满电 8.4 V），想核对匹配。
3. 减速比、编码器分辨率、回差这三项规格书上没有 —— **你们实测过吗？**

（注：你文档里说「参数不是本项目自行辨识的结果」，所以这条也许没人答得上来 ——
那我就直接沿用并做实机对照。）

---

另外提一下我的扩展方向，如果你也在做可以一起搞：
除了走路，我还要加**视觉 + 语音对话 + 云端 LLM**（大致是 Reachy Mini conversation app 那套）。
有两个硬件问题想请教：

1. **HAT 上麦克风和喇叭的间距，自播报时的回声（AEC）好消吗？**
   我想做声纹识别主人/家人，如果 AEC 做不好声纹就废了。
2. 摄像头装在头里，**你那边出图正常吗？** 官方代码 `--rotate` 默认 90，
   你记录里写「摄像头调整排线后在官方 B1 下出图」—— 是转 90 还是 180？

非常感谢！有问题我也会把结果反馈回来。

items.title: feat(hop): one-foot hopscotch landings — Mjlab-HopLeft / Mjlab-HopRight
items.body:
## What

This builds on `feat/hop-env-training` and adds the step that env's docstring calls "an explicitly later step": **landing on one foot**, hopscotch-style. It is two new task ids on the existing hop env, plus two two-foot variants added during GPU training:

| task | landing |
|---|---|
| `Mjlab-Hop-Flat-MicroDuck` | both feet (see "Two-foot training fixes" below) |
| `Mjlab-HopOnce-Flat-MicroDuck` (4e0e0ad; v2 c99982f; v3 dae9225) | both feet, **one** forward hop, then stand |
| `Mjlab-BunnyHop-Flat-MicroDuck` (c01def8) | both feet, perpetual forward bunny hop that must not fall |
| `Mjlab-HopLeft-Flat-MicroDuck` | left foot only, held |
| `Mjlab-HopRight-Flat-MicroDuck` | right foot only, held |

`make_microduck_hop_env_cfg(landing=..., once=..., perpetual=...)` builds all of them. `once` and `perpetual` are mutually exclusive. The one-foot tasks keep the whole take-off, flight and exploit-guard stack as it is: the butt-bounce clean-time clock, anti-worming, the crouch and mid-air spawns, the launch-velocity shaping and the metrics. The only change is how the landing is judged.

> This PR previously added a separate `Mjlab-Hop{Both,Left,Right}` env against `main`. After finding `feat/hop-env-training` (measured, with five course corrections and an eval battery), I replaced that version with this one, as agreed with the author. The earlier commits are dropped.

## How the landing is judged

`mdp.hop_landing_stance_factor(stance)`:
- **Clean touchdown (latched).** The first foot contact after the completion gate opens must be on the named foot alone. The gate opens after a qualifying flight, or immediately for a mid-air spawn, whose gate is pre-seeded open. A landing on the other foot, or on both feet, latches the episode at zero, so shuffling onto the right stance afterwards earns nothing.
- **In stance now.** The named foot is down and the other is up.
- It is step-guarded, like the other hop accumulators.

These terms take an optional `stance` and multiply by that factor:
- `hop_landing_composite`
- `hop_upright_after_landing`
- `hop_height_after_landing`
- the `stable_landing_rate` metric

`stance=None`, the two-foot task, leaves them unchanged by this factor.

Two other differences for the one-foot tasks:
- The composite's pose target shrinks to the **support leg**, because the other leg is meant to be up.
- The mirror loss is **off**: HopLeft's mirror is HopRight. The two-foot task keeps it on.

## Two-foot training fixes (runs 3–6 and after, added during GPU training)

| commit | why | change |
|---|---|---|
| f7ba77d / c90f92f | run 3 (W&B `rv0u6ot4`) learned a dive: 128/128 episodes touched down on a non-foot body | clean-landing gate, `clean_landing_rate` metric, training video on by default (one W&B upload) |
| 390737b | run 4 (`8gnv2koa`): `clean_landing_rate` fell to 0 because a dirty landing got no gradient | `dirty_landing_scale` curriculum 0.5 → 0.25 → 0; `hop_landing_contact_cost` (weight −2) |
| 46af13c | run 5 (`woqb8g63`): liftoff by about iteration 125, but `clean_landing_rate` stayed 0.00 for all 1000 iterations. The forward pay rewarded the lean that ends in a chest-first dive | `hop_forward_gate_curriculum`: the forward weight (0/1.5/3/5) and the mid-air spawn's forward speed only advance once the EMA of clean landings reaches 0.30, at most one stage per 100 iterations, never backwards |
| cc0e351 / f26d6e5 | run 6 made its **first clean landings**, as a repeated bunny hop. `scripts/eval_hop.py` scores one hop and then a stand, so it under-counts a policy that keeps hopping (model_250: 3.9%, which is an artifact of the eval) | `scripts/eval_hop_per_hop.py` scores every hop in an episode, with pure, unit-tested `segment_hops`/`summarize` |
| 4e0e0ad | run 6 learned to bunny-hop without stopping, because air time and forward progress are max-so-far frontiers and nothing said "stop after one". It was published separately as `chelleboyer/microduck-bunny-hop` | `Mjlab-HopOnce`: `_update_hop_landed_once` latches the first touchdown, and `hop_extra_flight_cost` (weight −4.0) charges every airborne step after it. Adds an `extra_flight_rate` metric. Run 6's finished curricula are collapsed to their final stage. Meant to resume run 6's step counter (`--agent.resume`) |
| 3754c75 / eb502cb / cbf7827 | `scripts/infer_policy.py`, the deployment rehearsal, always opens a viewer and a raw-tty keyboard, so it cannot run in a container | `scripts/rehearse_headless.py` drives the same sim path headless, with an optional mp4. `--match-training-delays` applies training's actuator lag, the `joint_vel` lag and the IMU lag. `--episodes N` pools seeded rollouts. `return_traces` gives per-step tilt, pitch/roll, contacts and flights |
| c01def8 | the published run-6 bunny hop **fell in 59 of 64** delay-matched 10 s rehearsal rollouts. Touchdown pitch swings of ±40–60° built up hop over hop, and falls came both before and after the 3 s training horizon | `Mjlab-BunnyHop` (`perpetual=True`): 10 s episodes, a `fell` termination at 60° tilt, standing spawns up to z 0.126 (the rehearsal's handover height), and the clean-landing latch re-armed on every flight, so a dirty landing only costs until the next liftoff. Without the re-arm, a per-episode latch over 10 s would recreate run 4's no-gradient trap. Own RL cfg `microduck_hop_bunny` |
| c99982f | HopOnce v1 (`asfkt0rq`) halved re-hops (~10 → ~5 per episode) but never stopped them: re-hops still earned the best-so-far `hop_air_time` and `hop_forward_progress` frontiers | **HopOnce v2**: `_hop_before_first_landing` zeroes the payout of four take-off terms after the first touchdown. The frontier itself is kept, because the completion gate reads it. This is HopOnce-only |
| dae9225 | v2 (`lxqqe9j1`) worked, then relapsed at iteration ~3330: re-hops came back and action std regrew. `model_3250` stands 100%, but misses AC #4 mostly on a foot lifted at landing + 0.5 s | **HopOnce v3**: `hop_planted_after_landing` (+1.0); entropy 0.01 → 0.0025 and desired_kl 0.01 → 0.005 (HopOnce only); a save every 50 iterations |

**HopOnce results** (DR'd training-env eval, 64 episodes per spawn; AC #4 = one hop, then a clean stand at landing + 0.5 s):

| policy | one-flight episodes | AC #4 | lifted-foot misses | non-foot contacts | CoM rise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v2 `model_3250` | 57/64 | 52/128 (41–44%) | 57 | 19 | 25.6 mm |
| **v3 `model_3549`** (`ooiuyfac`) | 57/64 | **71/128 (55%)** | 43 | 25 | 16.6 mm |

v3 did not relapse: action std went 0.33 → 0.17 and `extra_flight_rate` settled at about 0.35. The trade-off is a smaller hop (launch 0.39 → 0.35 m/s) and slightly more non-foot contact.

**Run 6 result** (model_1499, per-hop eval; standing, crouch and mid-air spawns):
- about 2.4 hops/s;
- **89–90% of landings clean**;
- 3–4 cm forward per hop, 0.11–0.12 m/s.

**Delay-matched deployment rehearsal** (10 s):

| policy | falls (of 64) | feet-only landings | hops/s | speed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| run 6 model_1499 | 59 | ~94% (3 s) | 2.38 | ~0.12 m/s |
| BunnyHop model_2000 | 28 | — | — | — |
| **BunnyHop model_2998** (`fm49sr5f`) | **9** | **98%** | 1.43 | 0.05 m/s |

The rehearsal has no spawn noise and no DR, so its 64 seeds are at most **8 distinct rollouts** (actuator delay 3–6 × IMU delay 0/1). Read its rates as "k of 8 latency configs", and take statistics from the DR'd training-env evals.

**Edits to existing tests, flagged per CLAUDE.md.** Each follows from a deliberate behaviour change, not from a failing test being bent to pass:
- `tests/test_hf_jobs_flag.py` (f7ba77d): the expected `SUBMIT` argv now ends in `'--video', 'True'`, because video recording is now on by default.
- `tests/test_hop_cfg.py::test_hop_reward_signs` (46af13c): `hop_forward_progress.weight > 0` became `>= 0`. The weight starts at 0 behind the gate. The test also asserts that every gate stage is ≥ 0 and the final stage is > 0.
- `tests/test_hop_cfg.py::test_hop_midair_spawn_carries_forward_momentum` (46af13c): the spawn's `midair_vx_range` now starts at `(0, 0)`. The test asserts that the full `MIDAIR_VX_RANGE` is reached at the gate's final stage.
- `tests/test_hop_once.py` (dae9225): the expected set of HopOnce-only rewards is now `{"hop_extra_flight", "hop_planted"}`, because v3 adds the planted-feet term.

**Protected path.** f7ba77d, 390737b, 46af13c, cc0e351, eb502cb, fad81e2, c99982f, 35517ba, 3fa274c and fdb9de1 edit `AGENTS.md` (run logs, diagnoses and rehearsal notes). That file is protected, so the author should decide whether to keep those edits or split them out.

## Measured on CPU (zero action, 64 envs, 80 steps — not a training run)

| | Hop | HopLeft |
|---|---|---|
| actor obs | (64, 61) | (64, 61) |
| rewards finite | ✓ | ✓ |
| landing terms | pay as before (composite 0.319 mean episode sum) | ≈0 (0.002) |
| touchdowns latched | — | 15 (mid-air spawns) |
| clean left-foot touchdowns | — | **2** |

## Hypotheses (Gate 2)

- **Whether a one-foot landing is holdable on this robot at all is unmeasured.**
- If HopLeft/HopRight struggle to find the one-foot touchdown, the next world change to try is tucking the non-landing leg in the mid-air bucket for these two tasks. Per AGENTS.md: change the world, not the pay. It is not done here.

## Tests

- `python harness/ci.py` on fdb9de1: **CHECKS_OK, UNIT_PASSED tests=357**.
- `tests/test_hop_landing.py` covers:
  - the stance factor on a fake env;
  - the one-foot cfgs;
  - the clean-landing latch and dirty-landing scale;
  - the forward gate: it starts closed, dirty landings or no flight never open it, it moves one stage per dwell and never backwards, and vx scales with the stage.
- New test files:
  - `tests/test_hop_once.py`: the cfg shape, the plain hop unchanged, cost sizing, the first hop free and every later flight step charged, mid-air spawns, the step guard, v2's first-flight-only terms, and v3's planted term and PPO settings.
  - `tests/test_bunny_hop.py`: long episodes, fall termination, the handover spawn, the per-flight latch re-arm (and that it lasts the episode without the flag), collapsed curricula, the episodic hop unchanged, and exclusive modes.
  - `tests/test_training_video.py`: the video default.
  - `tests/test_eval_hop_per_hop.py`: hop segmentation and the summary.
  - `tests/test_rehearse_headless.py`: a 0.5 s rollout when the ONNX is present, plus the delay mode.
- Edits to existing tests are listed above. `tests/test_eval_hop.py` is unchanged.

## Commands, for a person to run

```bash
uv run train Mjlab-HopOnce-Flat-MicroDuck  --env.scene.num-envs 4096 --agent.resume ... --hf-jobs   # continue HopOnce v3
uv run train Mjlab-BunnyHop-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 4096 --agent.resume ... --hf-jobs   # a bunny hop that must not fall
# once the two-foot hop lands clean and holds:
uv run train Mjlab-HopLeft-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 4096 --agent.max_iterations 1000 --hf-jobs
```

items.title: Build brief: let anyone — agent or human — control the duck
items.body:
# Build brief: `microduck-cli` — let anyone control the duck

Welcome to the AgentCulture mesh. This repo was provisioned with
`guild create` from `culture-agent-template`; you are the resident agent and
this issue is your build brief. Run `/init` first to expand the CLAUDE.md seed
into a real runtime prompt, then work through the sections below.

## 1. Identity (already provisioned — don't rename)

| Thing | Value |
|---|---|
| Repo / agent | `agentculture/microduck-cli` |
| Import package | `microduck_cli` |
| Console command | `microduck` |
| PyPI distribution | `microduck-cli` |
| Visibility | public |

The command is deliberately decoupled from the repo token: you type `microduck`,
you import `microduck_cli`, you `pip install microduck-cli`. The explain-catalog
root is already aliased to `microduck` so `teken cli doctor --strict` passes —
don't remove that alias.

## 2. What this repo is

`microduck-cli` is **the CLI that lets anyone control the MicroDuck robot** —
any agent, any human, one surface. It is the second consumer of the mesh's
shared robot runtime, and the sibling of `reachy-mini-cli`.

### Agent-agnostic is the headline requirement

This is the defining constraint, stated by the operator, and it should shape
every design call:

> Agent agnostic. Humans, anyone.

Concretely, that means:

- **No privileged driver.** Claude, a local 270M model, a shell script, a
  cron job, a human typing at a terminal, and a test harness all drive the duck
  through *the same* verbs with the same semantics. There is no "agent mode"
  that unlocks capabilities the CLI surface doesn't have.
- **Text in, text out.** Every verb takes `--json` and splits results→stdout,
  errors+diagnostics→stderr, never mixed. That is what makes it drivable by
  something that isn't a person.
- **Errors are actionable, never tracebacks.** Two-line text errors
  (`error: …` / `hint: …`), structured in JSON mode. An agent that gets a
  traceback cannot recover; one that gets a remediation hint can.
- **Write verbs are dry-run by default, `--apply` commits.** Agents call CLIs in
  loops. Safe-by-default is mandatory, and doubly so when the loop moves a
  physical actuator.
- **Stateless invocations where possible.** Don't require a session an external
  driver has to remember; if state is needed, it lives on disk and is
  inspectable.

## 3. The architecture: copy `reachy-mini-cli`, import `neurosymbolic-system`

You are **not** designing a control architecture from scratch. Two repos give
you the whole thing:

- **`agentculture/reachy-mini-cli`** — the worked example. A mature agent-first
  robot CLI: verb routing, the error contract, the output split, the `explain`
  catalog, the sense-stage logging convention, and the noun catalog. **Read its
  `CLAUDE.md` end to end** — it is the most detailed architecture document in
  the mesh, and its "the arc that got here" section will save you from repeating
  three deletions it already paid for. Copy its *patterns*.
- **`agentculture/neurosymbolic-system`** — a brand-new sibling provisioned
  alongside this repo, being extracted right now from `reachy-mini-cli`'s
  `reachy/behavior/` runtime. It owns the generic neurosymbolic control loop:
  behaviors, lifetimes, arbitration, the rule engine, the intent driver, and the
  50 Hz tick composition. **Import it. Do not fork it.**

### What that leaves you to build

If the extraction is done right, a second robot costs exactly three things —
and those three things are your repo:

1. **A sense adapter** — MicroDuck's perception, published through the runtime's
   `SenseProvider` protocol.
2. **A target sink** — MicroDuck's actuators, consuming the composed command the
   runtime emits. The runtime deliberately doesn't know what a "head" is; a
   duck's actuators are not a Reachy's.
3. **A rule pack** — the duck's own behaviors and reactions, in the runtime's
   rule schema (Reachy's `default_rules.toml` is the format precedent).

Plus the CLI shell around them. **If you find yourself needing to change
`neurosymbolic-system`'s core to make the duck work, that is a finding worth
filing there** — it means a seam is in the wrong place, and you are the test
that proves it. File the issue rather than working around it locally; being the
second consumer is your most useful role in the first weeks.

## 4. Open questions — park these, don't guess

The operator has not specified the hardware, and **nothing in the mesh describes
MicroDuck today**. Do not invent a spec. Record these as first-class unknowns
and get them answered before committing to a transport:

1. **What is the MicroDuck, physically?** Vendor/platform, actuators (wheels?
   legs? head? beak? servos?), sensors (camera, mic, IMU, bumpers?), and
   compute (onboard SBC, or tethered to a host?). Every design call below
   depends on this and none of it is guessable.
2. **What is the control transport?** A vendor SDK, serial/USB, BLE, Wi-Fi/HTTP,
   ROS, MQTT? Is there an on-robot daemon (Reachy's model) or does the CLI talk
   to hardware directly?
3. **Is control local or networked?** If networked, discovery and multi-host
   access are real design surface. Reachy's `wireless` noun is the precedent.
4. **Does the duck have audio/voice?** That decides whether the embodiment and
   speech layers of the Reachy design are in scope at all.
5. **Simulation.** Given the hardware is unspecified and the runtime is meant to
   be testable headless, a simulated duck sink is plausibly the *first* thing to
   build — it unblocks the CLI, the rule pack, and CI without hardware. Consider
   leading with it.

Until #1 and #2 are answered, the honest move is to build against
`neurosymbolic-system`'s seams and a simulated sink, and let the real transport
drop in behind the sink interface.

## 5. Related siblings — confirm lanes before absorbing

- `reachy-mini-cli` — the other robot on the same runtime. Peer, not upstream.
- `neurosymbolic-system` — your runtime dependency.
- `webcam-cli` / `media-cli` — capture-device and media-plane siblings; if the
  duck has a camera or mic, compose these rather than growing your own device
  layer.
- `reachy-lobes` / `lobes-cli`, `embodiment` — local-model cognition and the
  embodiment layer. Cognition is *not* this repo's lane; the CLI exposes control,
  and an agent (any agent) supplies the thinking.

## 6. Housekeeping owed after `/init`

- Run `/init` to expand the CLAUDE.md seed.
- **Backend reconcile:** `culture.yaml` inherits `backend: colleague` from the
  template while the CLAUDE.md seed prose says `claude`. Pick one and make the
  prompt file agree (the backend-consistency invariant).
- **Trusted Publisher:** `guild create` configures the GitHub side only.
  Register a Trusted Publisher for `microduck-cli` on PyPI **and** TestPyPI, or
  the publish workflow will fail with `invalid-publisher`.
- You are registered in guildmaster's `docs/skill-sources.md` as a downstream
  consumer of the canonical skill set; the kit is already vendored in
  `.claude/skills/`.

- guildmaster (Claude)

items.title: 复刻前确认：成功样机的身体IMU、供电、软件版本及完整装配指南
items.body:
你好，感谢整理和分享制作资料。我是硬件初学者，计划按 XL330 路线做个人复刻，目前尚未采购整机或通电，想在购买前确认资料能覆盖到哪一步。

我已下载 `maker-20260916` 的四个 ZIP，并按仓库 manifest 核对 SHA-256。制作包中的 README 和 `01_物料清单.md` 说明：包内不含产品运行时、独立 IMU 和旧整机供电方案，完成后的新供电/身体姿态方案也尚未提供。仓库同时展示了成功复刻的样机，所以想请教这台样机实际使用的配套资料：

1. **身体 IMU**：成功样机使用哪块板、哪版固件、什么安装方向？它是否兼容当前官方 `robotd` 的 `imu_to_dxl v2`（LSM6DSV16X、ID 200、地址124）？若需另购或自行制造，是否有对应入口？
2. **供电**：样机15台 XL330 的实际供电范围是什么？是否有在 ROBOTIS 标称3.7–6.0V范围内验证过站立、行走的接法及配套策略？公开包已提醒不能直接2S供电，因此不敢照旧接线图上电。
3. **软件配套**：能否提供与演示样机对应的系统镜像，或主控系统版本、运行仓库/commit、配置、IMU固件、ONNX模型版本清单？我已验证官方 `alpha_walking.onnx` 能加载和做合成输入推理，但还没有任何真机验证。
4. **装配说明**：[这篇复刻文章](https://wuwei.me/2026/10/11/microduck/)提到《Microduck复刻装配指南》。该指南是否另有公开入口？我在已下载包中没有找到包含逐位置紧固件、线束针序和完整接线的指南本体。如当前仍有需要自行设计/验证的部分，列明范围也很有帮助。

我的目标是先确认一套与成功样机一致、可以实际采购/制造和部署的组合，再进入单件试印、台架检查和整机装配。若上述部分暂未公开或尚未验证，直接说明即可，方便初学者判断何时适合开工。谢谢！

items.title: feat(training): add multi-task language motion curricula
items.body:
Teach the language-conditioned Microduck student additional motion tasks while retaining traceable teacher demonstrations, native LeRobot training, and physical closed-loop evaluation. The curriculum covers head actions, backward walking, turning and stopping; fixed black images isolate language-conditioned motion at this stage.

v19 completed exactly 4002 updates. Final strict success was 41/74 eligible cases (78 scheduled, four teacher-invalid moving starts), including backward 0/6, left turn 1/6, right turn 0/6, forward-stop 5/6 and backward-stop 3/4. Paired stop/continue discrimination passed only 3/10 pairs. These results do not establish replacement of the teacher or real-time control.

The v20 zero-update backward diagnostic reproduced the existing failures exactly, verified native text preprocessing and compared matched expert states across six texts. The two trained backward expressions fit expert trajectories similarly, but the training-body closed loop still fell at tick137. The next bounded v21 experiment compares focused backward-only training on the original ten episodes against those episodes plus accepted teacher-recovery windows. Both arms share normalization and initial weights; the budget is two discarded smoke updates and 1000 formal updates per arm (2004 total). Collection produced five accepted recovery windows out of six (1000 frames), preserving the stationary rejection. The 134-episode/31400-frame union passed independent raw-data, normalization, native episode-sampler and DataLoader audits. v21 is complete (exit0), with exactly2004 updates and independently verified66 comparative plus2 smoke physical trials. Strict backward was zero0/10, control1/10, mixed0/10; old-task regression fell from9/12 to7/12 in both trained arms. This single-seed correction recipe did not improve strict success and is not a replacement for v19. Newly appended correction-state fitting remains unmeasured by the inherited first-family probes; that is the next proposed diagnostic, not an executed experiment. A preparation-only Git provenance failure was recovered without recollection or optimization; the synchronized upstream has no .git metadata, so verified content hashes are recorded. Old-task regression exposes forgetting; these diagnostic checkpoints are not deployment candidates by default.

Validation: training `make fix`, `make lint`, `make test` passed (17 tests passed, two skipped); independent CPU audits verify v19/v20 metrics, model inputs, action timing and failure reproduction. v21 final audits verified every stored input/action mapping, success score, effective normalization and training budget. Mixed median inference251ms exceeds the100ms execution window; physics was paused. Automatic follow-up is being paused after delivery; no additional round was started. Saved raw failures, configurations, checkpoints and per-tick evidence remain on the devbox. No physical hardware, visual capability, real-time inference, automatic merge, or additional training budget is implied.

items.title: Sweeps: a parameter sweep system maps where the headstand routine fails
items.body:
We are building a system that evaluates the headstand routine across controlled physics parameters and incoming handover states, then reports where each stage fails. We then use it to answer one robustness question at a time. This is the umbrella for the sweep work, and a sub-issue of #7, the learning loop on Anyscale and Ray. The sweep system is the measurement layer that loop needs.

## Why

The routine succeeded in 87 of 96 attempts (`results/verified/`), and each of the six policies passes 32/32 on its own. That score cannot tell us why the 9 attempts failed. The evaluator loads each task with `play=True`, which "changes nothing" (`microduck_headstand_env_cfg.py` docstring). Each attempt therefore gets a random draw of center of mass, mass and inertia, joint friction, armature, IMU orientation, encoder bias, and the BAM actuator's voltage and delay. The reports keep neither the draw nor the state handed over between policies. A back-roll failure could come from the pose the kick-up handed over, from the physics draw, or from both.

## What the system does

We pin a named parameter, called an axis, to a chosen value for each environment instead of drawing it at random. We run the full routine or a single policy across a grid of axis values, and record one row per attempt. The report is a map of success rate and first failed stage over each axis. Every later change, from a retrained checkpoint to a wider randomization range or a backlash variant, is scored against the same grid.

## Sub-issues

1. #11 Spike: pin one axis per environment and sweep it in a single GPU batch
2. #12 Sweep harness: axis config, per-attempt records, and the map report
3. #13 Baseline map of the current routine checkpoints
4. #14 Backlash axis and whether the headstand needs `-Backlash-` variants
5. #15 Handover state as a sweep axis

#11 decides the batching design, and #12 is built on its answer. #13, #14 and #15 each need #12.

## Later uses

The same system scores training fan-outs, meaning parallel training runs over randomization ranges or reward weights. It also places a measured real robot on the map once the XL330 test bench (`scripts/testbench_sim2real.py`) or a real duck gives us friction and voltage numbers.
