items.title: [Tasks] Add MicroDuck flat velocity walking task [4/6]
items.body:
# Description

Adds `IsaacContrib-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`: MicroDuck flat walking on Newton MJWarp with native BAM servos (#8161), ported from [microduck_rl](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl) through the original Lab MicroDuck task. It keeps that task's 14-joint action order, 61-value actor and 76-value critic inputs, 50 Hz control, rewards, command sampling, randomization, curricula, and PPO settings, so existing checkpoints load.

- Encoder bias is owned by the biased joint-position action term and IMU misalignment by its startup event term; observations read them from there.
- Joint velocity uses the core one-step `delay_min_lag`/`delay_max_lag`; `delayed_observation` only provides the IMU lag redrawn on a fixed 64-step period.
- Curricula use `modify_term_cfg` with one `staged_value` schedule; stages switch at `>=` their step (the old task used `>` for some, a one-step difference).
- Reuses core terms where they match (`body_projected_gravity_b`, `randomize_rigid_body_*`, `randomize_joint_parameters`, `push_by_setting_velocity`, `joint_pos_limits`, `action_rate_l2`, `bad_orientation`, `UniformVelocityCommand`). Task-local rewards keep upstream's formulas, which differ from the nearest core terms: tracking combines planar and off-axis error in one kernel, `body_ang_vel_xy_l2` uses the world-frame trunk rate, `foot_slip` squares contact speed, and `self_collision_cost` reads the filtered force matrix.
- MJWarp line search uses 50 iterations instead of 20; 20 repeatedly exhausted the current solver.
- Critic foot observations, the upright reward and a termination guard against non-finite MJWarp states, which occurred under heavy contact in the original task.
- The environment-browser preview image is served from the docs image host (to be uploaded), not committed.

**Stacked on #8266.** [Task-only diff](https://github.com/AntoineRichard/IsaacLab/compare/antoiner/feat/bam-backlash...antoiner/feat/microduck-flat-velocity).

## Type of change

- New feature

## Validation

Runs used a local mirror of the `isaac-dev` Nucleus MicroDuck assets until the public S3 mirror syncs.

- `uv run python -m pytest source/isaaclab_tasks/test/test_microduck_velocity.py` — 1 passed (61/76 inputs, policy term order, action joint order, per-reset BAM friction draw). These guard the deployed ONNX interface: a reorder against the USD's different joint order silently breaks shipped checkpoints, which stepping tests cannot see. Stepping is covered by `test_contrib_environments_kitless.py`; 100 random-action steps stayed finite here.
- Joint-velocity delay check without noise: the observation equals the previous step's joint velocity exactly.
- Curriculum check: at the last stage, action-rate weight −1.0, head-bias weight −3.0, standing fraction 0.25, widest head ranges, and CoM ranges ±0.015/±0.01 m; encoder bias and IMU misalignment sampled into their owners.
- Supplied `velocity_flat.onnx` (original Lab checkpoint, iteration 49,999), 32 envs × 1,000 control steps:

| Playback condition | Falls | Timeouts | Mean planar velocity error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed 0.15 m/s forward, play mode | 0 | 32 | 0.136 m/s |
| Training commands, corruption and disturbances | 0 | 32 | 0.185 m/s |

  This shows the existing policy runs stably, not exact parity with the old dynamics.
- `uv run isaaclab -f`

## Not in this PR

- Rough and backlash variants (#8270), recovery task (#8271).

## Follow-ups

- Replace `delayed_observation` with core `ObservationTermCfg.delay_*`. Kept for parity: the IMU lag is redrawn on a fixed 64-step period with a per-environment phase, whereas core redraws with a per-sample hold probability.
- Find the source of the occasional non-finite MJWarp states and drop the observation guards; reset-time CoM randomization on Newton is a candidate.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution guidelines and ran `uv run isaaclab -f`
- [x] Validated with focused coverage and the test-audit criteria
- [x] Added a changelog fragment for `isaaclab_tasks`

items.title: Maploc: mapping & localization as a robotd-hosted subcrate — and why it never worked
items.body:
Absorbs `microduck_maploc_rs` (already Rust) as the `maploc/` subcrate — and, per the brief, spends most of its effort on **why the results were "kinda ok but noisy" and relocalization never worked**. Every fix below was found and verified offline against the prototype's own recorded `.mdlg` sessions, using a replay bench that ships with the crate.

## The bugs, each with the measurement that exposed it

1. **Sensor-origin asymmetry.** Maps were inked from the *sensor* world pose (10–15 cm ahead of the body, moving with head yaw), but MCL and brute-force relocalize scored beams from the *body* pose. `Scan` is now per-beam `origin → endpoint` pairs; every consumer derives world beams identically. The shape also makes scans **composable** — frames at one body pose with different head yaws merge exactly.
2. **Off-map cherry-picking.** Relocalize/MCL silently skipped out-of-bounds beams, so a wrong pose that threw 95% of its scan off the map was scored on the agreeing remainder — measured beating the true pose with mean residuals near zero from a tenth of the beams. Every beam now counts (off-map = full clamp).
3. **See-through degeneracy.** Endpoints-only scoring let poses dump whole scans into dense wall blobs at ~0 residual. One mid-ray occupancy sample per beam breaks it.
4. **The ~9 cm map noise floor.** Stop-and-scan inked every raw frame; walking-passer-by transients and the sensor's far-range noise tail set a floor above every downstream gate (loop closures gated at 10 cm never fired; the true pose scored worse than the 5 cm relocalize acceptance — *the* "never locks" mechanism, jointly with #2 accepting lies). New `accumulator`: a still window's frames **vote** per endpoint cell; beams confirmed by ≥3 distinct frames survive; ranges cap at 2 m; one wide composite comes out per stop.
5. **The correction that never reached tracking.** The current submap's pose-graph node was created with no edge attached — invisible to the optimizer — and the post-closure tracked-pose correction rides that node. Closures moved every frozen anchor while live tracking sailed on uncorrected (the prototype wired it identically). Nodes now chain at open time; pinned by a synthetic walked-loop test.
6. **Over-closing / room-folding.** 43 "closures" in one 5-minute session folded the two recorded rooms onto each other: aliased matches pass every local gate in blobby rooms. Three data-derived defenses: witnesses are the *largest* scans (≥150 beams — the 12-beam scraps were vetoing the 6000-beam composites' consensus), a closure needs **two agreeing strong witnesses**, and its correction must be plausible for the odometry drift accumulable over the gap it spans. Also: coverage is measured against beams landing in cells the target submap actually *observed*.

**Bench result on the recorded room**: brute-force relocalize went 0/13 → 6/20 probes within 30 cm/20° — every miss a narrow-wedge probe, every wide head-sweep composite a hit — and MCL stopped locking onto wrong clusters. The clear operational lesson, now quantified: *relocalization wants a deliberate head sweep*, which the robot can do on demand (follow-up).

## Integration

- **`[maploc]` in robotd.toml, off by default** (documented in `deploy/robotd.toml`): `enabled`, `mode = "stop_and_scan" | "continuous"` (the requested toggle), `map_path`, `wipe_on_boot`. Sessions autosave once a minute + on shutdown, restore on boot.
- **robotd hosts it** on a niced (+10) worker thread: the control loop pays one `try_send` per tick; depth frames arrive via a reconnecting subscription to tofd's socket; frames go through the Posture-aware (lean-corrected) reprojection.
- **`robot.map` (API v12 → v13)**: a `robot.state`-style subscription; `map.frame` notifications carry the trinary grid as base64 (tiny RFC 4648 module in the proto), map-frame pose, tracking flag, submap/loop counts, at 1 Hz while subscribed.
- **Monitor**: the path panel becomes **" map "** when frames flow — walls in braille, free space a sparse stipple, the robot its yellow marker (magenta `?` while searching) — and stays the odometry track otherwise. **`m` puts either view over the whole terminal.**
- Trimmed from the satellite: TCP telemetry (later, per decision), `rand`/`rayon` (pinned xoshiro — relocalize runs replay bit-for-bit — and `std::thread::scope`), the fixed-mount projection.

## Testing

- Workspace green (46 suites), clippy clean. New: 15+ maploc unit tests including the synthetic walked-loop closure test, accumulator voting, session round-trip (format bumped to v2 for the Scan reshape), b64 RFC vectors, map render.
- Replay bench: `cargo run -p maploc --release --example replay -- <session.mdlg>` — builds the map (PGM dump), measures window self-consistency, probes relocalization with truth-pose scores. The prototype's recorded sessions in `~/MISC/microduck_maploc-rs/sessions/` drive it.
- Hardware: enable `[maploc]`, `robotctl monitor`, walk stop-and-scan around a room and watch the map build live; restart robotd and see the session restore. CPU: watch `top` — the worker is niced, and the loop's `hz` in the monitor should not move.

Follow-ups noted, not included: head-sweep-on-relocalize (the robot pans its own head to build the wide composite that provably relocalizes), `robot.look`-style goal/navigation (planner + follower are ported and dormant), MCL boot relocalize wiring in robotd (the crate machinery is fixed and tested; the robotd flow wants the head sweep first).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: Use the Microduck's ToF depth sensor, as an optional composable capability
items.body:
The Microduck has a head ToF depth sensor (microduck `tof/`, `tofd`): a VL53L5CX or VL53L8CX, an **8×8 grid of distances** (64 zones, a few metres, roughly 45–65° FOV), looking where the head looks, plus a head IMU (`head_imu.stream`, 100 Hz). It is not a scanning LiDAR: too sparse to map a room on its own, but useful as metric depth.

**Possible uses:** metric scale for monocular reconstruction, depth sanity/outlier rejection, floor/wall distance, obstacle stop in drive tests (#25).

**Architecture requirement (owner):** composable. The core must not depend on specific robot parts.
- Robot drivers advertise optional capabilities (e.g. `depth.sparse`, `imu`), each a generic message on the wire (sparse depth: directions/zones + ranges + timestamp + sensor pose).
- Reconstruction backends declare what they can use; the pipeline feeds what is available. Ito already has an `rgb + depth` submit path (`rgbd` backend) to build on.
- A robot without the sensor works exactly as now.

**To do:**
- [ ] tof in the sim (MuJoCo rays) so it can be tested without hardware
- [ ] wire message + Microduck driver adapter
- [ ] first consumer: scale/depth prior in reconstruction

items.title: Sim: head camera stutters (frames hold 40, 40, 20 ms of motion by turns)
items.body:
The virtual Microduck's head camera stutters frame by frame: during a smooth head turn the image moves 12, 12, 6, 12, 12, 6 px per frame.

Cause: physics runs in 20 ms batches (four 5 ms steps under one lock, one per 50 Hz control tick), and the render thread in `drivers/microduck/sim_body.py` reads the live world on its own 33 ms clock. Each frame catches one batch or two by turns, so consecutive frames hold 40, 40, 20 ms of motion. No real camera does this. There is no image noise in the sim; it only adds noise to the IMU and ToF readings.

Fix: render each frame from the physics state at its exact moment in sim time (every 1/30 s), paced to the wall clock. This touches only Ito's sim camera code, not upstream Microduck, and it applies to the main sim and the beta sim.

Out of scope: the walking sway (~5°, the gait rocking the body), which a real Microduck would also have.

items.title: Register signed-percentage sensory areas at the width the encoder streams
items.body:
Found while running a balance-learning brain on the microduck biped through the MuJoCo controller: the SmartIMU orientation area was created 4 columns wide and each RawIMU sub-area 3 wide, while the connector streams 8 and 6 (a plus and a minus column per component). FEAGI dropped the extra columns, so a negative pitch never reached the brain until someone widened the area by hand, and the next controller restart shrank it again because agent registration re-applies the registered width.

The controller cannot fix this: `register_sensor_units` carries no width, and the encoder tuple `{"Percentage": [depth, positioning, is_signed, "D3"]}` is all FEAGI sees.

Changes:
- `agent_registration.rs`: `extract_signed_percentage_channel_width` reads `is_signed` and `D1..D4` from the encoder tuple and returns `dims * 2`, matching `PercentageNeuronVoxelXYZPEncoder::channel_width` (signed 1D Linear keeps its single along-Z column; unsigned encoders keep the template width). RawIMU and SmartIMU join the grouped-strip width expansion so two IMU sites on one unit register `2 * 6` columns, which is where the encoder writes channel 1.
- RawIMU and SmartIMU templates: `channel_dimensions_default` / min / max are `[6, 1, *]` and `[8, 1, *]` instead of 3 and 4, so areas created without an agent (MCP `create_io_area_for_unit`) match too.

Tests: six new cases in `sensory_dimension_extraction_tests` (signed D3 → 6 with site expansion, D4 → 8, Fractional D3 → 6, signed D1 Linear stays 1, unknown dimensionality and short tuples fall back to the template); `tests_genomic` IMU template assertions updated. `cargo test` for feagi-api (lib), feagi-structures and feagi-sensorimotor passes.

Not verified live: the running desktop experiment was not restarted on a rebuilt FEAGI. After deploy, `list_io_areas_compact` should show orientation `[8,1,10]` and each RawIMU sub-area `[6,1,10]` straight after launch, with the minus-pitch column carrying data.

Related: Neuraville/nrs-embodiments#258 (controller-side items from the same session). The Python SDK docstrings in `feagi/pns/brain_output.py` and `brain_input.py` still describe the IMU sub-areas as `[3, 1, z]` / `[4, 1, z]`; they are comments only.

items.title: armless-hd1910: 混搭 14 舵机版 spec（父议题）
items.body:
# Spec：混搭 14 舵机版 Microduck（HD-1910，无臂形态）

> 源自 `混搭方案-14舵机HD1910.md` + 2026-10-12 grill 五问答。
> 决策已定：Q1=C 无臂起步不封死、Q2=A 分批采购、Q3=A 保留 OpenRB-150、Q4=A 本地 2× RTX 5090D、Q5=A 起步（规格书 BAM 训「能走」）→ B 收尾（单摆辨识精调）。

## Problem Statement

官方 Dynamixel XL330 舵机因机器鸭热潮断货炒价（淘宝现货 ¥456–498/颗），按 19 舵机带臂版买齐成本不可接受。用户已有 FanGe 打印件（19 舵机带臂版几何，沉没成本 ¥50 耗材），需要一条能走、可控成本、且不浪费已有打印件的路线。

## Solution

按 FanGe README 的 14 舵机无臂版装机：腿部 10 + 头颈 4 全部用飞特 HD-1910-C001（¥123/颗），手臂 6 舵机直接不买、手臂打印件封存（保留以后升级可能）。执行器更换导致官方 walk 策略作废，走完整 sim2real 重训管线（本地 2× RTX 5090D 训练）。驱动层从 Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 换成飞特 SCS，物理链路保留 OpenRB-150 USB 串口透传。

## User Stories

1. As 建造者，I want 用 ¥123/颗的国产舵机装出一只能走的鸭，so that 不为炒价的 XL330 支付 4 倍价钱
2. As 建造者，I want 手臂舵机完全不采购、手臂打印件封存不装，so that 省 6 舵机（≈¥738）且保留日后补臂的升级路径
3. As 建造者，I want 先买 2 只 HD-1910 + URT-2 做台架验证，so that 在补购剩余 14 只之前用实物否掉「薄 3mm + 舵盘凸出」两个最大适配风险
4. As 建造者，I want 保留 OpenRB-150 当 USB-串口透传，so that 硬件零改动、软件风险集中到协议层一处
5. As 建造者，I want 用本地 2× RTX 5090D 重训 walk 策略，so that 不租云、训练成本可忽略、迭代不受配额限制
6. As 建造者，I want 第一版重训用规格书 BAM 参数走通全管线（能走标准），so that 最快见到走路；单摆辨识作为收尾迭代而非前置阻塞
7. As 操作者，I want 14 只舵机按 constants 表烧好 ID / 1Mbps / 响应等级并打开过流过压保护，so that 装机后总线一次点亮
8. As 操作者，I want 实机先站立后行走（平整地面、可随时抱起），so that 首次上电风险可控
9. As 操作者，I want 收尾阶段用备用舵机做单摆台架辨识并重训 v2，so that 步态质量逼近原版且辨识参数今后每只鸭复用
10. As 未来会话的 agent，I want ADR 和 GLOSSARY 记录执行器/形态/链路三个决策及其理由，so that 不会建议「换回 XL330」或「把手臂装上」这种已被否决的路线
11. As 未来会话的 agent，I want 票据图（blocking edges），so that 快递等待期可以并行推进纯软件票（MJCF、驱动层、训练环境）
12. As 观看者，I want 鸭子以官方无臂形态走路，so that 外形与 Pollen 官方一致

## Implementation Decisions

- **执行器**：14 × 飛特 HD-1910-C001（腿 10 + 头颈 4），单协议飞特 SCS；出「模式 4：纯位置 PD（Sim2Real）」直接对应 RL 落地；KP/KD 起步值参照 Xgoduck 运行时（KP 6 / KD 20）
- **形态**：无臂（官方 Pollen 形态）。手臂打印件（shoulder/humerus/radius/arm_bearing_support ×2）不装配、不改造、妥善封存
- **采购节奏**：分两批。首批 2 只 + URT-2（¥291）做台架与试装验证；通过后补 14 只（含备用）+ 主控/IMU/电池
- **物理链路**：保留 OpenRB-150 作 USB-串口透传；UART 直连 + 半双工缓冲留给 v2
- **ID 表**：以 constants 表为准（1–14：右腿 1–5、左腿 6–10、头颈 11–14），不是 assembly.md 的带臂 19-ID 表
- **仿真**：从现有 MJCF 派生无臂 14-DoF 版（删 6 臂 body/actuator，头颈从 1 个执行器扩成 4 个，与 constants 的 4 头颈关节一一对应）；删除而非质量归零，使质量分布与实机一致
- **BAM**：先规格书占位（减速比 1:320、回差 ≤0.5°、12bit 磁编码、vin_range 5.0–6.5V 对应 6V 电池带载区间）；收尾阶段单摆辨识替换精确值
- **训练**：本地 2× RTX 5090D（Blackwell sm_120，需 CUDA ≥12.8 的 PyTorch）；域随机化按无臂质量分布 + HD-1910 电压区间重设
- **驱动层**：Dynamixel SDK → 飞特 SCS（scservo_sdk 或手写帧协议）；需实现 ping、sync_write 目标位置、sync_read 位置/速度/电压；串口探测路径改为 OpenRB-150 实际路径
- **已核实事实（2026-10-12）**：walk.onnx 输入 obs [1,51] / 输出 actions [1,14]；constants 表 14 电机含头颈 4 关节——head 4 关节确实是策略动作空间的一部分，训练 MJCF 必须带 4 头颈执行器。注意：无臂 MJCF 会改变 obs 维度，重训配置的 obs/action 维度必须自洽，导出 ONNX 由驱动栈实测加载

## Testing Decisions

- 驱动层用 mock 串口传输做单元测试（帧构造/解析、校验和、sync_read 组包），不依赖实物；台架上用 2 只首批舵机做集成验证
- 仿真验收走对齐启动器（aligned launcher）：MJCF nq/nu 与 14 电机映射关系打印核对 + 站立不倒 + 行走速度参考
- 试装验收是物理判定：femur/tibia 腔体装得进 HD-1910、舵盘配合件能锁紧；失败则记录并触发 fanhao375 v2.1 `-FT` 改件补打印
- 重训验收：策略在仿真内稳定行走（步速参考社区公开值量级）+ 导出 ONNX 能被驱动栈加载推理
- 实机验收分级：站立 → 原地小步 → 平整地面直线行走，每级稳定再升下一级

## Out of Scope

- 手臂 6 舵机（采购、装配、驱动、进策略全部不做；打印件封存）
- UART 直连主控链路（v2 议题）
- 摄像头/ToF 等感知扩展（本次只要「能走」）
- 官方 Pollen 软件栈（duck-sim/microduck_rl）的改动——本次全部工作在 FanGe 树
- 商用/发布考虑（CC BY-SA-NC 非商用约束照旧）

## Further Notes

- 方案原文（BOM、ID 表、装配差异、风险清单）见 `混搭方案-14舵机HD1910.md`；其 ⚠️ 项随事实核实在原文件更新
- HD-1910 若试装失败：fanhao375/microduck-replica-cad v2.1 `-FT` 已提供 8 个舵盘配合改动件（STEP/3MF）
- 快递等待期（首批舵机在途）与纯软件票完全并行：票 01/02/03 无阻塞可直接开工

items.title: Add a physical HD1910M prototype and a measured dance policy
items.body:
Sweep of 2026-09-27 → 2026-09-29. **207 → 209 entries.**

## Added

- **[RDK X5 MicroDuck](https://github.com/Xiaomiju-x/rdk-x5-microduck)** (Hardware). A real physical prototype on Feetech HD1910M servos, with an RDK X5 as the brain over a bus-servo adapter and an external IMU. It's assembled and shown taking a short walk on flat ground, and the failed early takes are published beside the successful one.
  - **Caveat, stated in the entry:** the author's own readme says the demo is *a replay of a recorded servo-target sequence with live correction on one joint*, **not** the full policy running each step, and that no HD1910M-specific policy has been trained yet.
  - It redistributes no official meshes or weights (no STL/STEP/ONNX in the tree) and ships a `NOTICE.md`. Apache-2.0.
- **[microduck-groove](https://huggingface.co/kramp/microduck-groove)** (Policies). Ten-second in-place dance, published with its `robotctl policy add` line. Simulation: never falls, max trunk tilt 1.6°, but it bounces at 87% of the reference amplitude and ~126 BPM against a 100 BPM target, and the planned head nod, tilt and hip sway were **not learned**. The entry also notes the training fork is unpublished, so the commit on its card doesn't exist upstream.

## Skipped

- **`DANVEZ/microduck-replica-guide`**. A fifth replica compilation, under an unasserted licence, whose own readme says *"no one has built one from this repository"*. It's honest, but everything in it is gathered from sources already listed
- **`zhangpf21/vlm-microduck`**. Sim-only red-box detector, no licence
- **`witcheer/microduck-walk-rough`**. Its card says the terrain curriculum stayed on the easiest tier, so it's effectively a flat-ground walker; already covered by the skill-tree entry
- Empty or undescribed repos (`xiaohu-art`, `superobk/microduck-imu`, `BaoBao112233`, `rbmakers`, `dongheonh`) and `kathula29/bird-robot` (a different robot)

## Unchanged

`pollen-robotics/microduck-challenges` still returns 404, so the Arena reference policies entry still says the challenge repo isn't public.

## Checks

Tests 6/6 · `policies.json` regenerated and valid · revocations clean · `awesome-lint` clean · both new URLs 200.

items.title: PiCrawler: the sim-trained brain walks the robot; the MicroDuck port plan
items.body:
## Summary

The PiCrawler milestone branch. The sim-trained walking brain, P-e·h0, runs the real SunFounder PiCrawler from the dashboard and looks like the sim (ledger entry "MILESTONE", 2026-10-04). This PR brings the whole hardware campaign onto master, merges master back in so the branch carries the MicroDuck modules, and adds the plan for the next phase.

**The robot (pi_host)**
- `ogma_benchd` and `ogma_host`: the brain-input feed (servo forward model, IMU attitude on a 225 Hz thread, stride odometry, FSR feet, boom ToF), the actuation path, and a dashboard that runs a brain config after a countdown with stop, reset and end controls.
- Fail-safes measured on the bench: servos disarm on a HAT reset instead of driving to their stops; a HAT reset is confirmed before acting; a sustained low-voltage limp; the first command ramps from the pulse the HAT holds.
- Instruments: INA219 fast capture, the estimated 3.3 V rail, servo current, the mic, the scale probe and stall probe.

**The findings (ledger)**
- The "HAT resets" were mostly not current-triggered: the HAT's 3.3 V rail browns out, concrete resets ~13× more often than carpet. A dedicated servo supply (Mod D) is the planned fix.
- The servo: drives at ~0.22–0.25 N·m, holds ~0.5–0.6 N·m by gear friction, cuts its own drive after ~3.3 s of stall.
- The height homeostat is the long-horizon destabiliser on this body; P-e·h0 tips 0.25 times per 100k ticks against 8.4 for P-e.

**The sim (godot_host)**
- Honest inputs (`honest_joints/imu/upright/distress`), the measured body with FSR legs, the boom ToF, an asymmetric torque cap and a servo power model with a HUD power panel, all default off. The harness now applies a config's `body_env`.
- The picrawler menu is pruned to the three configs that run on the robot.

**The merge and the plan**
- origin/master merged in (three append-only conflicts), so this branch carries the MicroDuck modules.
- `docs/plans-and-designs/picrawler_microduck_port_plan.md`: the duck's level 2 (place map, play loop, avoidance priors, stuck detector, arbiter) on top of P-e·h0 unchanged, stages S0–S6, each gain-0-guarded.

## Gates run

- P-e·h0 and its two speed variants byte-identical on body JSON across the merge (seed 1, 6000 ticks, all three).
- cpp_core: 818/819 of the project's tests pass. The one failure, `RunTumbleNavV2.DirectionalBeliefInfersGoodDirection`, fails identically on master before this PR; it is pre-existing and not touched here.
- pi_host builds and tests pass on x86 (benchd, hw library); `ogma_host.cpp` syntax-checks against the merged headers.
- godot_host builds; the launcher loads. Python tests 7/7.

items.title: Add follow-me behavior demo (CPU MuJoCo, stock walking policy)
items.body:
## What this adds

A self-contained **behavior demo** in which the Microduck follows a moving leader's **actual walked path**, turning where the leader turned instead of cutting the corner.

It is a **behavior layer over a stock exported walking policy**: it only chooses the 3-DoF twist command `(vx, vy, wz)` written into the policy's existing command slots. No locomotion network is trained, fine-tuned, replaced, or filtered.

> **Scope:** this is a **CPU MuJoCo simulation demo, not production robot autonomy**. See [Limitations](#limitations) — I'd rather be explicit about that up front than have it read as more than it is.

Opening as a **draft**: I don't know whether a `scripts/behavior_demos/` area is something you want in this repo at all, and I'd rather check that before polishing further. Happy to relocate, reshape, or drop it.

## Use case

"Follow me" is the demo people ask a small legged robot for first, and it's a good stress test of the shipped walking policy: it needs sustained forward motion, two opposite corners, a stop, and a reverse — driven purely through the command interface the runtime already exposes.

The interesting part is *what* the robot follows. Selecting a command from the leader's **current pose** makes the robot turn from its own coordinates the moment the leader turns, cutting across the inside of the corner. Following a **queue of world-space footprints** makes it walk to the place the leader actually stood, so it arrives at the corner and turns there.

## Implementation

- **`FootstepTrail`** records the leader's accumulated path in world coordinates at 50 Hz and returns the interpolated point walked **0.65 m of path length** earlier. Because the gap is a *path length*, not a time delay, a corner stays in the queue — producing measured **5.44 s delayed turns**. A stopped leader freezes the queue.
- **True opposite turns.** The route uses conventional actor-relative directions: facing `+X`, the left turn adds `+90°` of world yaw and the later right turn subtracts `90°`, returning the leader to its original heading. An earlier iteration labelled a *negative*-yaw curve `LEFT TURN`, so the two turns were physically same-signed; a test now locks the signs.
- **Asymmetric measured controller.** The stock policy's turning authority is strongly asymmetric — a single mirrored command does not produce mirrored body motion. The controller closes the loop on the delayed footprint yaw using separately measured bands: left `wz = +0.60…+1.00`, right `wz = −0.18…−0.32`, `3°` deadband, `vx = +0.24` while turning. The policy has a sharp gait-onset threshold, so inside the deadband the command is exactly zero rather than a small nudge.
- **Reverse safety exception.** When the leader backs toward the follower, the duck backs away **immediately** instead of waiting for the leader's reverse footprint to arrive, so the leader cannot walk into it. This is the one deliberate departure from trail following, and it is why the queued-footprint error grows during the final reverse. Cornering and lateral motion still come exclusively from the recorded trail.
- **Isolated gaze.** Gaze and camera stabilization run entirely in a separate rendering `MjData` copied from the physical state each step. They never feed back into walking dynamics.
- **Sensor resolved by name.** The angular-velocity sensor is looked up by name (`imu_ang_vel` and aliases). Reading the last sensor by index silently picked up a different quantity during development and produced unstable, falsely-good results, so it's rejected explicitly.

### Scene asset resolution

`scene_follow_me.xml` includes the official `robot_walk.xml` (the collision model the walking policy was trained on) from outside the robot directory, so it restates `<compiler meshdir=...>` pointing back at the robot assets.

That tag **must stay after the `<include>`**: MuJoCo resolves `meshdir` against the top-level file and applies the *last* `<compiler>` it parses. Placing it before the include lets the robot's own `meshdir` win and the meshes fail to load. Since a stray compiler tag could also silently change joint units, a test compiles the demo scene and compares joint and control ranges against `scene_walk.xml` rather than merely asserting the file loads.

## Measured validation

A 44 s / 2,200-step rollout driven by the stock `alpha_walking` policy:

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Duration | 44.0 s / 2,200 control steps, all 7 phases |
| Duck turn yaw Δ | **+86.4° / −84.0°** (leader `+90.0° / −90.0°`) |
| Delayed turn starts | **5.44 s** after the leader, at the queued footprint (both turns) |
| Falls | **0** (`fallen_steps = 0`) |
| Trunk height | min **0.114 m**, final **0.116 m** |
| Leader visible in stabilized view | **2,200 / 2,200** steps |
| Leader range | mean 0.857 m (0.519–1.363 m) |

The turn signs are measured from the simulated trunk orientation, not inferred from phase labels or camera projection — that's what makes "the two turns are genuinely opposite" a measurement rather than an assertion.

`run_follow_me.py` writes all of these to the `--metrics` JSON so any run can be re-checked.

## Tests

`tests/test_follow_me_demo.py` adds **28 CPU tests** that need **no policy file, no GPU, and no renderer**:

```bash
uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_follow_me_demo.py
```

They cover the pure behavior logic (choreography phase order and continuity, opposite turn signs, trail lag and corner retention, queue freezing, yaw wrap-around, controller deadband/asymmetry/proportionality, the reverse exception) and model/path invariants (scene compiles and matches `scene_walk.xml`, required bodies and cameras exist, the leader never collides with the robot, the `STAND` keyframe matches the policy's `DEFAULT_POSE`, the gyro resolves by name, and `--policy` is mandatory).

I checked the tests actually have teeth by mutating the source and confirming they fail: flipping the left-turn sign, making the controller symmetric, removing the deadband, removing the reverse exception, zeroing the trail distance, turning the corner into a stationary pivot, replacing the yaw interpolation with a naive lerp, dropping the trail interpolation, and inverting the proportional gain are each caught.

Full suite on this branch: **182 passed, 1 skipped**.

## What is *not* included

- **No ONNX policy committed.** `--policy` is required and has no default.
- **No video or image files committed.**
- **No `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` changes** and no new dependencies. The demo uses `mujoco`, `numpy` and `onnxruntime` (already required); Pillow and imageio are needed only for the optional rendering path, which is skipped entirely under `--no-render`.
- **No changes to any existing file** — the PR is purely additive (7 new files).
- **No private or local paths**; the scene path resolves from `__file__`, so the demo runs from any working directory.

## Limitations

I want these read as part of the contribution, not buried:

- **The leader is a scripted semantic actor.** It follows a fixed choreography and its pose is read directly from the simulator. There is **no real person detector**, no tracking from images, and no perception of any kind.
- **Simulation only.** All numbers above are from MuJoCo. There is **no hardware validation**, and nothing here has been run on a real robot.
- **Gaze is isolated render state.** It exists to make the picture-in-picture watchable and never influences locomotion.
- **The policy is unmodified**, so its turning authority — including the left/right asymmetry compensated above — is a fixed constraint rather than something this PR improves.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/behavior_demos/follow_me/scene_follow_me.xml` | Official walking collision model + animated leader, footprint marker, camera rig |
| `scripts/behavior_demos/follow_me/follow_motion.py` | Leader route, world-space trail, asymmetric controller (no MuJoCo/ONNX imports, so it's unit-testable) |
| `scripts/behavior_demos/follow_me/camera_tracking.py` | Isolated gaze + geometric visibility |
| `scripts/behavior_demos/follow_me/video_overlay.py` | HUD, PiP, timeline (rendering only) |
| `scripts/behavior_demos/follow_me/run_follow_me.py` | ONNX rollout + metrics |
| `scripts/behavior_demos/follow_me/README.md` | Usage, design notes, limitations |
| `tests/test_follow_me_demo.py` | 28 CPU tests |

## Open questions

1. Is `scripts/behavior_demos/` welcome here, or would you prefer demos live elsewhere (or outside the repo entirely)?
2. Should the demo scene live next to the other scenes in `src/mjlab_microduck/robot/microduck/` instead? I kept it beside the demo to stay self-contained and avoid touching the robot directory, at the cost of the `meshdir` note above.
3. Happy to trim the HUD/video layer entirely if you'd rather keep the demo headless and dependency-light.

## Demo video

Fresh render from commit `131db5c` (44 s, 2,200 frames at 50 fps, 960×640). It shows the delayed world-space footprint target, both genuine opposite turns, the reverse safety exception, and the stabilized head-camera PiP.

Every new entry has every field filled, each with its evidence. Every entry is pinned to the repository's HEAD except `microduck_tutorial`, which is pinned to the last commit before HEAD deleted the robot module its task imports.

## Removed

- `booster`: its task's pull request is #54.

## Moved and re-scored

- **`h1mimic`** moves from 39th on `main` to 61st, from ease 1 to 0. Its checkpoint is a Git LFS pointer, and GitHub's LFS store does not serve the object. The media URL at the pinned commit returns 404 with an empty body; the same URL form serves `visionrl`'s LFS ONNX with 200. So it has no usable policy.
- **`g1_videodance`** is re-pinned from `155a02d` to `f27250e`. The author amended and force-pushed the release commit with an identical tree, and `155a02d` is on no branch now. The `v1.0-hrfest2026` tag points at `f27250e`.
- No other score changed. Every other entry keeps its relative order, and positions shift for the insertions and for `booster`'s removal.

## Stars refreshed

None crossed 50, 200 or 1,000:

| Entry | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `microduck_hd1910` | 57 (17 forks) | 62 (19 forks) |
| `parkour` | 89 | 91 |
| `teleopit` | 196 | 197 |
| `vibe` | 58 | 59 |
| `microduck_challenges` | 6 forks | 10 forks |

Two pinned commits are no longer their repository's HEAD. Both entries stay pinned where they were reviewed:
- **`microduck_hd1910`** (HEAD `692278a`): only duplicate ONNX copies were deleted. The six ported policies are unchanged at HEAD, and the roller and right-kick policies are left out anyway.
- **`parkour`** (HEAD `dfe09f4`): the low-step teacher's `.pt` was replaced.

## Judgment calls

- **Robot or task types the playground lacks, for the tie-break:**
  - Counted as new: the tennis serve (`adapt`), Go1 and the LEAP hand (`qoed`), Go2 (`visionrl`, `tp2`), footstep tracking (`gloria`) and loco-manipulation (`orcs`).
  - Not new: the G1 walking or tracking of `prism`, `rugiar`, `mimicx`, `kungfuathlete` and `cmoe`, and the Microduck's walks and races.
- **`mimicx`'s five box scenes at ease 2, not 3.** Upstream builds those scenes only inside its release runner, under one fixed id per process. The port therefore has to register its own id per scene, which part A counts as 2.
- **`visionrl` at 3.** The ONNX's run does not record which of two configs trained it, Flat or Rough-Blind. Both have the same 48-input actor and differ only in terrain, so the flat scene fits either.
- **`microduck_tutorial`'s policy is its own.** Its `walk.onnx` blob appears in none of the 4,173 commits of pollen-robotics/microduck and microduck_rl. The README's main path flashes a prebuilt Raspberry Pi image from a release. The scout did not download or open it, and the port needs nothing from it.
- **The search covered `mjlab in:readme`** sorted by recently updated, as the last run's did. Six of today's seven first-round candidates came only from there; this run's part E proposes adding it to step 1.

## Looked at and left out

**A checkpoint that fails a check:**
- HazinTihoa/athlete-humanoid-tennis (1): its policy needs an unpublished dataset, its own `PhaseAccelerationActionCfg` and a step wrapper that launches the ball.
- GIAR's dance policy: byte for byte Unitree's, which unitreerl already runs.
- 66Leslie/booster-mjlab (12): no published policy.

**Not mjlab tasks, or mjlab only as a backend:**
- Axellwppr/motion_tracking (406), btx0424/active-adaptation (162) and EGalahad/mimic-lite: Active Adaptation.
- Mondo-Robotics/PMT (307): Isaac Lab.
- zhutengjie/CLOT (65): HumanoidVerse.
- LeCAR-Lab/BFM-Zero (812): Isaac Lab and HumanoidVerse.
- omarrayyann/FetchMan: no mjlab.
- hitchopen/HOPE (47): Isaac Lab.
- About 15 more smaller repositories.

**No published policy:**
- SUZ-tsinghua/smp (276): diffusion priors only.
- LuwuDynamics/xgoduck_rl (64) and xgoduck_runtime_arduino (85): their own XgoDuck on BAM, with no data-only precedent here.
- About 20 repositories pushed since the last scout.

**Re-checked, unchanged since 2026-10-13:** InstinctMJ, mpc-rl, mjlab_playground, pal_mjlab, anymal_c_velocity, BDX-R, mjlab_manipulation, mjlab_hand, mjlab_microban, Go2_ARX, UniLab, dive-into-embodied-ai, fanhao375/microduck-replica (still "no walking policy validated") and php_parkour.

**Not opened, flagged:**
- minheinchay/g1_spinkick_example: a zip in a random-word folder.
- Four 0-star copies of awesome-microduck.
- yilv1982/duck-robot: pushes `.exe` files.
- Trainnr-AI/trainnr: pushes installers.
- RaphaelGrj/microduck-project: an `.apk`.

## What this session could not reach

A person would have to lift these limits:
- **Hosts WebFetch could not resolve** (`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`): `arxiv.org`, `hn.algolia.com`, `news.ycombinator.com`, `mujocolab.github.io`, `wandb.ai`, `www.kaggle.com` and `www.youwei-yu.com`.
- **Reddit:** WebFetch refuses it.
- **GitHub's API:** `api.github.com` answers 403 through WebFetch, and `gh api` refuses repositories outside the session.
- **Git LFS for unattached repositories:** the git proxy refuses it (`access denied by the git proxy: ... is not in this session's authorized repository set`). GitHub's media URLs worked instead.
- **emwstudio/DuckEMW's submodules:** `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled`.

## Review

There is no code to review here: the PR changes data alone (`net: 0`). `/simplify-comments` over the whole diff changed nothing, since the file's header comment is untouched and the entries are data.

items.title: 支持 Dynamixel 2.0 FAST_SYNC_READ (0x8A)
items.body:
你好，感谢开源这个项目。
想提一个和当前 Pollen 官方 microduck 主线兼容性有关的功能请求：为 imu_to_dxl 固件增加 Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 的 FAST_SYNC_READ (0x8A) 支持。
背景：
- 当前官方 microduck 的总线实现默认启用 Fast Sync Read，普通 sync_read 会走 0x8A：
  - [https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/duck-control/src/bus.rs](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/duck-control/src/bus.rs?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
  - [https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/docs/design/robotd-design.md](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/docs/design/robotd-design.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- 官方默认配置里 bus.fast_sync_read 为 true；若某个设备不支持 0x8A，整组读取会超时。
- 本项目当前已经实现普通 SYNC_READ (0x82)，并且 ID=200 / addr=124 / len=12 的 DXL 数据布局与官方要求是对齐的，但目前 board.h / dxl2.c 中还没有看到 0x8A 的处理。
希望可以考虑：
1. 增加 DXL_INST_FAST_SYNC_READ = 0x8A。
2. 按 Dynamixel 2.0 Fast Sync Read 规范处理 ID 列表、设备顺序和聚合响应。
3. 保持现有 IMU 数据映射：ID 200、地址 124、长度 12。
4. 如果方便，增加一个和当前官方 robotd / rustypot 对拍的测试，最好能验证 IMU 与 XL330 同总线时的 0x8A 读取。
这项支持对 XL330 原版路线会很有价值，可以避免为了兼容 IMU 而在 robotd.toml 中关闭 fast_sync_read。

items.title: [Newton] Add BAM servo actuator and MicroDuck walking tasks
items.body:
# Description

Adds a Newton-native [BAM](https://github.com/Rhoban/bam) servo actuator, Pollen Robotics' MicroDuck built on it (with gearbox-backlash variants), and MicroDuck flat and rough velocity walking tasks. This combines the former stack #8161, #8265, #8266 and #8267, which are closed in favor of this PR.

### BAM servo actuator (`isaaclab`, `isaaclab_newton`)

BAM is an identified voltage-domain model of small smart servos (firmware P loop, PWM, DC motor, supply sag, command delay, load-dependent gearbox friction) for sim-to-real on low-cost legged robots.

- `BamActuatorCfg` / `BamMotorCfg` (core) configure the fit and deployment settings; authoring writes `NewtonBamDriveAPI` actuator prims.
- `isaaclab_newton.actuators.DriveBam` is a Newton `DriveBase` running Warp kernels each physics step; CUDA-graph safe, per-environment delay streams and supply.
- `MjWarpActuatorBridge` publishes the friction budget into MJWarp `dof_frictionloss` and reads the previous solve's external load. BAM requires Newton + MJWarp + `use_newton_actuators=True`; other backends and solvers, including CPU MuJoCo, raise.
- `NewtonManager.register_pre_actuator_callback` / `register_solver_init_callback` hooks for solver-coupled drives. Hard resets discard pre-actuator hooks with the other per-model hooks, and BAM binds again on the new model.
- **Backlash:** `BamActuatorCfg.backlash_joint_template` names each servo's passive play hinge (e.g. `"passive_{}_backlash"`). The firmware then measures servo angle plus play angle; motor velocity, friction, and applied torque stay on the servo joint. Authoring writes `newton:hasBacklash` on every BAM prim (1 when the template is set, 0 otherwise) so backlash and regular drives never merge, and the MJWarp binding resolves each hinge per world before graph capture; missing or non-revolute pairs raise.
- Each Newton BAM drive takes the start-up settings of the groups it drives, so groups in separate drives (e.g. different `max_delay`) can use their own supply ranges and backlash; groups that share a drive must agree. A supply sagged to 0 V applies no voltage, leaving only back-EMF braking.
- **Deprecated:** Newton-native actuators follow the Newton 1.6 drive API, so `read_group_parameter` / `write_group_parameter` address the component as `"drive"`. `"controller"` still resolves to the drive and emits a `DeprecationWarning`; it is scheduled for removal in 3.2.

- Native actuator authoring reactivates a replaced `NewtonActuator` prim whose path matches one it deactivated; before, the joint silently kept no actuator. This applies to every Newton-native actuator config, not only BAM.

Core keeps only the config and USD authoring; all Newton/MJWarp code lives in `isaaclab_newton`. The backend check in authoring uses `FactoryBase._get_backend()`, as `base_visualizer.py` does, since `SimulationContext.backend` reports the tensor backend.

### MicroDuck asset (`isaaclab_assets`)

- `MICRODUCK_CFG`, `MICRODUCK_ALLCOLLISIONS_CFG`, `MICRODUCK_ROLLERS_CFG` with Dynamixel XL330 BAM servos: the `m6` fit from Rhoban BAM `62bd8ce`, firmware gain, nominal and sampled supply voltage, supply sag, and a 3–6-step command delay, shared by all variants.
- `MICRODUCK_BACKLASH_CFG`, `MICRODUCK_ALLCOLLISIONS_BACKLASH_CFG`, `MICRODUCK_ROLLERS_BACKLASH_CFG` use `replace(..., backlash_joint_template=...)` with the `*_backlash.usd` assets (14 ±1° play hinges; 28/28/32 joints). Inserting the play links removed the all-collisions variant's implicit shin–sole exclusions; the USD now authors those two pairs explicitly.
- Variants are `clone` + USD path overrides, like the Unitree H1 variants. The roller variant leaves its four wheel joints passive and starts 2 cm higher to clear them.
- USDs load from `ISAACLAB_NUCLEUS_DIR/Robots/PollenRobotics/MicroDuck/` (with `ATTRIBUTION.txt` and `LICENSE`).
- `MICRODUCK_JOINT_NAMES` lists the 14 servos in the robot's servo order (left leg, neck and head, right leg), with leg and head subsets; every USD lists the right leg first, so tasks select them with `preserve_order=True`.
- `test_valid_configs.py`: articulations with BAM actuators spawn on Newton MJWarp through a one-environment clone plan, since BAM runs on no other backend. Other assets are unchanged.

### Walking tasks (`isaaclab_tasks`)

`IsaacContrib-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck` and `IsaacContrib-Velocity-Rough-MicroDuck`, ported from [microduck_rl](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl) through the original Lab MicroDuck task. Both keep its 14-joint action order, 61-value actor and 76-value critic inputs, 50 Hz control, rewards, command sampling, randomization, curricula, and PPO settings, so existing checkpoints load.

- Encoder bias is owned by the biased joint-position action term and IMU misalignment by its startup event term; observations read them from there.
- Joint velocity uses the core one-step `delay_min_lag`/`delay_max_lag`; `delayed_observation` only provides the IMU lag redrawn on a fixed 64-step period.
- Curricula use `modify_term_cfg` with one `staged_value` schedule; stages switch at `>=` their step (the old task used `>` for some, a one-step difference).
- Reuses core terms where they match (`body_projected_gravity_b`, `randomize_rigid_body_*`, `randomize_joint_parameters`, `push_by_setting_velocity`, `joint_pos_limits`, `action_rate_l2`, `bad_orientation`, `UniformVelocityCommand`). Task-local rewards keep upstream's formulas, which differ from the nearest core terms: tracking combines planar and off-axis error in one kernel, `body_ang_vel_xy_l2` uses the world-frame trunk rate, `foot_slip` squares contact speed, and `self_collision_cost` reads the filtered force matrix.
- MJWarp uses 100 solver iterations and 50 line-search iterations instead of microduck_rl's 10 and 20; the original budgets were exhausted with the current solver.
- Critic foot observations, rewards and a termination guard against non-finite MJWarp states, which microduck_rl's rough velocity task hit under heavy contact. Rewards run before resets, so the reward terms stay finite on the step a diverged environment is terminated.
- **Rough terrain:** [microduck_rl's gentle mix](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl/blob/8d0db74916a4f833d1d9b95d6a1d7f4d13b9d5ec/src/mjlab_microduck/tasks/microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py) (25% flat, 25% stairs ≤1.5 cm, 30% random grid ≤1 cm, 20% slopes 0.03–0.10) with the existing distance-based terrain curriculum. It is a new mix rather than `ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG` because the steps are centimeter-scale. The actor stays blind; two downward rays per foot give the critic and foot rewards the ground height, handling missed rays and step undersides.
- Lab builds triangle-mesh terrain instead of mjlab's boxes, so a task-local `TerrainImporter` subclass authors upstream's softer MuJoCo contact (`solref=(0.04, 1.0)`) on the terrain mesh; `TerrainImporterCfg` has no collision-property field yet. The rough task uses 200 contacts and 1024 constraint rows per environment.
- **Backlash preset:** `presets=backlash` switches either task to the backlash robot and, together, the output-side encoder observations, head-pose rewards, a servo-only joint-limit penalty, and a separate experiment name. One `_backlash_preset` helper builds each pair, so no backlash task IDs, environment subclasses, or runner subclasses are added.
- The environment-browser preview is committed under `environment-previews/`, following develop's convention for ground-plane tasks; the rough row reuses the flat still until a rough-terrain capture exists. Both rows list the `backlash` preset.

### Newton model updates (`isaaclab_newton`)

- Batches pending model-change flags into one solver notification before stepping. MicroDuck queues armature (`JOINT_DOF_PROPERTIES`) and CoM (`BODY_INERTIAL_PROPERTIES`) changes on every reset, and `SolverMuJoCo` reruns `set_const_0` and the solref update for each flag, so one combined notification halves that work.

  | Flat MicroDuck, 4096 envs, idle RTX 5090 | Per-flag notify (develop) | Batched |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Env step, median | 20.8 ms | 15.9 ms |
  | Model-change notification per env step | 10.2 ms | 5.4 ms |

  Median of 8 alternating rounds of 100 env steps after 100 warmup steps, in one process; every round showed a 4.6–5.0 ms gap. About 100 environments reset per env step, so notification runs on nearly every step. The resulting model matches the per-flag path to float32 roundoff.

## Type of change

- New feature
- Deprecation (`"controller"` → `"drive"` group-parameter component)

## Validation

Run on an RTX 5090 with the branch merged into `develop` at `2224495d` (Isaac Sim 6.2, Newton `5ea82eef`, MuJoCo Warp 3.14), in a `uv sync --locked --extra isaacsim --extra test --extra skrl --extra all --extra teleop` environment. BAM fixtures (`ISAACLAB_NUCLEUS_DIR/Tests/BAM/`: two USDs, upstream BAM `62bd8ce` goldens, recorded pendulum trajectory) and the MicroDuck USDs loaded from the default public asset root.

- `test_bam_actuator.py` — 32 passed (goldens: motor, friction, supply sag, mjlab delay replay; authoring; reset/RNG/graph replay; play-angle feedback with non-zero rotor velocity; unbound play hinge; supply exhausted to 0 V).
- `test_bam_actuator_mjwarp.py` — 14 passed (live MJWarp pendulum vs recorded trajectory, decimation 1/2; multi-articulation merge, re-bound after hard resets without accumulating hooks; per-group settings on separate and shared drives; solver and CPU MuJoCo rejection; missing play hinge). Without the hard-reset fix the hook check fails (pre-actuator hooks 1 → 2).
- `test_newton_adapter.py` — 17 passed; `test_actuator_collection.py` — 30 passed (including the `"controller"` deprecation warning at the caller's line); `test_newton_actuators_newton.py` (Isaac Sim) — 37 passed.
- `test_microduck.py` — 7 passed: all six variants spawn and step (14 servos, passive joints undriven), and the backlash test sets a distinct play angle per joint and environment and checks the analytic servo effort.
- `test_valid_configs.py` (Isaac Sim) — passed; BAM entities, including all six MicroDuck variants, spawn on Newton MJWarp.
- `test_microduck_velocity.py` — 4 passed:
  - deployed interface (61/76 inputs, policy term order, action joint order), per-reset BAM friction, 20 finite default-preset steps, and a NaN-injected environment that terminates alone with finite rewards and observations (flat);
  - foot height from ray hits, including misses, step undersides, and world elevation (synthetic);
  - rough terrain: contact parameters authored on the terrain mesh, finite foot rays at tile height, and foot heights;
  - `presets=backlash`: distinct play angles per joint and environment reach the policy and critic encoders and head rewards, play stops incur no limit penalty, 20 steps stay finite, and play joints stay undriven.
- `test_contrib_environments_kitless.py -k MicroDuck` — passed; it samples one task per family and steps `IsaacContrib-Velocity-Rough-MicroDuck` with the default preset.
- `test_newton_manager_abstraction.py` — 114 passed (combined notifications, CUDA graph capture/recapture); `test_articulation.py -k hard_reset` — passed.
- `tools/update_environments_rst.py --check` — up to date; `tools/changelog/cli.py check` — passed; `make -C docs current-docs` with warnings treated as errors — passed; pre-commit hooks — passed.
- Before the rebase: flat and rough, with and without `presets=backlash`, 30 random-action steps stayed finite (14 or 28 joints; experiment names `microduck_velocity_{flat,rough}[_backlash]`; solver iterations 10/100), and regression tests (shared per-environment delay, torque feedback with sag, zero-Coulomb seeding, damping resync, configuration replacing existing USD values, play-angle read) failed without their fixes. Supplied `velocity_flat.onnx` (original Lab checkpoint, iteration 49,999) on the flat task, 32 envs × 1,000 control steps:

| Playback condition | Falls | Timeouts | Mean planar velocity error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed 0.15 m/s forward, play mode | 0 | 32 | 0.136 m/s |
| Training commands, corruption and disturbances | 0 | 32 | 0.185 m/s |

  This shows the existing policy runs stably, not exact parity with the old dynamics.

## Known limitations

- `DriveBam` registers the `NewtonBamDriveAPI` token when `isaaclab_newton` loads Newton articulations, so USD files with pre-authored BAM prims cannot be parsed on PhysX/OVPhysX.
- `applied_effort` reports motor torque; solver friction is read from `drive.friction_budget`.
- Groups and robots that Newton merges into one drive share its supply and delay per environment, and must agree on start-up ranges, `stiff_frictionloss`, and `backlash_joint_template`.

## Not in this PR

- MicroDuck fall-recovery task.
- Golden regeneration tooling; provenance (BAM commit, mjlab version, settings) is stored in the NPZ metadata.

## Follow-ups

- Add collision properties to `TerrainImporterCfg` and drop the task-local importer.
- Replace `delayed_observation` with core `ObservationTermCfg.delay_*`. Kept for parity: the IMU lag is redrawn on a fixed 64-step period with a per-environment phase, whereas core redraws with a per-sample hold probability.
- Find the source of the occasional non-finite MJWarp states and drop the observation guards; reset-time CoM randomization on Newton is a candidate.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution guidelines and ran `uv run isaaclab -f`
- [x] Added tests that fail without the change
- [x] Updated docs (`concepts/actuators.rst` with a MicroDuck example, API reference, 3.0 migration guide)
- [x] Added changelog fragments (`isaaclab`, `isaaclab_newton`, `isaaclab_assets`, `isaaclab_tasks`; `.skip` for test-only `isaaclab_physx` / `isaaclab_ov`)

items.title: Add a Hermes Agent duck client, a hopscotch game and a servo rework
items.body:
Sweep of 2026-10-04 → 2026-10-06. **217 → 220 entries.**

## Added

| Section | Entry | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Agent Tools | [microduck-lab (Hermes Agent)](https://github.com/notwitcheer/microduck-lab) | A client that lets a Hermes Agent drive the duck from plain sentences by sending **intents only** to `robotd`, never the servo bus. It refuses speeds outside the policy's trained range because, per its wire-contract notes (every command cited to a file and line), `robotd` doesn't clamp them. Also: tools that score takes from logged trunk height and gravity rather than from watching frames, and **six patches to the rough-terrain training** correcting how height and terrain difficulty are measured. Apache-2.0, sim-only |
| Apps | [Rayuela](https://github.com/Bravo-Robots/microduck_rl-rayuela) | Hopscotch: the duck kicks a ball onto a board, a camera rectified to top-down finds the square, the duck walks or rolls there. ROS 2 Humble over the official policies with the BAM model. Workshop project, Spanish install notes. Apache-2.0, sim-only |
| Hardware | [Dukki](https://github.com/lachlanhurst/dukki) | Rework around **Unitree J288 servos** (~3× faster; bench-measured 0.45 N·m peak vs the XL330's 0.43) and a Radxa CM4. KiCad boards, STM32 bridge firmware, one servo bench-characterised, software changes on branches of forks. Records a fix for a head-IMU bug its author says affects Pollen's robots too (a temperature below 23° reads near 280°). **Its latest commit says it is nowhere near complete**, and the entry says so. MIT |

The rough-terrain patches matter beyond this entry: an earlier `witcheer` policy card noted the stock terrain curriculum stayed on the easiest tier all run, and these patches target how that difficulty is measured.

## Held back (not rejected)

- **`zhuoligetu123/microduck-hd1910m`** (26★): a Radxa ZERO 3W + 15 HD1910M build with wiring, servo IDs, four-skill adaptation, a Rust backend and an APK. Its own `THIRD_PARTY.md` says the four ONNX files it bundles come from `xgoduck_runtime_arduino`, which has **no LICENSE**, and that *"public redistribution and commercial authorisation need separate confirmation"*. The repo itself has no licence, and its validated demos are simulation, as it says. It's the same chain as the held **XGO-Duck** (still no top-level licence, now 502★). Both should be revisited once the terms are written down
- **AIcrowd challenge CLI**: `aicrowd-microduck` still isn't on PyPI and the challenge page still can't be checked
- **`guang384` side-roll policies**: no measured results on the cards

## Skipped

`luoyanfeidao/microduck_android` (a second Android port, no licence), `barlowski/umcp-it-microduck-farm` (a one-page pitch for a game concept), `xiongy26/unitree-g1-race` (six robots, Microduck is one), and empty or undescribed repos.

## Checks

Tests 6/6 · `policies.json` regenerated and valid · revocations clean · `awesome-lint` clean · all 3 new URLs 200.

items.title: MicroDuck agentic: onboard-only loop (own camera/ToF/IMU, cuVSLAM, YOLOE) + skating
items.body:
## MicroDuck agentic demos, onboard-only: honest loop + skating

Stacked on #328. Rule from the 2026-10-13 review: **no cheating**. The robot and its agent may use only what a real
MicroDuck has. All runs in #328 and all earlier skating runs on this branch used the simulator pose, a ground-truth
detector stand-in and loops closed on truth, so they are relabelled **privileged-state prototypes**. This PR adds the
loop that replaces them.

### What the robot has (`--honest`)
| | |
|---|---|
| Head camera | OVRTX render, 640x360 at 15 Hz, jaw_soft lens (82.3 deg HFOV). Rendered from the live Newton body poses in a sensor process, so robots see each other. |
| ToF | VL53L8CX 8x8 model: the gtceu model on the walker, the same zone model on rendered depth on the skate robot (96 % status agreement with gtceu). |
| IMU | Trunk IMU model: delta-angle gyro and accelerometer, with noise and bias. |
| Encoders | Joint angles, used only through forward kinematics. |
| Localization | Own estimate in its start frame, or from an operator start pose on a shared map for multi-robot runs: AHRS heading (gyro on SO(3) + accelerometer tilt; residual gyro bias after the standard at-boot calibration). Translation: leg odometry from encoder FK (walker), floor-flow visual odometry (skates: LK on floor corners, back-projected onto the floor plane with the estimated camera pose), and cuVSLAM 17 RGBD increments (gated; the skaters' fallback). It drifts. |
| Detector | YOLOE-11s prompt-free (Cascade model) on the head image, ranged by the ToF zone or the ground plane. Labels on synthetic props can be odd and are shown as is. |
| Map / memory | Per-robot ToF occupancy map built on its own estimate, plus its own memory. |

`HonestWorld` is a closed proxy: the agent tools reach only the estimate, the robot's own sensors and its own
commands. The skate policy's heading error is computed from the estimated heading.

Simulator truth is used only offline: the verifier, the clearance check, and the localization error printed on the
end card (and the grey trace in the review video, never shown to the robot). Still scripted, on the estimate: the
waypoint/steering loop, brake-to-halt, and the ToF guards. `depth_navigation_v4` is not used, because it needs a depth
camera the robot lacks.

### Skating
- **Robot:** skate-wheel MicroDuck variant `microduck_rollers.usd` (sha256 `cd117510…`). It is the canonical robot plus
  passive wheels under the feet.
- **Policies:** learned `natural_roller` (plaza) and `oval_roller` (race), unchanged, in ONE shared Newton world;
  skaters can collide.
- **No get-up on skates:** a fall ends the run.
- **Scenes:** `skate_plaza` (traffic cones A/B/C, bench, planter, stop mark) and `skate_race` (3-lane oval).

### Measured so far (every attempt listed; `docs/evidence/microduck-honest-20261013/`)
#### Summary
| scenario | attempts | passed | typical failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| backstage (walker) | 7 | 0 | Reaches the pad (0.14-0.17 m in 4 runs) but grazes the cable reel on the way. bsH7 kept 0.073 m from the reel (radial), yet the box-based check still flags it. |
| multi-room fetch (3 walkers) | 1 (3 robots) | 2 of 3 robots | duck_a stopped 0.412 m from the red box (limit 0.4). |
| skate plaza | 8 | 0 | Cone B is never seen: the agent always swerves left of the bench. Early runs also had camera-odometry drift up to 3.7 m. |
| skate race (3 skaters, shared world) | 3 (9 skaters) | 1 skater | skateraceH3/duck_a: one lap in 25.3 s, 5 % off-track. The others: falls (no get-up on skates), off-track, out of steps. |

#### Localization measured (offline, vs truth)
- **Walker:** 0.24-0.55 m over 5-15 m.
- **Skates, cuVSLAM only:** 1.2-3.7 m over ~9 m.
- **Skates, floor flow:** 0.35-0.49 m final (0.7-1.1 m peak) over 10-12 m.

<details><summary>All 27 robot-runs</summary>

| run | scenario | result | detail | own localization error final / max (path) | agent claimed | LLM calls | stack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bsH1 | backstage_obstacles | FAIL | goal 0.323 m (<= 0.35); possible contact with LowCase | 0.55 / 0.63 m (9.25 m) | failure | 30 | v1: scalar gyro heading, leg odometry, cuVSLAM with ToF-zone depth |
| bsH2 | backstage_obstacles | FAIL | goal 0.745 m (<= 0.35); possible contact with LowCase | 0.32 / 0.329 m (14.9 m) | failure | 41 | v2: + floor-plane depth for cuVSLAM, leg-odometry scale 1.19, contact-FK height, set dressing |

| bsH4 | backstage_obstacles | FAIL | goal 0.14 m (<= 0.35); possible contact with CableReel | 0.314 / 0.333 m (5.43 m) | failure | 17 | v3 (repeat of bsH3) |
| bsH5 | backstage_obstacles | FAIL | goal 1.594 m (<= 0.35) | 0.25 / 0.253 m (4.57 m) | failure | 20 | v4: walker honest prompt updated (drift numbers, side-blind ToF, inflation 0.20-0.25 m advice) |

| skateH6 | skate_plaza | FAIL | cones A:0.246 B:1.35(miss) C:0.345; stop 1.873 m | 3.729 / 3.768 m (8.79 m) | failure | 41 | v5 (repeat of skateH5) |
| skateH7 | skate_plaza | FAIL | cones A:0.335 B:1.187(miss) C:0.534(miss); stop 1.656 m | 2.386 / 2.386 m (9.9 m) | failure | 41 | v6: + 'bring the expected target into the 82 deg view before detecting; pass furniture on the side toward the next target' (H5, H6 missed B) |
| skateH8 | skate_plaza | FAIL | cones A:0.204 B:1.216(miss) C:0.554(miss); stop 0.187 m | 0.352 / 1.102 m (10.44 m) | failure | 40 | v7: + floor-flow visual odometry on skates (cuVSLAM fallback) |
| skateraceH1/duck_a | skate_race | FAIL | laps 0.269, off-track 0.551 | 2.207 / 2.343 m (5.61 m) | failure | 63 | v6 + operator track map and start pose; skate_lane on the estimate |
| skateraceH1/duck_b | skate_race | FAIL | laps 0.762, off-track 0.0 | 1.222 / 1.222 m (10.35 m) | failure | 63 | v6 + operator track map and start pose; skate_lane on the estimate |
| skateraceH1/duck_c | skate_race | FAIL | laps 0.105, off-track 0.848; possible contact with BoardS; FELL | 0.382 / 1.279 m (2.44 m) | failure | 63 | v6 + operator track map and start pose; skate_lane on the estimate |
| skateraceH2/duck_a | skate_race | FAIL | laps 0.808, off-track 0.253 | 0.879 / 1.437 m (9.33 m) | failure | 63 | v7: + floor-flow odometry (skateraceH1 ran the VO-only v6 stack) |
| skateraceH2/duck_b | skate_race | FAIL | laps 0.424, off-track 0.42 | 1.727 / 1.756 m (6.55 m) | failure | 63 | v7: + floor-flow odometry (skateraceH1 ran the VO-only v6 stack) |
| skateraceH2/duck_c | skate_race | FAIL | laps 0.137, off-track 0.54; possible contact with BoardE10 | 2.268 / 2.268 m (5.93 m) | failure | 63 | v7: + floor-flow odometry (skateraceH1 ran the VO-only v6 stack) |
| skateraceH3/duck_a | skate_race | PASS | laps 1.043, off-track 0.054, time 25.28 s | 0.491 / 0.697 m (11.94 m) | success | 47 | v8: + calibrated-IMU residual gyro bias, 30-step budget |
| skateraceH3/duck_b | skate_race | FAIL | laps 0.695, off-track 0.194 | 1.744 / 2.195 m (10.86 m) | failure | 47 | v8: + calibrated-IMU residual gyro bias, 30-step budget |
| skateraceH3/duck_c | skate_race | FAIL | laps 0.186, off-track 0.0; FELL | 0.43 / 0.667 m (3.04 m) | failure | 47 | v8: + calibrated-IMU residual gyro bias, 30-step budget |

</details>

### What breaks (honest)
- **Camera odometry on skates (fixed in part by floor flow).** Without wheel encoders, cuVSLAM is the only source of translation. Errors seen:
  1.2 m (skateH2) and 2.2 m (skateH3) over ~6.7 m. After the AHRS and velocity carry-over: 0.31 m final but 1.3 m
  peak over 8.4 m (skateH5). Offline replays of the same recording vary by ±0.3 m (cuVSLAM is not deterministic
  here), and gated rejections cluster when the bench or planter fills the view.
- **Heading on skates.** Integrating only the vertical gyro component drifted ~20 % in carves (coning under push
  sway). Fixed with an SO(3) AHRS and a delta-angle gyro model: < 2 deg over 26 s.
- **ToF false obstacles.** The centre-ray floor test made grazing floor zones into obstacles: phantom brakes, the
  skater stalled (skateH1). Fixed by testing the zone's full 5.6 deg extent.
- **The agent.** It gives up early when unsure (skateH4 called task_done after 6 calls). It never sees a cone outside
  its 82 deg view, so it went left round the bench and missed cone B (skateH5). It lets speed build up to
  0.55-0.77 m/s at throttle 0.25-0.3 on legs without a stop. On the walker it stepped on/against equipment (bsH1,
  bsH3) and once ran out of steps (bsH2).
- **Detector.** YOLOE prompt-free names synthetic props oddly ("white stab" for tape, "pulpit" for a flight case).
  Traffic cones are recognised once they look like traffic cones; the first plaza had yellow-looking cylinders.
- **Walker blind sides.** The ToF sees only ahead, so with 0.2-0.4 m of drift the walker grazed the cable reel in
  bsH3, bsH4 and bsH6. A map guard on the robot's own ToF map was added (bsH7: 0.073 m radial gap, still flagged by
  the box-based check).
- **Skaters fall:** there is no get-up policy on skates (skateraceH1 duck_c after hitting the boards, skateraceH3
  duck_c).
- **Not done yet:** honest stage_edge, the hard skating pack and skate_dropin.

### Videos
Each video is OVRTX 1080p and shows:
- the follow view (illustrative only);
- the robot's own head camera with its detections;
- its own ToF;
- its own estimate vs truth (grey, evaluation only);
- its own map;
- the agent panel and an end card with the offline check.

items.title: Robot-first tracking (phase A of #36)
items.body:
This implements phase A of the recommendation in #36 (`docs/research/tracking.md`, "Order of work" steps 1 to 3). It stays with SLAM, as the owner asked, and makes the robot the tracker: vision corrects it. One commit per step, plus one for the measurement hooks. **Do not merge until it has been tested on the GPU PC.**

## Commits

1. **Stream the Microduck's camera motion at 50 Hz, stamped at the source.**
   - The driver subscribes to `robot.state` at the loop rate and stamps every sample with robotd's `t_ns`. That is the same CLOCK_MONOTONIC the driver's `perf_counter` reads, so the existing link offset applies unchanged. A driver running somewhere else falls back to a min-arrival offset.
   - New wire v3 messages: batched `Motion`/`MotionSample` (camera-to-world in the odometry frame, camera-frame angular velocity, state) on the frames lane. A dropped batch is resent with the next one.
   - `RobotDescription.motion_noise`: 1.32° p95 and 1.77 cm/m from #33 (sigma about p95/2), loosened 10× while the robot is held or fallen.
   - `Camera.capture_delay`: the driver's frame-delay estimate, 90 ms for Microduck.
   - `--head-imu` turns the camera by the head IMU's gyro on hardware. The sim has no head IMU, so it uses FK.
   - Frame metadata keeps today's receive-stamped 20 Hz pose, so the old path stays comparable.
   - `slam_drive --record` writes `motion.jsonl` on both clocks.
2. **Track the camera robot-first.**
   - New modules: `motion.py` (MotionBuffer plus a non-blocking shared-memory ring), `fusion.py` (PoseGraph), `tracking.py` (Frontend/VisualResult) and `mast3r_frontend.py`.
   - PoseGraph: 12 keyframes plus the current frame. Factors: robot relative pose, gravity, a weak anchor, and visual factors weighted by match fraction with a Cauchy loss. Variables also include the frame delay td and a log-scale. Solved with scipy `least_squares` on a sparse Jacobian.
   - The MASt3R front end seeds every solve at the fused prediction and adds that prediction as a prior inside the vendored `FrameTracker.solve` normal equations. `ito.build` applies this adaptation and checks it; the bundle moves to **v4, so rebuild `models/`**.
   - Fused keyframe poses and scale are written back into MASt3R.
   - **No map restarts.** A frame that matches too little becomes a keyframe at the fused pose, and the pilot's view keeps moving.
   - The old path is now `slam_vision.py`, selected with the per-robot setting `tracking=vision` (`--tracking vision`) for A/B on the same build.
   - Pilot comfort: the eye is the robot's newest 50 Hz pose times fusion's correction. The renderer eases changes in: the world turns back at most 2°/s and the eye slides at most 5 cm/s, only while the view moves (`e2e/correction_ease.py`).
3. **Online frame-delay estimate and blur gate.**
   - td is estimated on each keyframe solve, bounded to capture_delay −0.1/+0.2 s.
   - A frame is gated when |ω| × 10 ms × fx > 8 px. It still gets a pose from the graph but adds no visual factor and no splats.
4. **Measurement hooks.**
   - `microduck-sim --truth FILE` writes each rendered frame's true pose plus a thumbnail. `--blur N` adds synthetic motion blur for drive (f).
   - `slam_drive` gets `--route sweep --turn-rate`, `--reconstruction video` (records with no CUDA) and writes `robot.json`.
   - `slam_replay --pose L1..L5 --truth FILE` reports rotation p50/p95/max, translation after a fixed first-frame alignment, usable fraction, restarts, eye correction rate and frame-to-pose latency.
   - `--poses-only` runs L2/L3/L4 without MASt3R.

## Verified here (CPU, no GPU)

- **Real Pollen stack in the sandbox** (robotd, mediad and the MuJoCo body): Motion arrives at 50.0 Hz, 3 ms after its source. robotd's `t_ns` shares the driver's clock (`motion_clock: robot t_ns`).
- **How the sim had to be set up:** HuggingFace is blocked here, so I had no walking policies. I welded the trunk and used a stand-in ONNX policy that passes robotd's head command straight to the head joints. That rig only exercises drive (a), standing head sweeps; walking was **not** measured. It was a scratch rig and is not committed.
- **L2 vs L3 against sim truth**, standing sweeps of ±80° yaw and ±25° pitch, 2 laps:

  | head turn rate | rung | rotation p50 / p95 / max (°) | usable |
  |:-|:-|:-|:-|
  | 90°/s | L2 (receive-stamped 20 Hz) | 0.28 / 1.60 / 4.27 | 97.9 % |
  | 90°/s | L3 (source-stamped 50 Hz) | 0.24 / 1.31 / 3.53 | 98.9 % |
  | 180°/s | L2 | 0.25 / 2.03 / 4.24 | 94.7 % |
  | 180°/s | L3 | 0.21 / 1.82 / 4.31 | 96.6 % |

  - Translation p95 is 4 mm on every row.
  - L4 without vision gives exactly the same numbers as L3 here: the trunk is still, so there is no drift to correct.
  - The gain from timestamps is smaller than the note predicted. Even at the truth-matched exposure, L3's p95 stays 1.1 to 2.6°, and error grows with |yaw|. So in the sim the remaining error is robotd's FK against MuJoCo, not timing.
  - The measured frame delay is 82 ms p50 (75 to 115 ms p5 to p95). The fixed value is 90 ms, which is why td is now estimated online.
- **Fusion on synthetic motion:**
  - It corrects a 0.5°/s robot yaw drift: 1.75° error against 9.7° at the end.
  - td converges from 60 ms to 91 ms (truth 90).
  - It rides out a 3 s blank-wall gap and a blurred second without restarting.
  - Solve cost on this slow CPU: about 10 ms per frame and about 70 ms per keyframe window. The note estimated 1 to 5 ms, so this is worth profiling on the PC.
- **e2e tests that pass:** `correction_ease`, `anchor_glide`, `reconstruction` (RGB-D), `slam` (CPU fallback), `slam_recall`, `stall`, `stream`, `mujoco_driver`, `webrtc`.
  - Without CUDA, the robot-first worker fails with the clear "MASt3R model missing" message and the pilot shows the flat feed.
  - The vendored tracker patch applies cleanly to upstream `e6f4e3d`.
- **ruff** passes.
- **Failures that are not this PR's:**
  - `lifecycle` (stuck_link scenario): fails 3/3 on unmodified `origin/main` in this sandbox.
  - `pose_pacing`: flaky on `main` too (sent/s just under its 0.85 bound).

## Needs the GPU PC

- Rebuild models: `uv run --python 3.12 --extra slam python -m ito.build`.
- None of the MASt3R side has run anywhere: the in-solve prior, keyframe write-back and re-anchoring.
- Rungs L1, L4 and L5 with MASt3R depth.
- Prediction PSNR, ghosts, and whether the desktop renderer holds 90 fps alongside.
- Walking drives (b) to (e), blur drive (f), and the real head IMU.
- Suggested run:
  1. Start the sim: `microduck-sim --truth T.jsonl`.
  2. Record: `slam_drive --record R --route sweep --turn-rate 180`, and again with `--route tour`.
  3. Score each rung: `slam_replay R --pose L1|L2|L3|L4|L5 --truth T.jsonl`.
  4. A/B live with `--tracking vision`.

items.title: robotd: play and record on ALSA's default when the configured card is absent
items.body:
## Why

`[audio] device` defaults to `plughw:aic3104`, the Zero 3W's HAT codec. On a board without that card, robotd was silent and deaf with nothing above debug in the journal, even when the board has a working codec of its own. The beta board has an RK809 codec for playback and a face-board PDM mic for capture, two different cards.

## What

`AudioParams::resolve_devices` checks the card a `hw:`/`plughw:` device names against `/proc/asound/cards`. When it's missing, playback and capture both use ALSA's `default` (not `default,0`), and robotd logs the decision once at info. A device that names no card (`default`, a PCM from an asound.conf, a numeric card) is used as written. Boards route `default` through their own ALSA config: the beta image's does (`microduck_yocto`, `microduck-beta-audio`). `sounds` already fell back this way on each call.

The Zero 3W keeps its card, so nothing changes there.

## Checked

- robotd-params tests (98, including the new fallback test)
- robotd tests
- clippy `-D warnings`
- `cargo board -p robotd`
- `cargo +1.94.1 check` on top of #353 (pollen-robotics/microduck)

items.title: The beta board as a second machine, microduck-beta
items.body:
## What

The beta board (Seeed's RK3566 "MicroDuck Main Board", eMMC, no SD) as a second machine, `microduck-beta`, next to the Zero 3W. Some changes apply to every machine; they are marked **(all machines)**.

**Board support**
- **Device tree** in the layer (`rk3566-microduck-beta.dts`). It was transcribed from the V0.1 schematic, then corrected wherever it disagreed with the DTB Seeed's own image boots: VCCIO4 at 1.8 V, RK860 at 0x41, radio GPIOs on bank 2, PCA9535 + 12 face LEDs, PDM mic. The motor bus is UART3 but still `/dev/ttyS2` (serial alias swap).
- **Boot chain:** the RK3566's DDR4 init (rkbin `rk3566_ddr_1056MHz_v1.26` + SPL v1.14). make.sh's default RK3568 blob hangs this board at power-on.
- **Fan:** active trips in `soc-thermal` (off below 52 °C, steps at 60/68/75), switched to `step_wise` by `microduck-fan`. The kernel drives it; a fan zone of its own never registers on Rockchip.
- **USB-C gadget:** serial console plus NCM at 192.168.42.1. **Audio routing** (ALSA default → RK809 + face mic). **Face LEDs** writable by `robot`.
- **Radio:** WuQi WQ9201S driver + firmware (`LICENSE = "CLOSED"`, redistribution terms still to settle). The Bluetooth attach is tried once per boot.
- **`microduck-reboot-voltage`:** a shutdown hook raising vdd_cpu before a reboot. Kept because it is harmless, but **not shown to fix** the boot hangs below.

**Image (all machines)**
- **Daemon 0.15.3** and **policy set v7**. 0.15.3 is the first release that builds on wrynose's Rust 1.94 (pollen-robotics/microduck#358). v7 is its policy floor; below it robotd fails its gait and every update rolls back. `microduck-daemon-crates.inc` was regenerated from the release's `Cargo.lock` files.
- **`[board] version`** declared by `microduck-board` (the beta declares itself `beta`).
- **`microduck` / `microduck` account**, as on the Radxa: in `robot`, `sudo` (asks for the password), `audio`, `video`, `dialout`, `i2c`, `plugdev` and `input`. `sudo` is installed.
- **`aplay`/`arecord`** installed. robotd plays every sound through `aplay`.
- **Voice bank rendered at boot** (`microduck-voice-bank.service`, the release's own `sounds ensure-bank`). An image skips the release's postinstall, so a fresh robot had no voice.
- **`rootfs_b` filled at flash time.** U-Boot falls back to B after A spends its attempts, and an empty B panicked the shared kernel.
- Build plumbing: `kas/beta.yml`, `HFJOB_MACHINE`, a `machine` workflow input.

`docs/agents/beta-board.md` covers flashing, bring-up order, what came from where, and what the board showed.

## Verified on a beta board (2026-10-05/06)

Boots from eMMC, A/B works, and the fallback to slot B was exercised for real. ssh over USB-C and wifi (with the antenna fitted). Seeded 0.15.3, which declares `board beta`, policies v7 and `up_to_date`. The fan is off at idle and the kernel steps it at the trips (PWM levels 0/7.9k/12.9k/18k rpm). The 12 face LEDs, the speaker, `robotctl quack` with no servos, and the `microduck` login and sudo all work.

## Not working or open

- **Boots sometimes hang after U-Boot hands over** (LED off, fan full): warm resets often, including rkdeveloptool's reset after a flash; cold power-on rarely (1 in about 9). Power-cycle after flashing. The next step is a UART2 console during a failure, plus asking Seeed whether their image survives `reboot`.
- **Bluetooth:** the firmware loads, but the controller never answers on UART1. Questions are with Seeed.
- **Face mic** routed right but very quiet. **Face IMU** at 0x6a, which tofd cannot read yet. **Camera** waits on GC2613/GC2093 register tables. **ToF** later.
