items.title: feat: train Microduck language-conditioned action chunks from expert demonstrations
items.body:
## Problem and change

Duckmind has an Action Chunk runtime and replaceable Policy interface, but needs a learned language-conditioned model. This adds a simulation-only expert demonstration, native LeRobot dataset, SmolVLA fine-tuning and evaluation pipeline. The model consumes task text, head-camera RGB and measured body state and predicts 50 absolute joint targets at 20 ms intervals; teacher commands never enter learner features or select its behavior.

The expanded curriculum includes standing, forward/backward walking, turning, four head directions and stopping from either walking direction. State includes joint velocities. Failed expert trajectories are filtered, complete episodes and language expressions are held out, and checkpoint processors retain training-only normalization. Paired familiar-language and task-filtered evaluations separate motor imitation from paraphrase generalization. Training can use native SmolVLA prediction horizons; evaluation reads the horizon from each checkpoint. Robotd control ownership and Safety → RobotIo are unchanged.

## Validation and actual results

- Training formatting, lint and four tests passed; existing Policy tests and lint/type checks passed (10 tests, four pre-existing opt-in skips).
- Native dataset conversion, short CUDA training, checkpoint reload and Policy.infer contract checks passed on the devbox L4.
- Expanded collection accepted 132/132 episodes: 110 training, 22 evaluation, 26,400 frames. Source/data audit records are retained locally on the devbox.
- V2 completed 2,000 training steps and 44 synchronous MuJoCo trials. Only 8/44 passed, all standing or looking right. Execution horizons 5 and 10 each passed 4/22; 33/44 trials stayed stable. This is not yet an expert replacement.
- At the same seed/horizon, familiar language passed 5/11 (standing and all head directions), versus 2/11 for held-out wording. Walking, turning and stopping failed even with familiar wording.
- Follow-up round 1 completed 4,980 further updates: held-out success improved to 12/44 (stand and horizontal head directions), familiar wording to 6/11 (also forward-stop). Walking, turning and backward-stop still fail. Replanning every single tick on five failed familiar-language motion cases still passed 0/5.
- Final bounded round completed: native chunk size 10, unchanged data, 20-step smoke + 4,980 formal updates, and a real 10×15 Policy.infer check. Held-out wording passed 14/44 (standing, left/right looking, some look-down), familiar wording 7/11 (standing, all head directions and both stopping scenarios). Walking and turning still lose balance. Both follow-up training rounds are exhausted; no checkpoint is promoted as an expert replacement. Final model/config/report hashes are retained in run-v4.outputs.sha256.

## Limits

Physics pauses during inference; real-time execution, real hardware and visual grounding are unverified. V4 median inference was 344 ms, longer than its entire 200 ms predicted trajectory; sustainable real-time execution is not demonstrated. Sideways demonstrations were excluded because the installed expert had substantial heading drift; sit/stand transitions and recovery are not covered. Reused evaluation seeds are development diagnostics, not a final unseen test set. The current stock Runner still needs camera-aware observation collection for an online learned loop.

Devloop could not find repocli and used fallback component discovery. Relevant Python checks passed; unrelated Rust checks were not run for these Python/documentation changes. Detailed provenance, metrics and artifact paths are in docs/project/vla-baseline-2026-10-11.md and docs/project/vla-expanded-2026-10-11.md.

Replay learner prefixes with verified physics/actuator continuity, reconstruct the expert action history, and save independently gated correction windows. Keep unassisted controls and rejected attempts; preserve seed-level splits and native LeRobot conversion.

Validated on devbox: 18/18 four-second expert corrections across six seeds, while all six unassisted learners lose balance. Smoke retained one drift rejection and two unreachable prefixes. Nine tests pass against real artifacts; native 10x15 chunks and boundary padding verified for 15 train and 3 eval episodes. Local format/lint pass. No new training, hardware or real-time-control claim.

Autonomous forward evaluation now retains every applied physical state and reports the same sustained-progress, heading and balance gates used for corrective collection, alongside legacy success.

Launch a bounded v5 comparison from identical v4 weights: original data versus original plus 15 accepted correction episodes, 2000 updates each after disposable 20-step smoke runs. Preserve an untrained mixed-normalization control and evaluate all four checkpoints on fresh seeds with familiar and held-out language. Native merge passed 375 sample checks; split audit verified 15 train episodes and excluded seed355.

Validation: training format/lint pass; CPU tests 8 passed, 1 raw-artifact test skipped locally. Formal training and the paired physical outcomes are still running; no improvement or real-time capability is claimed. Experiment budget, confounds, provenance and artifact locations are recorded in the new project note.

The v5 pipeline consumed 4040 updates but mixed failed saving its final checkpoint because /data00 was full. Preserve the failed run and all data; verify/deduplicate one byte-identical model copy and evaluate matched 1500-step checkpoints without further training.

All 48 paired physical trials were completed and independently checked. Strict forward success remains 0/12 for all four model conditions. Mixed has one legacy-only pass with excessive transient yaw; that pass fails on repetition. Record numerical repeatability limits, processor parity, offline latency, raw evidence paths and the exhausted budget.

Validation: documentation diff check; evaluation-only continuation exit0; independent recomputation of 48 trace gates; state/action processor equality; two additional no-training repeats. No code changes or new training in this follow-up. Automatic follow-up ends after result delivery.

items.title: MicroDuck agentic demos: Cascade agents drive learned policies (Isaac Lab + Newton), OVRTX review videos (privileged-state prototypes)
items.body:
> **PRIVILEGED-STATE PROTOTYPES, NOT DEMOS (relabelled 2026-10-13).** Every episode documented in this PR fed the
> agent and its controllers privileged simulator information that the real MicroDuck does not have:
> * the simulator base pose (no SLAM);
> * a ground-truth object detector stand-in;
> * waypoint loops closed on simulator truth.
>
> They show the agent/tool plumbing, but they are not real robot behaviour. They must not be presented as demos.
> The replacement is the onboard-only ("honest") loop on the stacked branch `feat/microduck-agentic-skating`. Its
> parts:
> * own sensors: OVRTX head camera 640x360 at 15 Hz, VL53L8CX ToF model, IMU model, joint encoders;
> * own localization: gyro heading, leg odometry, cuVSLAM RGBD;
> * a real detector (YOLOE) on the camera image.
>
> Simulator truth is used only in the offline checks.

## What

Cascade LLM agents drive the **unchanged learned MicroDuck policies** in Isaac Lab 3.0 + Newton physics. There is one
`AgentOrchestrator` per robot, each with its own EpisodicMemory, its own ToF occupancy map and its own trace.
Recordings are replayed through the OVRTX MicroDuck replay into labelled 1080p review videos.

Stacked on #327 (OVRTX replay). That PR's commit appears here until it merges.

* Learned: every joint target. These come from the walker ONNX, the onboard_hero perception actor (ToF 8x8 + 48x36
  RGB), the get-up policy and depth_navigation_v4, all unchanged handoff deliveries.
* LLM (GPT-6-Astra via the Codex CLI, Cascade `codex_astra` profile): tool choice and parameters, plans, fleet
  messages, and the task_done claim. The simulation is paused while it thinks (lockstep).
* Scripted:
  * the ToF stop guard;
  * the turn-angle and waypoint heading loops, which only choose the walker's velocity command;
  * A* route proposals on the robot's own map;
  * the verifiers.
* Stand-ins, disclosed in the videos:
  * pose from the simulator (no SLAM);
  * object identity from simulator ground truth inside the head camera's field of view (`detect_objects`, used only
    in multi_room_fetch);
  * separate Newton worlds per robot: no robot-robot contact or sensing.

## Results (simulator check on the recorded final state)

| Scenario | Run | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stage_edge | stage2 | PASS: upright on the stage, 0.35 m from the front edge (the agent itself claimed failure) |
| backstage_obstacles | backstage9 | PASS: 0.25 m from the marker, no possible contact (min clearance 0.056 m). A parallel attempt (backstage10) FAILED on possible contact with a speaker box |
| multi_room_fetch (3 ducks) | multiroom6 | PASS 3/3: red box found in room B, room B mapped, blue box reached after a get-up from lying on its back; fleet board used. Two robots' body origins came within 1 cm of a crate/case box (not part of this check, shown on the end card) |
| creative_gym (extra) | gym1 | FAIL: onboard_hero fell on the ridge lane, get_up recovered, then the robot stuck tilted |

**Success rates from repeat runs (small samples):** backstage 1 of 3 (two runs had possible contact), stage_edge 1 of 2
(the failure stopped 5 mm short of the edge band), multi_room_fetch 1 of 2 episodes, 5 of 6 robots (the miss stopped
0.404 m from the box with a 0.4 m limit). In the near misses the agent stops at the limit it reads from the ToF, with
no margin. This was not tuned, to avoid fitting the verifier.

`docs/evidence/microduck-agentic-20261013/attempts.md` lists all 21 episode attempts, passes and failures alike.
Verifier changes made after seeing a result are marked there, and each was followed by a fresh run under the new
definition.

## Videos (1080p, workstation)

* `/home/johnny/Projects/microducks/train/cascade/runs/stage2/stage_edge_agentic_1080p.mp4`
* `/home/johnny/Projects/microducks/train/cascade/runs/backstage9/backstage_obstacles_agentic_1080p.mp4`

* each robot's own map;

* an end card with the simulator verdict next to the agent's own claim.

## Tests

items.title: robotctl led: list, switch, blink and trigger the face board's LEDs
items.body:
## What

`robotctl led list | set <led|all> <on|off|N> | blink <led> | trigger <led> <trigger>`: the beta board's twelve face LEDs, which its device tree exposes as `face:<place>:<colour>` in the kernel's LED class (gpio-leds on a PCA9535 expander).

## Ownership

It writes sysfs directly because no daemon owns an LED yet. Once one does (the camera LED as mediad's streaming indicator from architecture.md §7, status LEDs for whoever owns that status), that daemon is the LED's single writer (§1.1, invariant 4) and this stays the bench tool. Which LED means what is still to be decided.

The beta image gives the `robot` group write access to `brightness` and `trigger` (`microduck_yocto`, `microduck-face-leds`). A custom blink rate needs root, and a permission failure exits DENIED. A board without a face board says so.

## Checked

robotctl tests (206, five new), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo board -p robotctl`. The cheat sheet has the commands.

items.title: Bring the Rust floor back to 1.89, and keep it under Yocto's 1.94
items.body:
## Why

The Yocto image (`microduck_yocto`) builds each daemon release from source with the Rust its OpenEmbedded release ships, **1.94.1** on wrynose. 0.15.1 raised `rust-version` to 1.99 for the atomics' `try_update` in mediad, so cargo refuses to build it there: the image has to seed 0.15.0 instead.

## What

- mediad's two `try_update` calls become `compare_exchange_weak` loops: the same behaviour on every Rust version, and no trip over 1.99 deprecating `fetch_update` under CI's `-D warnings`, or over 1.94 not having `try_update`.
- `rust-version` goes back to 1.89.
- CONTRIBUTING.md now says that number is a **ceiling** as well as a floor, with `cargo +1.94.1 check --workspace` as the check.

## Checked

- `cargo +1.94.1 check --workspace --all-targets`
- stable (1.99) `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- mediad tests (122 pass)
- full `cargo board` with the cross sysroot

Once this is in a release, `microduck_yocto` can pin that release directly instead of 0.15.0.

items.title: Stage I of the agent and environment protocol: the Microduck simulator as an instance of the world interface, with its bridge
items.body:
Stage I of the design of #70 is an embodied instance of the world interface: the Microduck simulator (Pollen Robotics' MuJoCo simulator, which runs the same daemons and client interface as the robot), with a host bridge. Stages E, F and part of G are on `main` (#76, #85, #88, #93); #90 tracks the rest of stage G. This issue tracks stage I. Baseline: `main` at `0af22f8`.

The client interface was observed in one run of the simulator, and the findings are in [this comment of #70](https://github.com/rbeauchamp/acorn/issues/70#issuecomment-5976760764). In short: sensing arrives as JSON decimal numbers at 50 Hz and as an 8 × 8 depth grid at about 14 Hz, on one monotonic clock; a client sends intents (a velocity twist, a head pose, named skills) that vendor-trained networks execute; a velocity intent expires 500 ms after it was sent; a command can be refused, or accepted and not executed; a skill lasts 0.5 to 2.8 s and is not interrupted; there is no reset; the world does not wait for the agent.

## Why this is on the mission's path

Acorn's agent has learned in one world, a generated grid world that waits for each action. The interface of #76 is written for more than one world, and no second world instantiates it. An embodied world is the first one that moves while the agent computes, has no reset and bounds the agent by a clock. It is the first test of the claims of stage G on an executing world: the model `Moving` of `AcornVerif.StepParts` has no executing instance today.

## What the instance must have when the stage is complete

These are requirements read from the observed interface.

- **An observation frame of fixed-width words.** For each field a declared scale, a rounding rule and a saturation rule; presence bits for the fields that may be absent; the 8 × 8 depth grid as distance and status symbols; the age of the depth frame in each observation.
- **A closed finite action table.** Magnitudes that move the body in the simulator (the observed ones: forward 0.3 m/s, turn ±1.5 rad/s; forward 0.15 m/s and every backward command up to 0.3 m/s gave no net motion); sit and stand as two actions; a velocity intent that the bridge sends again inside the 500 ms limit; an outcome for a refused action and one for an accepted action that did not execute; actions that last longer than one decision step.
- **Ownership of power.** The bridge sends the enable command at start. No agent action sends relax, shutdown or disable. There is no reset: the setting is continuing.
- **A goal that the robot's own sensing computes.** Candidates from the observed run: a valid return (status 5) under a threshold in depth rows 0 or 1, which a flat floor cannot produce at the rest head pose; and goals that need no depth sensor (upright by gravity, standing or sitting by trunk height, a heading change by odometry). The nearest return over the whole grid is wrong: rows 2 to 7 see the floor.
- **The declaration of the vendor-network action path**, in the design: as a departure from the learned-only binding, or as the world's actuation interface.
- **The two parts of stage G that need a world on a wall clock** (#90): the timing value that each world declares and a host loop reads, and a host loop for a wall-clock world in which a missed deadline is a protocol fault during which the preceding action holds.

## Decisions of the design step

1. **The vendor networks are the world's actuation interface, not a departure.** The action path of the [learned-only binding](https://github.com/rbeauchamp/acorn/blob/main/docs/learned-only-binding.md) ends at an action of the declared interface. The networks run inside the vendor's daemon, behind the only write handle to the motors (a client cannot write a joint), they are the same in the simulator and on a robot, and Acorn authors none of them. What Acorn authors is the finite table of intents, which is the interface's action set, as the grid world's nine actions are. The limits are stated with it: a primitive action is then a pretrained behaviour of 0.2 to 2.8 s, nothing below an intent is learned, and a result obtained in this world is a result about control over intents. The frame's channel layout, scales and signals are authored, and the instance's adapter becomes a locus of departures D1 and D5 (and D8 if it supplies an achievement event).
2. **One percept and one action for each step, with host events as frame words.** The outcome of the preceding action (executed, unchanged, refused, accepted and not executed) is a word of the next frame, and a late release is a separate word: the fault of the deadline rule. The agent's step is unchanged.
3. **A late action is released late, and nothing the agent chose is dropped.** A missed deadline is counted as a fault. Until the late action is released, the action that was in force stays in force. The bridge keeps that action alive for a bounded number of cycles and then stops sending it, so that an agent that stops deciding lets the vendor's own 500 ms expiry stop the body.
4. **The decision rate starts at 5 Hz with a latency of one cycle**, and the step order is `act-then-learn`, which releases the action after the first part. Reason: one step is 10 control ticks and about one command ramp, and the releases of two consecutive cycles that both meet their deadlines are less than 400 ms apart, inside the 500 ms expiry.
5. **The transport is the trusted boundary and is kept thin.** The socket and the JSON text are outside the proof claim. The bridge parses each line into the proved types at that boundary, and every decision after it is a Lean definition with theorems.
6. **A run of the simulator is a measurement.** It is on a wall clock and is not reproducible bit for bit. Each run has a written protocol first, under the [scientific evidence guidance](https://github.com/rbeauchamp/acorn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#scientific-evidence): the smallest informative run, what it decides and its budget. No run confirms what a theorem settles.

## Increments, in order

Each is one pull request that stands alone.

- [x] **1. The timing a world declares, and the deadline rule.** Merged as #96. `Timing` in the world interface (a world that waits, or a wall clock with a cycle and a latency in cycles), the grid world's declaration, and the pure rule of a wall-clock world: the start of a cycle, the deadline of a percept's action, the verdict on the instant of a release, and a pure outcome that gives, at an instant, the action in force and whether a fault holds, with the theorem that a missed deadline is a fault during which the preceding action holds. It comes first because the instance's interface value, the bridge and the host loop all read it, and it is the smallest part that the executing grid world already instantiates.
- [x] **2. The action table and the bridge's state.** Merged as #98. A closed type of actions with its intents and magnitudes, the declared duration of each action, from which the cycle of the next percept is computed at the instant of its release (the table has no count of cycles for an action), the outcomes, the rule that sends a velocity intent again before it expires and stops after a bounded hold, and the commands a bridge can send, whose type has no relax, shutdown or disable.
- [x] **3. The reading.** Merged as #104. What the body senses, kept by a host as bounded integers: the conversion of a decimal number to a word (total, with its rounding, its saturation and its bounds as theorems or in the type), the declared scales, the state frame and the depth frame with presence for the fields that can be missing, and the age of the depth frame. It has no authored bias on the action path, so it comes before the frame.
- [x] **4. The frame and the interface value.** Merged as #107. The channels and the symbols of a frame built on a reading, the presence words, the depth symbols, the assembly of a frame, the signals and the goal, as a declared module with its departures.
- [x] **5. The host loop of a wall-clock world and the transport**, in six parts, each one pull request, all merged. This is the first executing instance of a world that moves while the agent computes.
  - [x] **5a. Reading a number of the daemon's text.** Merged as #109. The repository's JSON lexer scans a number into its parts with one scanner, with the form of a number in RFC 8259 as a proposition and theorems in both directions; a JSON value is read as a decimal, and the integer kept for it is the nearest to the number its spelling writes, saturated, by a theorem whose statement shares no arithmetic with the reader.
  - [x] **5b. The readers of a state frame and a depth frame.** Merged as #111. The parameters object of each notification, as a parsed value, into a state frame or a depth frame: a proposition for each field that names the member it is read from, and a theorem that a frame is read exactly when it is written so. The tables of labels and of limit names, the exact length of each array, the members that can be missing, and the refusal of a frame as a whole.
  - [x] **5c. The text of a request and a line of a daemon.** Merged as #112. The line of every send of a command and of a subscription, with a request identifier for each send, as the text of a JSON value that the repository's parser is proved to read back; and a daemon's line read as exactly one case by declared criteria taken from JSON-RPC 2.0 (not the whole of that specification), with the rest named invalid.
  - [x] **5d. What a host holds between two events, and its transitions.** Merged as #113. Pure definitions. Two types for the two phases of a host (no percept awaiting, and one awaiting), each sealed by a proof that its state is reached from the start by the transitions. Answers are attributed to the release that holds their identifier, with three reply states; a release names the cycle it answers; the standing of the deadline rule is computed from the last step; the latch of the goal is in the state; a depth frame is paired only when it is stamped at or before its state frame.
  - [x] **5e. The executing loop's pure core.** Merged as #116. A state machine with no IO that calls the host's transitions in the order of the events it is given, with the agent's two step parts as pure tasks: a percept awaits exactly while the agent chooses, the action released is the agent's choice on the percept sensed, the clock's tick reaches the host in every state, and what is sent is exactly the opening lines and the lines of the commands the transitions return. A loop is sealed by its derivation from its start, so no value pairs a sensed percept with a task of another choice. What a host does at a refused frame: it counts it for its stream and changes nothing else.
  - [x] **5f. The driver and the transport.** Merged as #118. The monotonic clock and a ticker, one `nc -U` child for each of the three sockets as the trusted boundary, the native entry point `microduck-host` with its audits and telemetry, and the first run of the simulator under a protocol written first. The loop's core starts the agent's learning only at an event that the driver hands after the release's lines were sent; a run ends as closed when a send fails or a connection ends before its deadline.
- [x] **6. The first measurement.** Merged as #120. A registered protocol for the smallest informative run of the simulator, and its record: in study microduck-depth-and-tilt no clear depth frame came between two near ones in 806 frames at rest in front of a wall, and every state frame of a scripted forward walk and of turns was upright (a tilt of at most 5.1 degrees), so the clear test and the upright bound stay; the contracts `microduck_upright` and `microduck_fresh` and a `learning` telemetry line came with it.
- [x] **7. The host reads the declared timing.** Merged as #123. The Microduck's host and the grid's campaign take their world's timing from its interface by their type: the Microduck's host starts only with the proof that the interface declares its pace, and the host of every stage of its loop holds that pace (`Stage.declared`); the grid's campaign entry takes the proof that the grid's interface declares `synchronized` (`AgentConstruction.runCampaign`); the grid's other entries, whose modules precede its interface, take none. The module text of `AcornVerif.StepParts` names the Microduck host loop as the executing loop of a world that moves while the agent computes, with what its theorems state.

## Completion

- Every requirement above is met by a definition on `main`, with the theorem that states it or with the boundary that is trusted for it, named.
- `./scripts/verify.sh` and the Regula audit pass on each increment.
- The design text states the vendor-network action path and its limits.
- #90's two lines about a world's timing are closed by the increments that deliver them.

Every line above is met as of #123 (`main` at `f3fc68f`). The line-by-line account, with the definition and theorem or trusted boundary for each requirement, is in the description of #123.

## Not in scope

The hardware and anything that needs it; the bounded-lag split on a second computer; the bounds of work and memory; the exact save and restore (#90); ARC worlds (#71); a change of a CI target or deadline.

## Open points

- The interface requires a symbol array. Whether a robot carries the depth sensor is not known, and the vendor's SDK says most units have none. An instance without it lays word codes over symbol positions, as the grid world does with its task context, until the deferred requirement that a world may supply no symbol array is taken up. That requirement (R1 of the interface design) is tracked here.
- Whether the hardware shares the simulator's dead zone for small velocity commands is not known.
- The memory of the robot's computer, and whether the agent runs on it beside the daemons, are not known.
- For increment 5e (the executing loop): the cycle of the next percept adds the action's declared duration for every release, including one that starts no skill (`sit` for a body that sits waits about 1.4 s; a refused pick waits 3 s). That is safe, since the duration is an upper bound, and it spends time of a world that does not wait. The first case can be decided at the release, because the state holds the stated posture; the second cannot, because the reply arrives later.
- Decided by increment 6 (#120): whether the depth status drops out at close range. In the simulator it cannot, since a zone's status is 255 only when its ray meets nothing within 4 m (read in the vendor's `tof.py`), and at rest in front of a wall no clear frame came between two near ones in 806 depth frames, so the test of a clear reading stays as it is. Whether a physical sensor's status drops out is not known.
- Decided by increment 6 (#120): the upright bound stays at the level of -0.95. Every state frame of a scripted forward walk at 0.3 m/s and of turns at 1.5 rad/s was upright, the trunk tilting by at most 5.1 degrees, and at the next level a sitting body pitched forward by 29.8 degrees would read a flat floor as near, at 237 mm. How far a learning agent's actions, skills and falls tilt the trunk is not known.
- Paid by increment 6 (#120): the upright and freshness tests are registered decisions with the contracts `microduck_upright` and `microduck_fresh`, beside `microduck_near` and `microduck_clear`.

### Added tool

items.title: policy search: say what each policy is, and show it
items.body:
`robotctl policy search microduck` answered with `org/name`, an origin and a like count:

```
RemiFabre/microduck-flamingo-cycle    community  29 likes
HannesVonEssen/microduck-swing        community  0 likes
neil-jo/microduck-polite-bow          community  0 likes
```

Every hit is somebody's `microduck-<something>`. That is enough to install one and not enough to choose one — the only way to find out what a policy did was to install it and run it.

Now, from a live search against the Hub:

```
RemiFabre/microduck-flamingo-cycle  community  29 likes
  "Stand on one foot, either side, on command, and come back to a two-foot stand: twist = [flag, side, 0]."
  https://huggingface.co/RemiFabre/microduck-flamingo-cycle/resolve/main/media/preview.mp4
RemiFabre/microduck-rough-walk-g  community  1 likes
  "Velocity-commanded walking trained from scratch on a rough-terrain ladder (3300 iterations): the sturdiest of the family on small stairs and slopes, at +17% motor power over alpha_walking."
  https://huggingface.co/RemiFabre/microduck-rough-walk-g/resolve/main/media/preview.mp4
```

Both `robotctl` and `duckctl` print it.

## Where both come from

Neither is new information — it was just not on this path. The **description** is `manifest.json`'s, the field `docs/policy-manifest.md` has always had and `policy fetch` already prints on the way in. The **video** is a file convention: published policies carry a clip at `media/preview.mp4`, and the [policy playground](https://huggingface.co/spaces/pollen-robotics/microduck-policy-playground) already finds it that way. This follows the playground's order rather than inventing a `preview` manifest field, because asking every publisher to write down again what the path already says buys nothing.

Measured against the Hub as it is today, running the real search function: **25 hits in 0.5 s, 11 with a description, 17 with a clip**, and the picks are the ones a person would make. `HannesVonEssen/microduck-stilts` carries `10cm/preview.mp4` and `100cm/preview.mp4` beside `media/preview.mp4`, and the agreed path wins; `Teethyfish/microduck-collision-flamingo-ii` has only a viewer screen-recording, and shows it, which is the playground's behaviour too.

## What it costs, and the three bounds on it

The clip is free: `full=true` on the search brings each repo's file list with the hits, so there is no tree listing per repo. The reply grows to tens of kilobytes, well inside the metadata cap.

The description is one GET per repo, and that is the one place a search fans out. Hugging Face rate-limits by address, and the address belongs to whoever else is on that network — a 429 earned here is paid for by somebody's browser and somebody's `git push`. So:

- only repos whose file list actually holds a `manifest.json` are asked, so a search matching 25 unrelated models makes no extra request at all;
- six in flight at a time;
- the whole thing gives up after 8 seconds and keeps whatever arrived, per hit rather than all-or-nothing.

Nothing here can fail a search. An unreadable manifest, a slow mirror and a repo that never had one all read as no description.

The description is also cut to its first line and 200 characters. It is a stranger's string landing on a line in a list of twenty-five, and a publisher who pastes an essay would otherwise reformat someone else's listing.

## Rendering, in both tools

`duckctl policy search` printed the reply whole, as JSON: every field of twenty-five hits, three lines apart, with the sentence that answers the question indented inside a string. It now prints the same block `robotctl` does — the third rendering exception after `scan` and `logs`, on the same rule those two state, that a command whose answer is a list somebody chooses from earns one and a command whose answer is a fact does not.

`PolicySearchHit::details` is shared between them, so the two cannot drift on the part that is the same answer. What each keeps is its own: the id column, and the next step, which is not the same command on the robot (`policy load <slot> <repo>`) as it is over a radio (`fetch`, then `load` with the path that comes back). `duckctl`'s advice goes to stderr, so a pipe gets hits only.

While there: this enum's doc claimed the Hub calls are not served over this transport. `btd` routes `policy.check`, `policy.fetch` and `policy.search`, and has for as long as `duckctl` has had the subcommands — which is the point of them, since a robot with no LAN is configured from a laptop that has one.

## Wire

`description` and `preview` on `PolicySearchHit`, both optional, `API_VERSION` 33 → 34. Additive: an older client ignores them, and a client talking to an older `updaterd` sees them absent and shows the id, which is what it showed before.

## Checks

`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean. `cargo clippy` clean on `updater`, `robotctl`, `duck-ipc-proto`, `duckctl`. Tests pass, with eight new ones: the preview order (agreed paths, one clip per variant, a named preview beating an unnamed video, GIF last, no video at all), the one-line cut, and the shared rendering contract.

Run end to end both ways. The search function against the live Hub, which is where the numbers above come from. And this branch's `duckctl policy search microduck` against a robot on `0.14.2`, which is the version-skew case: the robot answers `v33`, the client says so and carries on, and the hits print with no details under them because that `updaterd` does not send any — which is what a client meeting an older robot should do.

items.title: B50: capture-time alignment of camera, IMU and proprioception (opt-in)
items.body:
## B50 — capture-time alignment of camera, IMU and proprioception (opt-in)

ROADMAP Perception row: *"validate IMU/proprioception fusion and time alignment while preserving missing, stale and uncertain observations"*. This PR lands the **time-alignment** half in software; fusion and the live measurement stay open.

### The gap (pinned by premise tests that pass on main)
The sensing layer types IMU/joint captures (epoch, sequence, clock domain, capture time), but nothing paired a camera capture with the IMU/joint sample taken at its capture time. `read_sensor` returns each sensor's latest capture independently: on the real loopback mobile bridge a camera read at physics step 10 followed by an IMU read returns steps 10 and 11, and nothing says so. The only capture-time pairing in the repo was B39's link self-mask (`JointSamples`), private to that module.

### Why this increment
One shared component plus one opt-in consumer on the IMU/proprio path. It is the prerequisite the row names, it is measurable on CPU through the real path (loopback mobile bridge + MCP), and it **generalizes B39 instead of duplicating it**. A fusion estimator is out of scope: it needs its own live validation, and pairing first lets any later fusion refuse misaligned inputs.

### Mechanism
- **`src/cascade/sensing/alignment.py`** (new, stdlib only): `SampleBuffer` + `nearest()` (generalized out of B39's `JointSamples`) and `classify()` → `Pairing` with four states:
  - `aligned`: |skew| ≤ `max_skew_s` (inclusive).
  - `stale`: farther. Identity and skew are reported, the **value is withheld**.
  - `missing`: no sample; nothing is made up.
  - `uncertain`: the value is returned but flagged. Reasons: clock not comparable, payload `saturated`, or the sample's own rate × |skew| above a declared tolerance (a first-order estimate, not a bound).
  - Never interpolates or extrapolates, ties keep the earlier sample, unmeasured channels are listed as `absent` (never zero).
  - `align_capture()` pairs admitted `ObservationEnvelope`s on one clock instance only: same clock domain and epoch, or the process-local `monotonic` clock across provider epochs. With no comparable capture, the latest one is `uncertain` (skew unknown) while younger than the sensor's `max_age_s`, and `stale` after that.
- **Consumer (opt-in):** a sensors-domain `alignment:` block (`max_skew_s` required in (0, 1] s; optional `max_rotation_rad` / `max_translation_m`) adds the read-only tool **`sensing.read_aligned`** (RobotRuntime / MCP):
  - Reads ONE fresh reference capture. A failed or repeated reference read refuses the call; no older pixels are substituted.
  - Reads each paired sensor once. A refusal such as a replay is reported as `read_error`, not treated as fatal.
  - Pairs each sensor from the hub's bounded history. `SensorHub.now()` exposes the hub clock that ages are judged on.
- **`perception/link_mask.py`:** `JointSamples` is now a `SampleBuffer`, and the frame ↔ joint decision goes through `classify()`. Behaviour is unchanged (73 existing tests + 3 goldens).
- **Default byte-identical:** without `alignment:`, the sensors-domain tool catalog of all 5 shipped sensors profiles keeps the golden digest computed on be57535.

### Measured (CPU only, `tests/test_proprio_time_alignment.py`, 42 tests)
- **Real loopback mobile bridge** (state socket + RGB-D frame cache) **through the MCP composed-robot path**:
  - A step-10 camera capture pairs with the step-11 IMU and joint samples at **+5 ms → aligned** (bound 7.5 ms).
  - A step-14 capture finds only step 11: **−15 ms → stale**, value withheld, `replay` reported.
  - A **3 rad/s yaw 5 ms from the capture → uncertain** (0.015 rad > 0.01 rad).
  - Only reader-role `hello`/`state`/`frame` requests reach the bridge, and no actuator is constructed.
- RED on an export of origin/main be57535: `35 failed, 7 passed`. The 7 are 3 premises + 4 golden pins.
- GREEN: `42 passed`. Related test files (sensing, robot runtime/MCP, spatial, embodiment, link self-mask, …): `1191 passed, 5 skipped`.
- Mutation on scratch copies (3 test files): **66/66 killed**.
- Full suite (head ed3b0f8, same tree as the suite run on 80fbac7 = origin/main be57535 + this change): `3 failed, 10493 passed, 346 skipped, 4 deselected` (`EXIT=1`). The 3 failures are exactly the known baseline MuJoCo placement tests; baseline be57535 is `3 failed, 10451 passed, 346 skipped, 4 deselected`, so passed = 10451 + 42 new.

### Not claimed
- IMU/proprioception fusion: no estimator consumes the pairings.
- Any native/Isaac skew number.
- Producer-rate sampling: the pairing sees only captures that reads admitted, at most 32 captures / 16 MB shared by all sensors.
- Hardware clock sync.
- The accuracy of the first-order rate × skew estimate.

A CPU smoke of the parent's measurement tool against the loopback bridge with a fake producer is not a measurement. With 40 ms on-demand reads, a 30 ms camera and 5 ms state, most pairings were *stale* at a 10 ms bound: the state is read after the camera, and the history only holds earlier reads. That is why producer-rate sampling is the first follow-up.

### Follow-ups
1. A producer-rate IMU/state history: a bounded background reader, or a "state at step N" bridge query.
2. A fusion estimator that consumes only `aligned` pairings.
3. Optional use of `RobotState.dq` for the link mask's `uncertain` (needs its own flag).
4. Hardware clocks (PTP) for physical sensors.

### Live validation owed (parent, Isaac/Newton MicroDuck bridge, GPU)
1. Start an owned MicroDuck bridge with `--camera-rgbd`, using the same recipe as the stream07 run (docs/CUVSLAM_NATIVE_VALIDATION.md "Live native RGB-D stream", docs/OBSERVED_RGBD.md) and a new output dir `<run>`.
2. Measure while standing (zero policy commands). This is a passive reader that never steps or commands:
   ```
   env -u PYTHONPATH PYTHONPATH=<merged-checkout>/src CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 <venv>/bin/python \
     /home/johnny/Projects/demo/cascade-lab/HERMES_BACKLOG_20261009/proprio-alignment/live/measure_alignment.py \
     --run-dir <run> --samples 200 --period-s 0.05 --max-skew-s 0.02 --max-rotation-rad 0.02 \
     --out <run>/b50-standing.json
   ```
3. Run the same command during a walk/turn episode commanded by the bridge owner, with `--out <run>/b50-walking.json`.
4. From each JSON, report:
   - `summary.sensors.{imu,joints}.statuses`, the `abs_skew_s` quantiles, `reasons`, `reference_refusals` and `close.ok`.
   - That every pairing's epoch equals the run's.
   - That `motion_exceeds_tolerance` appears only while the gyro rate × skew > 0.02 rad.

### Proposed AGENTS.md line
> **Capture-time alignment (B50):** pair sensor samples by capture time only through `cascade.sensing.alignment` (`SampleBuffer`/`classify`/`align_capture`). Never interpolate, withhold stale/missing values and keep unmeasured channels absent. Compare clocks only within one clock domain + epoch (the process-local `monotonic` clock across epochs). `sensing.read_aligned` exists only with a sensors-domain `alignment:` block.

### Docs
- ROADMAP Perception row: struck, with a landed line and what stays open.
- ARCHITECTURE: mechanism bullet, `sensing/` in the module map, Known limitations.
- ROBOT_MODULARITY: "Capture-time alignment (B50, opt-in)".
- OBSERVED_RGBD: pointer.
- `configs/robots/mixed_mock.yaml`: commented flag example.

items.title: dev: do not run in a fork
items.body:
A contributor's push runs the `dev` workflow in their own fork, where `MINISIGN_DEV_SECRET_KEY` does not exist. Every such run built, then failed at "Sign with the dev key" — every recent run in `Quchaosheng/microduck` and `Nixxx19/microduck` ended that way. A fork's branch was therefore always red, and a real build failure there looked the same as the missing key.

The `publish` job now skips when the repository is a fork (`!github.event.repository.fork`). `ci.yml` on the pull request, which is unaffected, is what checks the change. The push of this branch confirmed the job still runs here.

items.title: B72: opt-in producer-rate sampling for sensing.read_aligned
items.body:
## B72: opt-in producer-rate sampling for `sensing.read_aligned`

Closes the ROADMAP Perception gap left after B50: "producer-rate sampling (the pairing sees only captures that reads admitted)".

### Problem (premise test, passes on main)
B50's `read_aligned` pairs a fresh reference capture only among the captures that READS admitted to the hub. Its skew therefore depends on when the caller reads. The IMU can have produced a sample at the camera's capture instant that no read ever saw. The pairing then takes a farther capture, often stale.

### Mechanism (all opt-in; absent = byte-identical, pinned by golden tests)
- **Producers record at publication, bounded.**
  - `MobileBridgeController(state_history=N)` (bridge CLI `--state-history N`, 1..256) keeps its last N completed states exactly as `state` would serve them, each with its own publication time.
  - It advertises `state_history` in `hello` (capability + size) and serves the states to reader channels as `state_history(after_step)`. These are copies of history, never a refresh, and a new epoch empties them.
  - Without the option, `hello` is unchanged and the op is refused. The flag is absent from the recorded arguments unless given.
  - In process, `BufferedSensorProvider(descriptor, history=N)` records its last N publications.
- **Reader.** `BaseTruthReader.history(after_step)` checks:
  - the advertised bound
  - the reply epoch
  - every state's identity
  - that steps and physics times strictly advance past `after_step`

  One reply has one receipt time, and every age includes the round trip. `MobileStateSensorProvider.read_produced` and `EmbodimentBoundProvider.read_produced` (payload contract re-checked) build on it.
- **Hub.** `SensorHub.enable_produced(N)` (before seal), `read_produced` and `produced`:
  - Each fetch runs through the sensor's own bounded worker, deadline and quarantine.
  - Samples are admitted under the read rules: identity, one epoch per sensor (shared with reads), strictly increasing sequence, capture time and receipt.
  - A violating batch is refused whole and its watermark does not move.
  - A sample that is stale or over the packet bound is seen but never admitted, not even when presented again.
  - Each sensor's ring holds at most N samples and `max_history_bytes`, apart from the shared read history, so RGB-D cannot evict IMU samples.
- **Domain.** `alignment.producer_history: N` (1..256; bool, float and string are refused) makes `read_aligned` do the following:
  - It reads each paired sensor once, then fetches its producer history. A refusal is reported as `producer_error`.
  - It pairs among both sets (`merge_captures`: capture-time order, one copy per capture, the read copy kept).
  - B50's classification is unchanged: nothing interpolated, ties keep the earlier sample, stale and missing values withheld, another epoch or clock domain never aligned, saturation or rate × skew uncertain.
  - Each pairing reports `from_producer`, and the policy reports `producer_history`.
- `mobile_state_offload.READ_ONLY` now includes `state_history`. The guard test `test_mobile_state_server.py` pins that set and was updated.

### Measured (CPU, `tests/test_producer_rate_alignment.py`)
Setup:
- Real loopback mobile bridge, reached through MCP (`McpSkillServer` → RobotRuntime → `mobile_rgbd` + `mobile_state` providers).
- Two domains on the same bridge: `read_time` and `producer`.
- One camera capture every 6 physics steps (33.3 Hz at 5 ms), 24 captures.
- `read_aligned` polled 0–5 steps (0–25 ms) after each capture, each delay used 4×.
- `max_skew_s` 7.5 ms, `max_rotation_rad` 0.01; IMU yaw ≈3 rad/s, joints 0.5 rad/s.
- Deterministic stepping: explicit publishes, no free-running thread.

| IMU/joints rate | mode | IMU | joints | \|skew\| mean / median / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 Hz | read-time | 4 aligned / 4 uncertain / 16 stale | 8 aligned / 16 stale | 9.167 / 10 / 15 ms |
| 200 Hz | producer ring | 24 aligned | 24 aligned | 0 / 0 / 0 ms |
| 50 Hz | read-time | 8 aligned / 16 stale | 8 aligned / 16 stale | 8.333 / 10 / 20 ms |
| 50 Hz | producer ring | 12 aligned / 12 stale | 12 aligned / 12 stale | 5 / 5 / 10 ms |

- At 200 Hz, 40 of the 48 read-time pairings took a farther capture although a closer one had already been produced. 32 of those were stale and 4 uncertain (IMU, +5 ms at 3 rad/s). The ring never paired a farther capture (`ring_farther` = 0).
- At 50 Hz, 8 of the 48 read-time pairings took a farther capture than one already produced, and all 8 were stale; the ring aligned them. A capture that falls between two produced samples stays stale at −10 ms. The ring cannot invent the missing instants, and nothing is interpolated.
- The bridge runner (`scripts/isaac_microduck_bridge.py --state-history 8`, CPU software backend) records every completed step it publishes.

### Tests
- New file `tests/test_producer_rate_alignment.py`, 60 tests.
- **RED** on an export of origin/main 38f6d08: `55 failed, 5 passed in 1.43s`. The 5 that pass do so by design:
  - the premise test
  - 3 goldens: default `read_aligned` digest `641a62f2…2635`, B50's shipped-catalog digest, and default `hello`/no `state_history`
  - the default-off bridge runner
- **GREEN**: `60 passed`.
- With `test_proprio_time_alignment.py` + `test_mobile_state_server.py`: `132 passed`.
- **Related set** (63 files touching the changed modules): `1 failed, 1948 passed, 6 skipped`.
  - The 1 failure is `test_mobile_effects::test_pre_admission_travel_never_confirms_an_inert_command` (`reader_timeout`; the fixture's `read_timeout_s` is 0.04 and the box load was ~17).
  - That file passes alone: `329 passed`.
- **Mutation** on a scratch copy: 83 mutants across all 9 changed modules plus the CLI, **83/83 killed** (unmutated: `155 passed`).
  - The first run left 1 survivor: the reader's step-order check, because the reversed tamper also reversed times.
  - Fixed by adding the `step` tamper (steps 1,2,3,3 at increasing times).
- **Full suite** (rebased head 1388108 = origin/main 38f6d08 + 1): `3 failed, 10790 passed, 346 skipped, 4 deselected, 2 warnings in 1632.20s`, `EXIT=1`. The 3 failures are exactly the known MuJoCo placement ones; baseline 38f6d08 was `3 failed, 10730 passed`, and 10730 + 60 new = 10790.

### Not claimed
- The native skew distribution on Isaac, with or without the ring.
- A fusion estimator that consumes the pairings.
- Hardware clock synchronization.
- Producer history through the off-GIL `--state-reader process` reader. A handed-off reader channel refuses `state_history`, so the pairing reports `producer_error` and falls back to read-time sampling.
- `--state-history` on the H2 owner.
- Producer history for RGB/RGB-D providers (the reference is read fresh).

### Follow-ups
- Fusion estimator over the aligned pairings (ROADMAP Perception, still open). It is the natural next step and was not done here.
- `state_history` on the off-GIL state reader (`mobile_state_server` frame ops) and on the H2 owner.
- The live Isaac distribution (below).

### Live validation owed (parent, Isaac/Newton MicroDuck bridge, GPU 0)
1. Start an owned MicroDuck bridge with `--camera-rgbd --state-history 64`. Use the same recipe as the stream07 / B50 runs (docs/CUVSLAM_NATIVE_VALIDATION.md "Live native RGB-D stream", docs/OBSERVED_RGBD.md), a new output dir `<run>`, and the default in-process state reader (not `--state-reader process`). Check that `BRIDGE_LISTENING.json` → `hello.capabilities` lists `state_history` and that `hello.state_history == 64`.
2. Standing (zero policy commands). This is a passive reader that never steps or commands:
   ```
   env -u PYTHONPATH PYTHONPATH=<merged-checkout>/src CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 <venv>/bin/python \
     /home/johnny/Projects/demo/cascade-lab/HERMES_BACKLOG_20261009/producer-rate-alignment/live/measure_producer_alignment.py \
     --run-dir <run> --producer-history 64 --samples 200 --period-s 0.05 --max-skew-s 0.0075 \
     --max-rotation-rad 0.02 --out <run>/b72-standing.json
   ```
   This script was smoke-tested on a CPU loopback bridge from the test fixtures: close ok, `ring_farther` 0, `producer_errors` 0.
3. Run the same command during a walk/turn episode commanded by the bridge owner, with `--out <run>/b72-walking.json`.
4. From each JSON, report:
   - `summary.sensors.{read_time,producer}/{imu,joints}`: statuses, `abs_skew_s` quantiles, reasons, `from_producer`, `producer_errors`
   - `summary.cases`: `ring_farther` must be 0
   - `reference_refusals` and both `close.ok`

### Proposed AGENTS.md line
> **Producer-rate sampling (B72):** a producer records the samples it publishes only behind an explicit bounded option (`state_history=N` / `--state-history N`, `BufferedSensorProvider(history=N)`). The hub admits them under the read rules into a per-sensor ring (`enable_produced`), and `read_aligned` pairs among read and produced captures only with `alignment.producer_history`. The classification stays B50's: never interpolate, and never let a produced sample bypass identity, epoch, ordering or age admission.

### Docs
- ROADMAP Perception row: producer-rate sampling struck, with a landed line, the measurement and what stays open.
- ARCHITECTURE: mechanism bullet, `sensing/` module map, Known limitations.
- ROBOT_MODULARITY: new section "Producer-rate sampling (B72, opt-in)"; B50's not-claimed item struck.
- OBSERVED_RGBD: pointer.
- `configs/robots/mixed_mock.yaml`: commented `producer_history` example. The sensors `alignment:` block lives in robot profiles, as with B50; `configs/demo.yaml` has no sensing block.

items.title: duck-sim: name a body that has no eye, and stop the right process
items.body:
Two fixes to `scripts/duck-sim`, independent of each other and of anything else.

## A camera the other repo does not have yet

`DUCK_SIM_CAMERAS=a` makes this script pass `--cameras a --frame-port 7901` to `duck-body` — the
MuJoCo process, which lives in `microduck_rl` and not here. The camera arrived there long after
`duck-body` did, so a checkout that predates it does not know those two arguments, and argparse
exits rather than ignoring them.

`duck-body` is started in the background with its output redirected, so from this side that looks
like a port that never opens. What you got was:

```
== starting the body — a MuJoCo window should open
error: the simulator did not come up. ~/.cache/duck-sim/body.log has why.
```

with the actual reason one line inside `body.log`:

```
body_server.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --cameras a --frame-port 7901
```

Now the script reads that log when the port fails to open, recognises this one case and says it:

```
error: this microduck_rl has no camera: its body server does not know --cameras.

    git -C /Users/you/Dev/duck/microduck_rl checkout develop && git -C /Users/you/Dev/duck/microduck_rl pull

The rendering is on develop; a checkout on an older branch has the body and not the eye.
Or unset DUCK_SIM_CAMERAS, and the duck runs blind.
```

Every other startup failure falls through to the existing message, unchanged.

`start_body` also prints which `microduck_rl` it is starting. `DUCK_SIM_RL` can point this script at
any checkout, so "which one is running?" is the next question after the error above — and the script
never said.

## `stop_one` identifies the process, it does not name its kind

The guard that keeps `down` from acting on a recycled pid checked the daemon's name — `robotd`. That
is a name check dressed as an identity check: a stale pidfile whose pid has since been recycled onto
*another* `duck-sim`'s robotd passes it, and `down` then TERMs somebody else's duck.

Two simulators on one machine is not exotic. Different `DUCK_SIM_STATE`, different ports is exactly
how you run one while another is up, and the stale pidfile is what the last run left behind. This
file already says a pid is not an identity and that nothing may act on one without confirming what
it is; this makes the confirmation say which duck as well as which daemon.

Every caller now passes something from the argv this script gave that process — the socket or config
path under `$STATE`, or for the body the port it was started on. None of those appears in another
state directory's daemon.

## Verified

`shellcheck -s sh` clean on the changed lines. The camera message fired against a checkout without
the rendering and printed the right branch; a checkout with it starts normally. A full `up`/`down`
cycle against MuJoCo starts every daemon and leaves nothing behind, with and without a camera.

items.title: [Feature] MicroDuck proprioceptive and visual prior recipes
items.body:
## Summary

MicroDuck priors can train from proprioception or proprioception plus a sampled head camera, with an explicit choice of actor-input or privileged-state critic. The legacy 56-value walker and nine-skill ordering remain compatible. Skills, prior training and controllers stay in TorchRL; the optional games zoo reuses the sensor sampler and encoder for recurrent game selectors.

The 53-value proprioceptive schema excludes simulator linear velocity and world pose. Camera inputs expose uint8 RGB, age and validity, with configurable rate, delay, dropout and noise. Camera history survives snapshots independently and clears on reset. The loader restores the recorded sensor architecture; controllers use the matching command and clock offsets.

## What changes

The legacy state observation contains privileged simulator velocity. The sensor actor instead receives an explicitly ordered deployable input:

```text
before, state (56):
  gravity[0:3], gyro[3:6], body_velocity[6:9], command[9:11],
  joint_position[11:25], joint_velocity[25:39], gait[39:42], action[42:56]

after, proprioception (53):
  gravity[0:3], gyro[3:6], command[6:8],
  joint_position[8:22], joint_velocity[22:36], gait[36:39], action[39:53]
```

Noise is applied only to `gyro[3:6]`, `joint_position[8:22]`, and `joint_velocity[22:36]`. A parametrized regression now proves that each option leaves every other field unchanged.

The pinned robot asset’s camera quaternion faces into its own head. The implementation preserves lens position and converts the matching camera site’s outward/up axes to MuJoCo’s optical frame. Native rendering retains at most two resolution-specific contexts, avoiding repeated context creation when policy cameras and spectator videos alternate. Snapshot renderers remain independent. Eviction and environment close make each renderer’s own graphics context current before releasing GPU objects, preventing cleanup from damaging another environment’s images.

Hydra observation groups compose with PPO/PPO-EWMA and the complete-episode prior recipe from #4378. This PR stacks on #4378 above #4375. Documentation cites the stock camera/IMU sources and records simulation/deployment limitations; no onboard-compatibility claim is made for the legacy 14-actuator simulator.

## Validation

- The sensor-noise layout regression passes for gyro, joint-position, and joint-velocity noise.
- 37 native, prior, loader, controller and rendering checks passed; one CUDA case skipped. Three optional accelerated-backend cases encounter the existing local mujoco-torch/MuJoCo 3.10 import incompatibility.
- All six prior combinations of sensor mode and critic inputs pass recurrent PPO-EWMA update/resume checks.
- Camera mount, ordered images, sample timing, reset and snapshot ownership regressions pass. Downloaded-asset images show an outward upright view; sustained discovery with the same corrected mount passes in the zoo.
- Installed zoo consumer: 44 tests passed, one accelerated skip. A visual hide-and-seek PPO-EWMA smoke with a frozen opponent and reference KL passes without importing examples.
- Sensor collection benchmarks pass in all three modes. A ten-pair 64-square/160-square render probe fell from 3.61 s to 0.55 s with identical pixels; the dedicated mixed-resolution benchmark passes.

The installed integration CI pins zoo commit `b1a4dcbdfd232f7c84ccf5190ea7ac4493842f2e`. Linux CI exposed a cross-environment rendering regression during clone cleanup. The strengthened pixel regression passes on Mac CGL and GLFW after the cleanup fix in `8c4cc4e725c12fa072df70cd1cd9dda45878237c`; the dedicated Linux GLFW regressions pass with MuJoCo 3.10 and 3.8.1, as do isolated ARM64 Linux tests with stable and nightly torch. The earlier x86 bulk-suite failure remains under investigation; the current full-suite rerun is pending. Installed integration and zoo native CI are green. Sensor prior learning and hardware deployment remain unevaluated.

items.title: provision-board: an ssh hiccup is not provisioning finished
items.body:
`provision-board.sh` sometimes reported `provisioning finished` while the board was still in apt, and then failed with `robotctl: command not found`.

`still_provisioning` treated any non-zero exit from `rsh "test -f provision.env"` as the file being gone. ssh exits 255 when a single round-trip fails, and that happens on a board running apt triggers (5 s connect timeout, 6 s keepalive budget). The `alive` probe that follows then succeeds, so the watcher reads that as finished.

Now only `test`'s own 1 counts as the file being gone. Any other status loops again if the board answers, or returns 2 (lost board) if it does not.

Seen on a microduck at 192.168.10.145: `robot-provision.service` was still active, `provision.env` was still present and apt was unpacking gstreamer when the watcher exited.

## Summary

Deepens the public Microduck reverse-engineering documentation while making the project substantially easier to enter for non-expert readers.

### New paired English / Simplified Chinese guides

- beginner-friendly **Start Here** project map
- **Simulation First** quickstart using official MJCF models and existing official ONNX policies before hardware work
- staged **Public Reproduction Roadmap** from simulation to small hardware benches, mechanical subassemblies and sim-to-real validation
- detailed **Hardware Parameter Reference**
- **Structure and Assembly Map** that turns the MJCF/mesh tree into understandable robot modules
- detailed **Sim-to-Real Parameter Reference** covering BAM, voltage, sag, delay, backlash, domain randomization, contact and terrain

### Navigation / information architecture

Reworks both repository home pages and both documentation indexes so a new reader can choose a goal-oriented path instead of encountering a flat list of technical pages. Updates both roadmaps accordingly.

### Examples of newly documented public parameters

- 15 physical motor IDs / 14 policy joints / 61-D observations / 50 Hz
- exact current runtime motor IDs and home pose
- current simulation joint limits and rigid-body inertial masses
- pinned full-collision model inertial-mass sum (~737.243 g)

### Public-source boundary

All additions are based on public official sources or clearly labeled public community reconstruction. Simulation-model quantities are not presented as production BOM quantities. Unpublished PCB, wiring, manufacturing, fastener and production details remain unresolved rather than guessed.

items.title: Sim head camera looks slightly lower than the pilot's gaze
items.body:
Pilot report (fix/slam-recall on Ceres, Microduck sim): the robot's camera points a little further down than the in-game camera. The top of the view is black (nothing captured yet) and splats exist below the view that the pilot never sees.

Suspects to check, in order:
- `drivers/microduck/adapter.py` aims `robot.look` at a point 2 m out (`x,y = 2·cos/sin(pan)·cos(tilt)`, `z = 2·sin(tilt)`). If robot.look measures that target from the trunk or neck rather than from the camera, a level gaze aims below the horizon. With the camera ~5–10 cm above that origin, the bias is ~1.5–3° at 2 m.
- Pitch offset in the `head_camera` site/camera quat (robot_allcollisions.xml vs robot_walk.xml), or body pitch while walking.
- Ito renders the view from the commanded head pose, but frames carry the measured `camera_pose`.

Done when: logged pilot tilt and measured camera pitch (frame metadata) agree within 1° standing and walking, in the sim. The fix belongs on the Ito side (target relative to the camera, or a measured offset), not in the robot's IK.

Note: real head cam is IMX219 at 62° HFOV, mounted 90° (#21).

items.title: docs: make knowledge + synthetic labs the core project direction
items.body:
## Summary

Reframes `robot-sysid-lab` around two first-class tracks:

- a **knowledge track** for robotics engineers learning practical SysID;
- a **simulation-first synthetic lab track** using teacher/student systems with complete hidden ground truth.

## What changes

- defines the project as a learning + synthetic research lab rather than a framework-first effort;
- adds a detailed knowledge syllabus covering SysID fundamentals, robot dynamics, actuator modeling, experiment design, identifiability, estimation, validation, and sim-to-real;
- defines the synthetic ladder:
  - 1-DoF concepts
  - synthetic actuator
  - fixed-base leg
  - leg + contact
  - Microduck
  - **Microban** small humanoid
  - sim-to-sim mismatch
  - later hardware validation
- introduces teacher/student truth difficulty levels and cross-cutting benchmarks for model mismatch, excitation design, observation ablation, optimizer behavior, and cross-condition validation;
- keeps supporting abstractions (`Dataset`, `Model`, `ParameterSchema`, `Estimator`, etc.) subordinate to concrete labs;
- removes the early `synthetic/one_dof_lab.py` implementation so the benchmark contract can be stabilized before code is rebuilt.

## Design intent

Synthetic simulation remains a long-term first-class environment, not only a stepping stone to hardware. The benchmark should exploit complete ground truth while restricting student observations to realistic signals, deliberately introduce model mismatch, and scale hierarchically from actuator to leg to Microduck to Microban.

No new implementation is introduced in this PR.

items.title: Add the parameter sweep harness and the first robustness map
items.body:
Adds a parameter sweep harness for the headstand routine and its first results. The top README gets a Robustness section with the map.

## What's in it

- **`tools/sweep/`** pins a physics parameter to a chosen value in each environment, runs one policy, the full routine, or one routine stage from recorded handover states, and writes one record per attempt. It covers 14 physics axes, backlash and 3 handover-state axes. `ray_sweep.py` spreads batches over a Ray cluster as one-CPU tasks. `check_axes.py` verifies every axis reaches the physics. `tools/test_sweep.py` covers the pure functions.
- **`results/sweeps/`** holds every sweep's map, records, handover states and provenance:
  - With nothing pinned, the harness reproduces the verified 87/96.
  - A baseline over 14 axes: 3,296 routine attempts.
  - A backlash sweep.
  - 24 handover-state sweeps.

## Findings

The routine is most sensitive to command delay (0/32 with no delay and at 50 ms or more), sideways trunk center of mass (28% at 15 mm to one side), IMU misalignment (41% at 9°) and high joint friction. Backlash up to 4° makes no difference. Details: zachgarner/microduck_rl#13, #14 and #15.

## Known gaps

- Replaying the split kick-up from its recorded states fails about 25% of the time unperturbed, so the split rows of the handover sweeps aren't trustworthy yet (#15).
- The commit message of 87c7258 says 7,488 attempts. The correct count is 7,616.

All sweeps ran on the Anyscale workspace on Warp's CPU backend, the backend the verified evaluators use.

items.title: Status can say "degraded", so a bench board stops reading as a broken one
items.body:
## The bug

`robotctl update status` prints `UNHEALTHY` for a robot with its servo supply off. That robot is fine, the release on it is fine, and the health gate had just committed that release onto it **on purpose**.

The collapse is one call. `Engine::status` built the field as `Some(health.is_healthy())`, and `is_healthy()` is `matches!(self, Health::Healthy)` — so four verdicts arrived as one `false`:

| verdict | gate | reported as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Degraded` — no servo power, no motor bus | **commits** | `UNHEALTHY` |
| `Unhealthy` — the real thing | reverts | `UNHEALTHY` |
| `Incompatible` — answered in a shape this `updaterd` cannot read | reverts | `UNHEALTHY` |
| `Unreachable` | reverts | `UNHEALTHY` |

`updater-design.md` §8 states the question as three-way in so many words — *"healthy commits, degraded commits, anything else reverts"* — and §4.1 asks of this route that "the app must be able to see `daemon unhealthy, version X, last update failed`". A boolean cannot carry that, and the app's own mirror of the type (`src/robot/api.ts` in `microduck-app`) inherits the same two states.

This is the same mistake `GatePassed` was split in two for, in the same file and in the opposite direction: that one reported a degraded commit as "the robot reported healthy" while the board's journal, at the same second, said degraded.

## The change

`ComponentStatus` gains `degraded` and `reason`, mirroring `HealthResult` — the vocabulary `robotd` already answers in and clients already model.

`Health::report()` does the mapping in one place. `degraded` is set for exactly the verdict the gate commits on and blames the board for; the three that revert carry their reason in words, because two booleans genuinely cannot tell "did not answer" from "answered unreadably" — and conflating *those two* is what `Health::Incompatible` exists to prevent.

`robotctl` renders it the way `robotctl health` has rendered the same distinction since it existed:

```
daemon: 0.14.1 (degraded: no robot on the motor bus after 4 attempts)
daemon: 0.14.1 (UNHEALTHY: policy unavailable: reading /opt/robot/policies/current/velstand.onnx)
```

`UNHEALTHY` stays shouted, because now it only prints when something is. The formatting moved into a pure function so the cases that matter — the ones a working robot never produces — are testable.

An exec probe gains its reason on the way past: it has no way to say degraded, but a failing one used to report a bare `UNHEALTHY` while holding the probe's own stderr.

## Compatibility

`API_VERSION` 31 → 32. Both fields `#[serde(default)]`, so an older `updaterd` reads exactly as it did — `degraded` false is the strict verdict it meant, absent `reason` is "it did not say". Nothing refuses on the difference, and there is a test for that shape.

## Verified

`cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. New tests: the five-verdict mapping in `updater/src/robot.rs`, `Engine::status` against the existing `DegradedRobot` double, four rendering cases in `robotctl`, and the older-`updaterd` JSON shape.

**Not** verified on a robot — no board here. The behaviour to confirm there is one line: `robotctl update status` on a bench board with the servo supply off should read `degraded:` and name the bus.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

`microduck-app`'s `ComponentStatus` mirror (`src/robot/api.ts:184`) still models `healthy: boolean | null` alone, so the app will keep showing a degraded robot as unhealthy until it reads the new fields.

Found while reviewing pollen-robotics/microduck_yocto#1, where this display is what made a release that rolled back for an unrelated reason look as though a missing policy set had caused it.

items.title: tofd: drive the beta's VL53L8CX over SPI; the board decides the bus
items.body:
## What

The beta board wires its ToF, a VL53L8CX (VL53L8CXV9GC/1), to SPI3, which both its images expose as `/dev/spidev3.0`. tofd only knew I²C, so it swept the face board's I²C bus and found nothing.

- **SPI in the platform layer.** `vendor/platform.c` gains SPI transfers behind the same six ULD hooks, in the framing of ST's own Linux platform layer (STSW-IMG042, `user/platform/platform.c`):
  - one full-duplex transfer per access, chip select low throughout;
  - the 16-bit index big-endian, with bit 15 clear for a read and set for a write;
  - data after the two index bytes;
  - chunks of 4094 bytes.

  The ULDs stay unedited.
- **SPI open and probe.** `vendor/probe.c` opens a spidev at ST's settings (mode 0, 8-bit words, 2 MHz) and reads the chip ID over SPI, so generation detection is unchanged. The `vl53l8cx` shim gains `vl8_open_spi`. The VL53L5CX has no SPI, and one answering there is refused.
- **`tof::link`: the board decides the bus.**
  - zero3 sweeps the HAT's I²C buses and addresses as before;
  - beta looks at `/dev/spidev3.0` only;
  - `--spi` forces a spidev, and `--bus` / `--address` force I²C, whatever the board.
- **One config read.** tofd reads `robotd.toml` once, before the sensor thread starts, for both the board and `[head_imu]`.

## Consequences

- No IPC change, no `API_VERSION` bump, no unit change.
- **The board has to give the spidev to the `robot` group**, which tofd's unit already has. On the Yocto image that is a udev rule in microduck_yocto, alongside the face-LED permissions. On Seeed's image it is one rule by hand.
- An empty SPI bus does not time out. SPI has no acknowledge, so "no sensor" shows up as an ID neither driver knows, which the error names.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p tof`, with four new tests for the bus choice.
- The C compiles for aarch64, and `cargo board -p tof --bin tofd` cross-builds and links.
- `cargo clippy -p tof --all-targets --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` is clean.
- Not yet run against the sensor.

items.title: audit: MicroDuck Manager-Based API 能力对照 microduck_rl
items.body:
## 审计目标

对照 `/home/tatp/ws/simulator/microduck_rl`，确认运行模式并逐项审计 UniLab 的 Manager-Based API 能力，重点覆盖 observation/action/command/reward/termination/event(domain randomization)/curriculum/metrics/recorder 及任务注册覆盖。

审计基线：

- 参考实现：`microduck_rl` 当前工作树，`src/mjlab_microduck/tasks`
- UniLab：`dev/issue-1042-manager-based-api`
- UniLab manager 来源/适配：pinned mjlab manager API 的 NumPy/SimBackend 适配

## 运行模式结论

`microduck_rl` 明确是 Manager-Based：

- 任务配置文件均使用 `ManagerBasedRlEnvCfg`
- 导出和 testbench 使用 `ManagerBasedRlEnv`
- `scripts/testbench_sim2real.py` 手动复现 `ManagerBasedRlEnv.step()` 的 decimation 生命周期
- 在 `src/`、`scripts/`、`tests/` 未发现 `DirectRLEnv`、`DirectRlEnv` 或 direct-mode 入口

UniLab 也使用 `ManagerBasedRlEnvCfg` + `ManagerBasedRlEnv`，并接入唯一 `NpEnv` lifecycle；不是通过 direct mode 绕过 manager contract。

## 任务注册覆盖

参考实现 `src/mjlab_microduck/tasks/__init__.py`：

- 18 个基础任务：Velocity flat/rough、VelStand、StandUp、SitStand、GroundPick、BallKick、Rollers、Swizzle、RollerCrouch、RollerSlope、RollerStandUp、Spin、Roulade
- 15 个 backlash 变体
- 合计 33 个 task IDs

UniLab `src/unilab/tasks/locomotion/microduck/__init__.py` 当前只注册：

- `MicroduckVelocityFlat`
- backend：`mujoco`、`mjwarp`

因此按 task-ID 计，尚有 32 个参考任务未迁移；rough velocity 也不在当前 UniLab 注册范围内。

## 能力矩阵

| 能力面 | 参考实现证据 | UniLab 当前证据 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ManagerBased env/config/lifecycle | `ManagerBasedRlEnv(Cfg)`；manager 顺序由 env lifecycle 驱动 | `src/unilab/envs/manager_based_rl_env.py`：统一 `NpEnv`、reset/step、partial reset、auto-reset、final observation | **Implemented (adapted)** |
| Manager core | Action/Observation/Reward/Termination/Event/Command/Curriculum/Metrics/Recorder 全套 managers | `src/unilab/managers/` 具备 9 类 manager、term cfg、SceneEntityCfg、Null managers、shape/finite diagnostics | **Implemented (adapted)** |
| Observation groups | actor/critic、noise、history、delay、privileged foot observations | `microduck_velocity_flat/base.yaml` 声明 policy/critic；IMU 0–1 step delay、joint velocity 1 step delay、noise、critic privileged terms；ObservationManager 支持 history/delay | **Implemented for velocity flat; Partial for full task set** |
| Actions | 当前参考 MicroDuck 配方主要使用 JointPositionAction，但 manager catalog 还提供多种 action term | UniLab 当前 MicroDuck 仅接入 JointPositionAction；通用 manager 没有参考侧的全部 effort/velocity/relative/tendon/site/differential action catalog | **Partial** |
| Commands | 参考 `mdp.py` 含 UniformVelocity、VelocityCommandCommandOnly、RelativeHeadingVelocity、GroundPickPhase、UniformPose、SitStand 等 | UniLab MicroDuck 只有 `MicroduckVelocityCommand(Cfg)`、`UniformVectorCommand(Cfg)`；没有 GroundPick/SitStand/relative-heading 等专用 command | **Partial** |
| Rewards | `src/mjlab_microduck/tasks/mdp.py` 约 7.2k 行，含 walking/recovery/roller/spin/ground-pick/ball-kick/roulade 等大量 task terms | UniLab 有通用 velocity/gait/sensor rewards，MicroDuck 私有 terms 主要是 head/leg pose、biped air-time、flight phase；velocity flat YAML 的 18 项 reward 已有 focused contract | **Partial** |
| Event / domain randomization | 参考侧含 reset/startup/interval/step，BAM per-world model fields、mass/inertia、gains、damping/friction、COM、base orientation、ball/reset state 等 | UniLab 有 GeomFriction、JointArmature、PdGains、mass/COM、gravity、push、encoder bias 等 NumPy/SimBackend terms；对直接 model-field mutation 明确 construction-time fail-closed，未实现 BAM `requires_model_fields` | **Partial; BAM path Unsupported** |
| Curriculum | 参考侧含 terrain levels、velocity/heading/push/wheel curricula、reward weight、command range、event parameter 等 | UniLab CurriculumManager + staged reward/termination/command/event curriculum；velocity flat 已配置 action-rate、head bias、standing、head range、base/head COM 六条 ladder | **Partial** |
| Termination/reset | 参考侧除 timeout/fall 外还有 terrain bounds/edge、illegal contact、task-specific recovery/impact 条件及多种 reset state | UniLab 当前 MicroDuck flat 有 timeout/tilt/base-height/NaN 和默认 scene reset；缺少其他任务族的 task-specific reset/termination | **Partial** |
| Metrics/Recorder | 参考 velocity base config 有 `mean_action_acc` metric，任务还有专用统计/调试路径 | UniLab MetricsManager/RecorderManager 已实现并测试，但 MicroDuck owner 当前没有完整参考 metrics/debug GUI wiring | **Partial** |
| Viewer/debug API | 参考 manager 暴露 command/reward/event debug-vis、GUI hooks | UniLab NumPy runtime 有意不引入 viewer/Warp/model mutation；这些差异需在兼容矩阵中保持显式 Unsupported，不能宣称 parity | **Intentional difference / Unsupported** |
| Actuator/backend | 参考含 BAM XL330 friction/backlash actuator 与 15 个 backlash tasks | UniLab 当前 XML position-PD + MuJoCo/MJWarp owner；BAM/backlash 未接入，且 deploy notes 已记录该 gap | **Unsupported** |

## 已验证的正向结论

以下不是空壳能力，已有代码和测试证据：

- Manager core、Hydra/Registry materialization、NumPy term pipeline、partial reset、NaN/Inf diagnostics
- velocity flat 的 61D actor / 76D critic observation contract
- command range/resampling、IMU/joint-velocity delay、noise、foot privileged observations
- velocity flat 的 reward、termination、reset event、foot friction、armature、COM、push
- staged reward/command/event curriculum
- focused test result：

```text
uv run pytest -q tests/managers \
  tests/envs/locomotion/microduck/test_velocity_contract.py \
  tests/envs/locomotion/microduck/test_microduck_rewards.py \
  tests/envs/locomotion/microduck/test_mjwarp_dr_smoke.py

72 passed, 3 deselected
```

另外，MuJoCo 实际 reset/step slow test：

```text
uv run pytest -q tests/envs/locomotion/microduck/test_velocity_contract.py -m slow
1 passed, 2 deselected
```

MJWarp 完整 CUDA smoke 因当前环境没有 active CUDA Warp device 被 deselect，不能据此宣称 GPU runtime 已完整验证。

## 关键审计判断

1. “UniLab 已有 Manager-Based framework”成立。
2. “UniLab 已完成 microduck_rl 全部 Manager-Based API / task parity”不成立。
3. #1402 的 velocity recipe 验收只证明当前 velocity owner 的纵向配方；不能外推为 33 个参考 task、BAM/backlash、全部 task-specific command/reward/event/curriculum 均已迁移。
4. 对缺失的 model-field/BAM/viewer 能力，应保持显式 Unsupported/fail-closed；不能通过 warning、skip、zero fallback 或旧 direct env 掩盖。

## 建议后续切片

- 为 32 个未迁移 task ID 建立按 family 的 child issues（recovery、ground-pick/ball、rollers、spin/roulade、backlash），每个 child 同时包含 config、term、registry、测试和文档。
- 先建立 source-to-UniLab parity fixture：自动列出每个 owner 的 command/reward/event/curriculum/termination/observation keys，避免只测单个 velocity owner。
- 对 `GroundPickPhaseCommand`、`SitStandCommand`、`RelativeHeadingVelocityCommand`、roller/spin/roulade rewards 和 task reset states 明确迁移或 Unsupported 决策。
- 对 BAM `requires_model_fields`/recompute 能力单独开公共 backend contract issue；本审计不把它伪装成已支持。
- 在实现 PR 的最终 head 上执行 `make test-all`，并维护 Compatible / Adapted / Unsupported 矩阵。

相关 issue：#1042、#1401、#1402、#1425。
