~150 LOC。

items.title: setup-login: install the robotctl completions where they are read on demand
items.body:
Follow-up to the review on [microduck_yocto#5](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_yocto/pull/5#pullrequestreview-5245507557), which is the half that cannot be fixed on the image side.

## What was wrong

`install_completions()` writes `/etc/bash_completion.d/robotctl` — the *compat* directory, sourced in full by every interactive bash. The file is a loader, not a snapshot: it asks `robotctl` for its own completions. So it costs a `robotctl` process at every login whether or not anybody means to type the word — 0.14 s against 0.05 s for the login shell, measured on duck-882e.

microduck_yocto#5 installs the identical loader at `/usr/share/bash-completion/completions/robotctl`, where bash-completion reads it the first time somebody types `robotctl<TAB>` and never otherwise. But as long as this script keeps writing the compat copy, the compat copy registers first and the image's file never fires: the image change buys nothing, on any board that has ever taken a daemon update.

## What this does

- `install_completions()` writes `/usr/share/bash-completion/completions/robotctl`. Same content, same indirection.
- **Removes the eager copy**, when it carries this script's own marker line (`# Generated by the robot daemon installer`). Leaving it would shadow the new file, so the update would change nothing it claims to change. A `robotctl` completion in the compat directory that this script did not write is left alone.
- **Guards on the dispatcher** (`/usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion`) rather than on a directory. `completions/` belongs to a separate package on both userlands we run on — oe-core's `bash-completion-extra`, Debian's `bash-completion` — so its absence says nothing about whether anything would read the file. The dispatcher is what defines the dynamic lookup; `mkdir -p` handles the directory.
- `install.sh`'s "Tab-completion is installed" claim, the `robotctl completions` help example and `docs/robot/cheatsheet.md` follow the path.

## Tested

- `cargo test -p robotctl` — 171 passed (the only Rust change is a doc comment).
- `sh -n` on `setup-login.sh`, `install.sh`, `board-test.sh`.
- `install_completions` driven against a fake root for its three paths: no dispatcher → writes nothing; dispatcher plus an old eager copy → writes the new file and removes the old one; a foreign `robotctl` in the compat directory → left in place.
- `board-test.sh` now stubs the dispatcher, seeds an eager copy from an older release, and asserts both halves — but **it was not run**: it needs Docker.

items.title: Replace nine copies of the sim2real obs wiring with one function
items.body:
Nine cfg modules each carried the same ~45 lines of observation wiring: IMU obs
delay, obs noise, IMU-misalignment DR, the 1-step `joint_vel` firmware lag,
passive-joint exclusion and encoder-bias DR. This replaces every copy with a call
to `microduck_mdp.wire_sim2real_obs()`.

Nine copies is nine places to forget one line, which is how two policies of the
hot-swappable 61D family end up subtly non-interchangeable on the robot.

The blocks were not quite identical, so the parts that genuinely varied became
parameters rather than being flattened away:

- `imu_delay_max_lag` — `ground_pick` trained at 3, every other env at 1
- `sanitize_critic_sensors` — only `velocity` and `standup` carried that block
- `misalign_gravity` — off for velocity's raw-accelerometer path

## Verification

Behaviour preservation was proven, not assumed: a structural dump of **all 10 env
cfgs x both play modes** is **byte-identical** before and after.

That dump also caught the one thing worth knowing about (below); without it the
change would have shipped a silent retune.

- `make lint` — passes
- `make tests` — 217 passed, 1 skipped
- Smoke tests (64 envs, 5 iters, NaN-free): `Velocity-Flat` and `GroundPick-Flat`
  (the `sanitize_critic_sensors=False` path)

## One pre-existing bug preserved on purpose

The actor's `joint_vel` noise is set *before* the shared term is deepcopied, so
`0.25` also lands on the **critic**, whose base-template value is `1.5`.

Every policy in the family has trained against that leak. Hoisting the deepcopy
(the obvious tidy-up) silently retunes every critic at once, so the original
ordering is kept verbatim. Fixing it is a deliberate retrain decision and belongs
in its own PR.

## Scope

Obs-wiring dedup only. An earlier revision of this branch also swapped hand-rolled
quaternion math for the mjlab/mujoco builtins; that is unrelated and dropped here
(see #55).

items.title: Declare the board in robotd.toml, and retire one with a single constant
items.body:
## What

- **`[board] version`** in `robotd.toml`: `"zero3"` or `"beta"`, unset is `zero3`. Editable in `robotctl configure`; owned by `robotd-params/src/board.rs`.
- **Provisioning writes it:** `provision-board.sh --board beta` → `DUCK_BOARD` → `install.sh`, which sets the key whatever shape the file is in (new template, a release's template that predates `[board]`, or a kept file). The bring-up (`setup-board.sh`) is still the Zero 3W's on either board, and `--board beta` says so.
- **`robotctl health`** prints the board, marked `(not declared)` when the key is unset. It warns when `/proc/device-tree/compatible` names the other board, and when the board has a last release.
- **Undeclared robots get asked.** When the key is unset and the device tree names a board, `robotctl health` (after its report) and `robotctl update apply` (before the call) offer to write it. They only ask at a terminal, and only if the user can write the file. `edit::set_board` writes the key even when it is the default.
- **The updater's `hw_rev` is the declared board** (zero3 1, beta 2), read from `robotd.toml` before every check. `hw_rev` in `updater.toml` applies only when no board is declared, so every existing robot (`hw_rev = 1`, no board) answers as before. `deploy/updater.toml` no longer ships it.
- **Retiring a board is one constant:** `Board::last_release`. From the release that sets it, health on that board warns; `xtask package` derives the manifest's `min_hw_rev` from the table, so the first release after it is refused by the updater the board already runs. `docs/design/updater-design.md` §5.6 has the procedure.

## Not in this PR

Nothing a beta does differently: no audio, camera, ToF or LED changes, and nothing from microduck_yocto#16. The Yocto image does not write the key yet.

## Consequences

- No IPC change, no `API_VERSION` bump.
- Manifests now carry `min_hw_rev: 1` instead of `0`. Every robot is revision 1, so nothing is refused.
- `xtask package --min-hw-rev` is gone. Nothing passed it.

## Tests

`cargo test -p robotd-params -p updater -p robotctl -p xtask`, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` is clean. `declare_board` was exercised against the four `robotd.toml` shapes. It has not run on a board.

items.title: `update_all`, so a full sample is one call and one pair of reads
items.body:
`Bmi088Ahrs::update` reads the accelerometer to feed Madgwick, then returns only the gyro and the quaternion. A consumer that also publishes acceleration — `microduck`'s `tofd`, serving `head_imu.stream` — has to call `read_accelerometer_ms2` afterwards, which reads the same six registers again. Three I²C transactions a sample where two carry all the data.

## What it is worth, measured

I opened this expecting a third of the thread's CPU back, because `tofd`'s `head-imu` thread costs 4.5% of a core at 100 Hz and 90% of that is system time. The board says otherwise — `bench_imu`, 10 s a mode at 100 Hz on a Radxa Zero 3:

```text
  update      (2 reads)   cpu  4.44 %   rate  99.90 Hz   mean 10.010 ms
  update_all  (2 reads)   cpu  4.46 %   rate  99.90 Hz   mean 10.010 ms
  three-reads (3 reads)   cpu  4.53 %   rate  99.90 Hz   mean 10.010 ms
```

A whole I²C transaction is ~0.09 points — about 9 µs against the ~440 µs a sample costs. So transaction count is not what this loop pays for, and neither is the filter; that is being chased separately with two modes that read nothing (`sleep only`, `filter only`), also in this PR.

So this is not a performance change. It is worth landing for three smaller reasons:

- The accelerometer a consumer publishes becomes the sample the quaternion was computed from, instead of one read ~200 µs later.
- A read can fail in one place instead of two.
- ~200 µs a sample of bus stops being spent on a bus that, on this robot, a ToF sensor and an audio codec share.

## The change

`update_all` returns `(accel, gyro, quaternion)` from the two reads it already performs, accel in m/s² — exactly what `read_accelerometer_ms2` returned. `update` keeps its signature and delegates, so no existing caller changes.

`examples/bench_imu.rs` grew the five modes above; run it with the bus to itself:

```bash
sudo systemctl stop tofd
```

```bash
./bench_imu --bus /dev/i2c-pihat --freq 100
```

Cross-builds for the board with `cargo zigbuild --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.31 --examples`.

items.title: [task] eval: body IMU power rail ~6V via DXL 3P to HAT
items.body:
## Type
`task`（设计评估 · 未授权改板/改拓扑前勿装机定稿）

## Goal
评估一条**备选供电路径**：机身侧取电 → **降到约 6 V**（是否还需稳压）→ 经 **DXL 3P（针 2 = VBATT）** 给头舱 **HAT** 供电；并厘清与机身 IMU（ID 200）接口/铜箔/保护的关系。

对照现行 wiki 定稿（**不要默认替换**）：
- `board-interconnect`：`NP-F550（机身）──电源线──► HAT（头舱）`，再经 J13/J14 把 **VBATT+DATA** 分给舵机/IMU
- HAT：`AP63205` 输入标称 **5–28 V** → 板载 5 V 给 Zero
- DXL 3P：`1=GND · 2=VBATT · 3=DATA`（HAT J13/J14 与 imu-to-dxl EH 同序）

## Questions to answer（交付）

1. **拓扑是否可行**  
   - 「从机身经 DXL 3P **回灌** HAT `+BATT`」与官方「电池先进 HAT 再出 DXL」的差异、风险（双供电、回流、地回路、颈线载流）  
   - 机身 IMU 板是否适合作为 **电源注入点**（双 EH 中继 / 单座叶子）；铜箔与 PPTC/TVS 是否按「穿堂大电流」设计  

2. **6 V 目标**  
   - XL330 / 母线：6 V 是否在推荐工作区；相对 7.4–8.4 V（2S）的扭矩/压降余量  
   - HAT buck：6 V → 5 V 是否在 AP63205 舒适区（含压差、纹波、Zero+外设电流）  
   - **是否需要稳压**：仅 buck 开环 vs buck+后级 LDO/理想二极管；台架 vs 电池两种场景  

3. **接口与保护**  
   - 机身「电源接口」形态（XT30 / 电池扣 / 台供）与 IMU 3P 的汇合方式  
   - 反接、浪涌、舵机堵转回流对 IMU LDO（3V3）与 HAT 的影响  
   - 与 Type-C 给 Zero 同时供电时的冲突规则（沿用「勿双灌」）  

4. **与在途工作的关系**  
   - 不阻塞 #4 / #7 / #8 的通信排障；本单结论写入 wiki 后再谈改 BOM/改线  

## Deliverables
- [ ] 一页评估写入 wiki（建议新页 `concepts/body-imu-hat-dxl-power-eval.md` 或并入 `board-interconnect` 专节）  
- [ ] 推荐：**采用 / 仅台架实验 / 不采用** + 不可破约束列表  
- [ ] 若采用：草图（电池→6V→哪只 3P→HAT→Zero）与电流预算粗表  
- [ ] Issue 评论摘要；`pm` 裁决是否改互联定稿  

## Constraints
- 规格冲突以 wiki 现行互联为准，直到 pm 改裁决  
- 禁止在未评估前把整机电池只挂在 IMU 链上长期跑舵机堵转工况  
- XL330 与 HAT 电压以手册/现页为准，引用出处  

## Related
- wiki：`board-interconnect` · `bench-power-supply` · `board-hat` · `board-imu-to-dxl` · `np-f550-battery`  
- Issues：#4 HAT TTL · #7/#8 机身 IMU 总线冒烟（通信，非本单电源定稿）  

## assignee-agent
`hardware`（主评估）· `pm` 收口 wiki 裁决；必要时 `structure` 只评线束/腔体走线

## Out of scope
立即改 Gerber；训练/固件；示波器通信排障（仍归 #4/#7）
